4.24.d: का सुष्टुतिः शवसः सूनुमिन्द्रमर्वाचीनं राधस आ ववर्तत् । ददिर्हि वीरो गृणते वसूनि स गोपतिर्निष्षिधां नो जनासः ॥
4.24.e: WHAT worthy praise will bring before us Indra, the Son of Strength, that he may grant us riches;  For he the Hero, gives the singer treasures: he is the Lord who sends us gifts, ye people.

4.24.d: स वृत्रहत्ये हव्यः स ईड्यः स सुष्टुत इन्द्रः सत्यराधाः । स यामन्ना मघवा मर्त्याय ब्रह्मण्यते सुष्वये वरिवो धात् ॥
4.24.e: To be invoked and hymned in fight with Vṛtra, that well-praised Indra gives us real bounties.  That Maghavan brings comfort in the foray to the religious man who pours libations.

4.24.d: तमिन्नरो वि ह्वयन्ते समीके रिरिक्वांसस्तन्वः कृण्वत त्राम् । मिथो यत्त्यागमुभयासो अग्मन्नरस्तोकस्य तनयस्य सातौ ॥
4.24.e: Him, verily, the men invoke in combat; risking their lives they make him their protector,  When heroes, foe to foe, give up their bodies, fighting, each side, for children and their offspring.

4.24.d: क्रतूयन्ति क्षितयो योग उग्राशुषाणासो मिथो अर्णसातौ । सं यद्विशोऽववृत्रन्त युध्मा आदिन्नेम इन्द्रयन्ते अभीके ॥
4.24.e: Strong God! the folk at need put forth their vigour, striving together in the whirl of battle.  When warrior bands encounter one another some in the grapple quit themselves like Indra.

4.24.d: आदिद्ध नेम इन्द्रियं यजन्त आदित्पक्तिः पुरोळाशं रिरिच्यात् । आदित्सोमो वि पपृच्यादसुष्वीनादिज्जुजोष वृषभं यजध्यै ॥
4.24.e: Hence many a one worships the might of Indra: hence let the brew succeed the meal-oblation.  Hence let the Soma banish those who pour not: even hence I joy to pay the Strong One worship.

4.24.d: कृणोत्यस्मै वरिवो य इत्थेन्द्राय सोममुशते सुनोति । सध्रीचीनेन मनसाविवेनन्तमित्सखायं कृणुते समत्सु ॥
4.24.e: Indra gives comfort to the man who truly presses, for him who longs  for  it, the Soma,  Not disaffected, with devoted spirit this man he takes to be his friend in battles.

4.24.d: य इन्द्राय सुनवत्सोममद्य पचात्पक्तीरुत भृज्जाति धानाः । प्रति मनायोरुचथानि हर्यन्तस्मिन्दधद्वृषणं शुष्ममिन्द्रः ॥
4.24.e: He who this day for Indra presses Soma, prepares the brew and fries the grains of barley—  Loving the hymns of that devoted servant, to him may Indra give heroic vigour.

4.24.d: यदा समर्यं व्यचेदृघावा दीर्घं यदाजिमभ्यख्यदर्यः । अचिक्रदद्वृषणं पत्न्यच्छा दुरोण आ निशितं सोमसुद्भिः ॥
4.24.e: When the impetuous chief hath sought the  conflict  , and the lord looked upon the long-drawn battle,  The matron calls to the Strong God whom pressers of Soma have encouraged in the dwelling.

4.24.d: भूयसा वस्नमचरत्कनीयोऽविक्रीतो अकानिषं पुनर्यन् । स भूयसा कनीयो नारिरेचीद्दीना दक्षा वि दुहन्ति प्र वाणम् ॥
4.24.e: He bid a small price for a thing of value: I was content, returning, still unpurchased.  He heightened not his insufficient offer. Simple and clever, both milk out the udder.

4.24.d: क इमं दशभिर्ममेन्द्रं क्रीणाति धेनुभिः । यदा वृत्राणि जङ्घनदथैनं मे पुनर्ददत् ॥
4.24.e: Who for ten milch-kine purchaseth from me this Indra who is mine?  When he hath slain the Vṛtras let the buyer give him back to me.

4.24.d: नू ष्टुत इन्द्र नू गृणान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो३ न पीपेः । अकारि ते हरिवो ब्रह्म नव्यं धिया स्याम रथ्यः सदासाः ॥
4.24.e: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let wealth swell high like rivers for the singer.  For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays, is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

4.25.d: को अद्य नर्यो देवकाम उशन्निन्द्रस्य सख्यं जुजोष । को वा महेऽवसे पार्याय समिद्धे अग्नौ सुतसोम ईट्टे ॥
4.25.e: WHAT friend of man, God-loving, hath delighted, yearning therefor, this day in Indra's friendship?  Who with enkindled flame and flowing Soma laudeth him for his great protecting favour?

4.25.d: को नानाम वचसा सोम्याय मनायुर्वा भवति वस्त उस्राः । क इन्द्रस्य युज्यं कः सखित्वं को भ्रात्रं वष्टि कवये क ऊती ॥
4.25.e: Who hath with prayer bowed to the Soma-lover? What pious man endues the beams of morning?  Who seeks bond, friendship, brotherhood with Indra? Who hath recourse unto the Sage for succour?

4.25.d: को देवानामवो अद्या वृणीते क आदित्याँ अदितिं ज्योतिरीट्टे । कस्याश्विनाविन्द्रो अग्निः सुतस्यांशोः पिबन्ति मनसाविवेनम् ॥
4.25.e: Who claims to-day the Deities' protection, asks Aditi for light, or the Ādityas?  Of whose pressed stalk of Soma drink the Aśvins, Indra, and Agni, well-inclined in spirit?

4.25.d: तस्मा अग्निर्भारतः शर्म यंसज्ज्योक्पश्यात्सूर्यमुच्चरन्तम् । य इन्द्राय सुनवामेत्याह नरे नर्याय नृतमाय नृणाम् ॥
4.25.e: To him shall Agni Bhārata give shelter: long shall he look upon the Sun up-rising,  Who sayeth, Let us press the juice for Indra, man's Friend, the Hero manliest of heroes.

4.25.d: न तं जिनन्ति बहवो न दभ्रा उर्वस्मा अदितिः शर्म यंसत् । प्रियः सुकृत्प्रिय इन्द्रे मनायुः प्रियः सुप्रावीः प्रियो अस्य सोमी ॥
4.25.e: Him neither few men overcome, nor many to him shall Aditi give spacious shelter.  Dear is the pious, the devout, to Indra dear is the zealous, dear the Soma-bringer.

4.25.d: सुप्राव्यः प्राशुषाळेष वीरः सुष्वेः पक्तिं कृणुते केवलेन्द्रः । नासुष्वेरापिर्न सखा न जामिर्दुष्प्राव्योऽवहन्तेदवाचः ॥
4.25.e: This Hero curbs the mighty for the zealous: the presser's brew Indra possesses solely:  No brother, kin, or friend to him who pours not, destroyer of the dumb who would resist him.

4.25.d: न रेवता पणिना सख्यमिन्द्रोऽसुन्वता सुतपाः सं गृणीते । आस्य वेदः खिदति हन्ति नग्नं वि सुष्वये पक्तये केवलो भूत् ॥
4.25.e: Not with the wealthy churl who pours no Soma doth Indra, Soma-drinker, bind alliance.  He draws away his wealth and slays him naked, own Friend to him who offers, for oblation.

4.25.d: इन्द्रं परेऽवरे मध्यमास इन्द्रं यान्तोऽवसितास इन्द्रम् । इन्द्रं क्षियन्त उत युध्यमाना इन्द्रं नरो वाजयन्तो हवन्ते ॥
4.25.e: Highest and lowest, men who stand between diem, going, returning, dwelling in contentment,  Those who show forth their strength when urged to battle-these are the men who call for aid on Indra.

4.26.d: अहं मनुरभवं सूर्यश्चाहं कक्षीवाँ ऋषिरस्मि विप्रः । अहं कुत्समार्जुनेयं न्यृञ्जेऽहं कविरुशना पश्यता मा ॥
4.26.e: I WAS aforetime Manu, I was Sūrya: I am the sage Kakṣīvān, holy singer.  Kutsa the son of Ārjuni I master. I am the sapient Uśanā behold me.

4.26.d: अहं भूमिमददामार्यायाहं वृष्टिं दाशुषे मर्त्याय । अहमपो अनयं वावशाना मम देवासो अनु केतमायन् ॥
4.26.e: I have bestowed the earth upon the Ārya, and rain upon the man who brings oblation.  I guided forth the loudly-roaring waters, and the Gods moved according to my pleasure.

4.26.d: अहं पुरो मन्दसानो व्यैरं नव साकं नवतीः शम्बरस्य । शततमं वेश्यं सर्वताता दिवोदासमतिथिग्वं यदावम् ॥
4.26.e: In the wild joy of Soma I demolished Śambara's forts, ninety-and-nine, together;  And, utterly, the hundredth habitation, when helping Divodāsa Atithigva.

4.26.d: प्र सु ष विभ्यो मरुतो विरस्तु प्र श्येनः श्येनेभ्य आशुपत्वा । अचक्रया यत्स्वधया सुपर्णो हव्यं भरन्मनवे देवजुष्टम् ॥
4.26.e: Before all birds be ranked this Bird, O Maruts; supreme of falcons be this fleet-winged Falcon,  Because, strong- pinioned, with no car to bear him, he brought to Manu the Godloved oblation.

4.26.d: भरद्यदि विरतो वेविजानः पथोरुणा मनोजवा असर्जि । तूयं ययौ मधुना सोम्येनोत श्रवो विविदे श्येनो अत्र ॥
4.26.e: When the Bird brought it, hence in rapid motion sent on the wide path fleet as thought he hurried.  Swift he returned with sweetness of the Soma, and hence the Falcon hath acquired his glory.

4.26.d: ऋजीपी श्येनो ददमानो अंशुं परावतः शकुनो मन्द्रं मदम् । सोमं भरद्दादृहाणो देवावान्दिवो अमुष्मादुत्तरादादाय ॥
4.26.e: Bearing the stalk, the Falcon speeding onward, Bird bringing from afar the draught that gladdens,  Friend of the Gods, brought, grasping fast, the Soma which be bad taken from yon loftiest heaven.

4.26.d: आदाय श्येनो अभरत्सोमं सहस्रं सवाँ अयुतं च साकम् । अत्रा पुरंधिरजहादरातीर्मदे सोमस्य मूरा अमूरः ॥
4.26.e: The Falcon took and brought the Soma, bearing thousand libations with him, yea, ten thousand.  The Bold One left Malignities behind him, wise, in wild joy of Soma, left the foolish.

4.27.d: गर्भे नु सन्नन्वेषामवेदमहं देवानां जनिमानि विश्वा । शतं मा पुर आयसीररक्षन्नध श्येनो जवसा निरदीयम् ॥
4.27.e: I, As I lay within the womb, considered all generations of these Gods in order.  A hundred iron fortresses confined me but forth I flew with rapid speed a Falcon.

4.27.d: न घा स मामप जोषं जभाराभीमास त्वक्षसा वीर्येण । ईर्मा पुरंधिरजहादरातीरुत वाताँ अतरच्छूशुवानः ॥
4.27.e: Not at his own free pleasure did he bear me: he conquered with his strength and manly courage.  Straightway the Bold One left the fiends behind him and passed the winds as he grew yet more mighty.

4.27.d: अव यच्छ्येनो अस्वनीदध द्योर्वि यद्यदि वात ऊहुः पुरंधिम् । सृजद्यदस्मा अव ह क्षिपज्ज्यां कृशानुरस्ता मनसा भुरण्यन् ॥
4.27.e: When with loud cry from heaven down sped the Falcon, thence hasting like the wind he bore the Bold One.  Then, wildly raging in his mind, the archer Kṛśānu aimed and loosed the string to strike him.

4.27.d: ऋजिप्य ईमिन्द्रावतो न भुज्युं श्येनो जभार बृहतो अधि ष्णोः । अन्तः पतत्पतत्र्यस्य पर्णमध यामनि प्रसितस्य तद्वेः ॥
4.27.e: The Falcon bore him from heaven's lofty summit as the swift car of Indra's Friend bore Bhujyu.  Then downward hither fell a flying feather of the Bird hasting forward in his journey.

4.27.d: अध श्वेतं कलशं गोभिरक्तमापिप्यानं मघवा शुक्रमन्धः । अध्वर्युभिः प्रयतं मध्वो अग्रमिन्द्रो मदाय प्रति धत्पिबध्यै शूरो मदाय प्रति धत्पिबध्यै ॥
4.27.e: And now let Maghavan accept the beaker, white, filled with milk, filled with the shining liquid;  The best of sweet meath which the priests have offered: that Indra to his joy may drink, the Hero, that he may take and drink it to his rapture.

4.28.d: त्वा युजा तव तत्सोम सख्य इन्द्रो अपो मनवे सस्रुतस्कः । अहन्नहिमरिणात्सप्त सिन्धूनपावृणोदपिहितेव खानि ॥
4.28.e: ALLIED with thee, in this thy friendship, Soma, Indra for man made waters flow together,  Slew Ahi, and sent forth the Seven Rivers, and opened as it were obstructed fountains.

4.28.d: त्वा युजा नि खिदत्सूर्यस्येन्द्रश्चक्रं सहसा सद्य इन्दो । अधि ष्णुना बृहता वर्तमानं महो द्रुहो अप विश्वायु धायि ॥
4.28.e: Indu, with thee for his confederate, Indra swiftly with might pressed down the wheel of Sūrya.  What rolled, all life's support, on heaven's high summit was separated from the great oppressor.

4.28.d: अहन्निन्द्रो अदहदग्निरिन्दो पुरा दस्यून्मध्यंदिनादभीके । दुर्गे दुरोणे क्रत्वा न यातां पुरू सहस्रा शर्वा नि बर्हीत् ॥
4.28.e: Indra smote down, Agni consumed, O Indu, the Dasyus ere the noontide in the conflict.  Of those who gladly sought a hard-won dwelling he cast down many a thousand with his arrow.

4.28.d: विश्वस्मात्सीमधमाँ इन्द्र दस्यून्विशो दासीरकृणोरप्रशस्ताः । अबाधेथाममृणतं नि शत्रूनविन्देथामपचितिं वधत्रैः ॥
4.28.e: Lower than all besides hast thou, O Indra, cast down the Dasyus, abject tribes of Dāsas.  Ye drave away, ye put to death the foemen, and took great vengeance with your murdering weapons.

4.28.d: एवा सत्यं मघवाना युवं तदिन्द्रश्च सोमोर्वमश्व्यं गोः । आदर्दृतमपिहितान्यश्ना रिरिचथुः क्षाश्चित्ततृदाना ॥
4.28.e: So, of a truth, Indra and Soma, Heroes, ye burst the stable of the kine and horses,  The stable which the bar or stone obstructed; and piercing through set free the habitations.

4.29.d: आ नः स्तुत उप वाजेभिरूती इन्द्र याहि हरिभिर्मन्दसानः । तिरश्चिदर्यः सवना पुरूण्याङ्गूषेभिर्गृणानः सत्यराधाः ॥
4.29.e: COME, lauded, unto us with powers and succours, O Indra, with thy Tawny Steeds; exulting,  Past even the foeman's manifold libations, glorified with our hymns, true Wealth-bestower.

4.29.d: आ हि ष्मा याति नर्यश्चिकित्वान्हूयमानः सोतृभिरुप यज्ञम् । स्वश्वो यो अभीरुर्मन्यमानः सुष्वाणेभिर्मदति सं ह वीरैः ॥
4.29.e: Man's Friend, to this our sacrifice he cometh marking how he is called by Soma-pressers.  Fearless, and conscious that his Steeds are noble, he joyeth with the Soma-pouring heroes.

4.29.d: श्रावयेदस्य कर्णा वाजयध्यै जुष्टामनु प्र दिशं मन्दयध्यै । उद्वावृषाणो राधसे तुविष्मान्करन्न इन्द्रः सुतीर्थाभयं च ॥
4.29.e: Make his cars hear, that he may show his vigour and may be joyful in the way he loveth.  May mighty Indra pouring forth in bounty bestow on us good roads and perfect safety;

4.29.d: अच्छा यो गन्ता नाधमानमूती इत्था विप्रं हवमानं गृणन्तम् । उप त्मनि दधानो धुर्या३शून्त्सहस्राणि शतानि वज्रबाहुः ॥
4.29.e: He who with succour comes to his implorer, the singer here who with his song invites him;  He who himself sets to the pole swift Coursers, he who hath hundreds, thousands, Thunder-wielder.

4.29.d: त्वोतासो मघवन्निन्द्र विप्रा वयं ते स्याम सूरयो गृणन्तः । भेजानासो बृहद्दिवस्य राय आकाय्यस्य दावने पुरुक्षोः ॥
4.29.e: O Indra Maghavan, by thee protected may we be thine, princes and priests and singers,  Sharing the riches sent from lofty heaven which yields much food, and all desire its bounty.

4.30.d: नकिरिन्द्र त्वदुत्तरो न ज्यायाँ अस्ति वृत्रहन् । नकिरेवा यथा त्वम् ॥
4.30.e: O INDRA, Vṛtra-slayer, none is better, mightier than thou:  Verily there is none like thee.

4.30.d: सत्रा ते अनु कृष्टयो विश्वा चक्रेव वावृतुः । सत्रा महाँ असि श्रुतः ॥
4.30.e: Like chariot-wheels these people all together follow after thee:  Thou ever art renowned as Great.

4.30.d: विश्वे चनेदना त्वा देवास इन्द्र युयुधुः । यदहा नक्तमातिरः ॥
4.30.e: Not even all the gathered Gods conquered thee, Indra, in the war,  When thou didst lengthen days by night.

4.30.d: यत्रोत बाधितेभ्यश्चक्रं कुत्साय युध्यते । मुषाय इन्द्र सूर्यम् ॥
4.30.e: When for the sake of those oppressed, and Kutsa as he battled,  Thou stolest away the Sun's car-wheel.

4.30.d: यत्र देवाँ ऋघायतो विश्वाँ अयुध्य एक इत् । त्वमिन्द्र वनूँरहन् ॥
4.30.e: When, fighting singly, Indra. thou o’ercamest all the furious Gods, thou slewest those who strove with thee.

4.30.d: यत्रोत मर्त्याय कमरिणा इन्द्र सूर्यम् । प्रावः शचीभिरेतशम् ॥
4.30.e: When also for a mortal man, Indra, thou speddest forth the Sun,  And holpest Etaśa with might.

4.30.d: किमादुतासि वृत्रहन्मघवन्मन्युमत्तमः । अत्राह दानुमातिरः ॥
4.30.e: What? Vṛtra-slayer, art not thou, Maghavan, fiercest in thy wrath?  So hast thou quelled the demon too.

4.30.d: एतद्घेदुत वीर्य१मिन्द्र चकर्थ पौंस्यम् । स्त्रियं यद्दुर्हणायुवं वधीर्दुहितरं दिवः ॥
4.30.e: And this heroic deed of might thou, Indra, also hast achieved,  That thou didst smite to death the Dame, Heaven's Daughter, meditating ill.

4.30.d: दिवश्चिद्घा दुहितरं महान्महीयमानाम् । उषासमिन्द्र सं पिणक् ॥
4.30.e: Thou, Indra, Mighty One, didst crush Uṣas, though Daughter of the Sky.  When lifting up herself in pride.

4.30.d: अपोषा अनसः सरत्सम्पिष्टादह बिभ्युषी । नि यत्सीं शिश्नथद्वृषा ॥
4.30.e: Then from her chariot Uṣas fled, affrighted, from her ruined car.  When the strong God had shattered it.

4.30.d: एतदस्या अनः शये सुसम्पिष्टं विपाश्या । ससार सीं परावतः ॥
4.30.e: So there this car of Uṣas lay, broken to pieces, in Vipāś,  And she herself fled far away.

4.30.d: उत सिन्धुं विबाल्यं वितस्थानामधि क्षमि । परि ष्ठा इन्द्र मायया ॥
4.30.e: Thou, Indra, didst. with magic power resist the overflowing stream  Who spread her waters o’er the land.

4.30.d: उत शुष्णस्य धृष्णुया प्र मृक्षो अभि वेदनम् । पुरो यदस्य सम्पिणक् ॥
4.30.e: Valiantly didst thou seize and take the store which Śuṣṇa had amassed,  When thou didst crush his fortresses.

4.30.d: उत दासं कौलितरं बृहतः पर्वतादधि । अवाहन्निन्द्र शम्बरम् ॥
4.30.e: Thou, Indra, also smotest down Kulitara's son Śambara,  The Dāsa, from the lofty hill.

4.30.d: उत दासस्य वर्चिनः सहस्राणि शतावधीः । अधि पञ्च प्रधीँरिव ॥
4.30.e: Of Dāsa Varcin's thou didst slay the hundred thousand and the five,  Crushed like the fellies, of a car.

4.30.d: उत त्यं पुत्रमग्रुवः परावृक्तं शतक्रतुः । उक्थेष्विन्द्र आभजत् ॥
4.30.e: So Indra, Lord of Heroes, Powers, caused the unwedded damsel's son,  The castaway, to share the lauds.

4.30.d: उत त्या तुर्वशायदू अस्नातारा शचीपतिः । इन्द्रो विद्वाँ अपारयत् ॥
4.30.e: So sapient Indra, Lord of Might, brought Turvaśa and Yadu, those  Who feared the flood, in safety o’er.

4.30.d: उत त्या सद्य आर्या सरयोरिन्द्र पारतः । अर्णाचित्ररथावधीः ॥
4.30.e: Arṇa and Citraratha, both Āryas, thou, Indra, slewest swift,  On yonder side of Sarayu,

4.30.d: अनु द्वा जहिता नयोऽन्धं श्रोणं च वृत्रहन् । न तत्ते सुम्नमष्टवे ॥
4.30.e: Thou, Vṛtra-slayer, didst conduct those two forlorn, the blind, the lame.  None may attain this bliss of thine.

4.30.d: शतमश्मन्मयीनां पुरामिन्द्रो व्यास्यत् । दिवोदासाय दाशुषे ॥
4.30.e: For Divodāsa, him who brought oblations, Indra overthrew  A hundred fortresses of stone.

4.30.d: अस्वापयद्दभीतये सहस्रा त्रिंशतं हथैः । दासानामिन्द्रो मायया ॥
4.30.e: The thirty thousand Dāsas he with magic power and weapons sent  To slumber, for Dabhīti's sake.

4.30.d: स घेदुतासि वृत्रहन्त्समान इन्द्र गोपतिः । यस्ता विश्वानि चिच्युषे ॥
4.30.e: As such, O Vṛtra-slayer, thou art general Lord of kine for all,  Thou Shaker of all things that be.

4.30.d: उत नूनं यदिन्द्रियं करिष्या इन्द्र पौंस्यम् । अद्या नकिष्टदा मिनत् ॥
4.30.e: Indra, whatever deed of might thou hast this day to execute,  None be there now to hinder it.

4.30.d: वामंवामं त आदुरे देवो ददात्वर्यमा । वामं पूषा वामं भगो वामं देवः करूळती ॥
4.30.e: O Watchful One, may Aryaman the God give thee all goodly things.  May Pūṣan, Bhaga, and the God Karūḷatī give all things fair.

4.31.d: कया नश्चित्र आ भुवदूती सदावृधः सखा । कया शचिष्ठया वृता ॥
4.31.e: WITH what help will he come to us, wonderful, ever-waxing Friend;  With what most mighty company?

4.31.d: कस्त्वा सत्यो मदानां मंहिष्ठो मत्सदन्धसः । दृळ्हा चिदारुजे वसु ॥
4.31.e: What genuine and most liberal draught will spirit thee with juice to burst  Open e’en strongly-guarded wealth?

4.31.d: अभी षु णः सखीनामविता जरितॄणाम् । शतं भवास्यूतिभिः ॥
4.31.e: Do thou who art Protector of us thy friends who praise thee  With hundred aids approach us.

4.31.d: अभी न आ ववृत्स्व चक्रं न वृत्तमर्वतः । नियुद्भिश्चर्षणीनाम् ॥
4.31.e: Like as a courser's circling wheel, so turn thee hitherward to us,  Attracted by the hymns of men.

4.31.d: प्रवता हि क्रतूनामा हा पदेव गच्छसि । अभक्षि सूर्ये सचा ॥
4.31.e: Thou seekest as it were thine own stations with swift descent of powers:  I share thee even with the Sun.

4.31.d: सं यत्त इन्द्र मन्यवः सं चक्राणि दधन्विरे । अध त्वे अध सूर्ये ॥
4.31.e: What time thy courage and his wheels together, Indra, run their course  With thee and with the Sun alike,

4.31.d: उत स्मा हि त्वामाहुरिन्मघवानं शचीपते । दातारमविदीधयुम् ॥
4.31.e: So even, Lord of Power and Might, the people call thee Maghavan,  Giver, who pauses not to think.

4.31.d: उत स्मा सद्य इत्परि शशमानाय सुन्वते । पुरू चिन्मंहसे वसु ॥
4.31.e: And verily to him who toils and presses Soma juice for thee  Thou quickly givest ample wealth.

4.31.d: नहि ष्मा ते शतं चन राधो वरन्त आमुरः । न च्यौत्नानि करिष्यतः ॥
4.31.e: No, not a hundred hinderers can check thy gracious bounty's flow,  Nor thy great deeds when thou wilt act.

4.31.d: अस्माँ अवन्तु ते शतमस्मान्त्सहस्रमूतयः । अस्मान्विश्वा अभिष्टयः ॥
4.31.e: May thine assistance keep us safe, thy hundred and thy thousand aids:  May all thy favours strengthen us.

4.31.d: अस्माँ इहा वृणीष्व सख्याय स्वस्तये । महो राये दिवित्मते ॥
4.31.e: Do thou elect us this place for friendship and prosperity,  And great celestial opulence.

4.31.d: अस्माँ अविड्ढि विश्वहेन्द्र राया परीणसा । अस्मान्विश्वाभिरूतिभिः ॥
4.31.e: Favour us, Indra, evermore with overflowing store of wealth:  With all thy succours aid thou us.

4.31.d: अस्मभ्यं ताँ अपा वृधि व्रजाँ अस्तेव गोमतः । नवाभिरिन्द्रोतिभिः ॥
4.31.e: With new protections, Indra, like an archer, open thou for us  The stables that are filled with kine.

4.31.d: अस्माकं धृष्णुया रथो द्युमाँ इन्द्रानपच्युतः । गव्युरश्वयुरीयते ॥
4.31.e: Our chariot, Indra, boldly moves endued with splendour, ne’er repulsed,  Winning for us both kine and steeds.

4.31.d: अस्माकमुत्तमं कृधि श्रवो देवेषु सूर्य । वर्षिष्ठं द्यामिवोपरि ॥
4.31.e: O Sūrya, make our fame to be most excellent among the Gods,  Most lofty as the heaven on high.

4.32.d: आ तू न इन्द्र वृत्रहन्नस्माकमर्धमा गहि । महान्महीभिरूतिभिः ॥
4.32.e: O THOU who slewest Vṛtra, come, O Indra, hither to our side,  Mighty One with thy mighty aids.

4.32.d: भृमिश्चिद्घासि तूतुजिरा चित्र चित्रिणीष्वा । चित्रं कृणोष्यूतये ॥
4.32.e: Swift and impetuous art thou, wondrous amid the well-dressed folk:  Thou doest marvels for our help.

4.32.d: दभ्रेभिश्चिच्छशीयांसं हंसि व्राधन्तमोजसा । सखिभिर्ये त्वे सचा ॥
4.32.e: Even with the weak thou smitest down him  who is stronger, with thy strength  The mighty, with the Friends thou hast.

4.32.d: वयमिन्द्र त्वे सचा वयं त्वाभि नोनुमः । अस्मास्माँ इदुदव ॥
4.32.e: O Indra, we are close to thee; to thee we sing aloud our songs:  Help and defend us, even us.

4.32.d: स नश्चित्राभिरद्रिवोऽनवद्याभिरूतिभिः । अनाधृष्टाभिरा गहि ॥
4.32.e: As such, O Caster of the Stone, come with thy succours wonderful,  Blameless, and irresistible.

4.32.d: भूयामो षु त्वावतः सखाय इन्द्र गोमतः । युजो वाजाय घृष्वये ॥
4.32.e: May we be friends of one like thee, O Indra, with the wealth of kine,  Comrades for lively energy.

4.32.d: त्वं ह्येक ईशिष इन्द्र वाजस्य गोमतः । स नो यन्धि महीमिषम् ॥
4.32.e: For thou, O Indra, art alone the Lord of strength that comes from kine  So grant thou us abundant food.

4.32.d: न त्वा वरन्ते अन्यथा यद्दित्ससि स्तुतो मघम् । स्तोतृभ्य इन्द्र गिर्वणः ॥
4.32.e: They turn thee not another way, when, lauded, Lover of the Song,  Thou wilt give wealth to those who praise.

4.32.d: अभि त्वा गोतमा गिरानूषत प्र दावने । इन्द्र वाजाय घृष्वये ॥
4.32.e: The Gotamas have sung their song of praise to thee that thou mayst give,  Indra, for lively energy.

4.32.d: प्र ते वोचाम वीर्या३ या मन्दसान आरुजः । पुरो दासीरभीत्य ॥
4.32.e: We will declare thy hero deeds, what Dāsa forts thou brakest down,  Attacking them in rapturous joy.

4.32.d: ता ते गृणन्ति वेधसो यानि चकर्थ पौंस्या । सुतेष्विन्द्र गिर्वणः ॥
4.32.e: The sages sing those manly deeds which, Indra, Lover of the Song,  Thou wroughtest when the Soma flowed.

4.32.d: अवीवृधन्त गोतमा इन्द्र त्वे स्तोमवाहसः । ऐषु धा वीरवद्यशः ॥
4.32.e: Indra, the Gotamas who bring thee praises have grown strong by thee.  Give them renown with hero sons.

4.32.d: यच्चिद्धि शश्वतामसीन्द्र साधारणस्त्वम् । तं त्वा वयं हवामहे ॥
4.32.e: For, Indra, verily thou art the general treasure even of all .  Thee, therefore, do we invocate.

4.32.d: अर्वाचीनो वसो भवास्मे सु मत्स्वान्धसः । सोमानामिन्द्र सोमपाः ॥
4.32.e: Excellent Indra, turn to us: glad thee among us with the juice  Of Somas, Soma-drinker thou.

4.32.d: अस्माकं त्वा मतीनामा स्तोम इन्द्र यच्छतु । अर्वागा वर्तया हरी ॥
4.32.e: May praise from us who think Qn thee, O Indra, bring thee near to us.  Turn thy two Bay Steeds hitherward.

4.32.d: पुरोळाशं च नो घसो जोषयासे गिरश्च नः । वधूयुरिव योषणाम् ॥
4.32.e: Eat of our sacrificial cake: rejoice thee in the songs we sing.  Even as a lover in his bride.

4.32.d: सहस्रं व्यतीनां युक्तानामिन्द्रमीमहे । शतं सोमस्य खार्यः ॥
4.32.e: To India for a thousand steeds well-trained and fleet of foot we pray,  And hundred jars of Soma juice.

4.32.d: सहस्रा ते शता वयं गवामा च्यावयामसि । अस्मत्रा राध एतु ते ॥
4.32.e: We make a hundred of thy kine, yea, and a thousand, hasten nigh:  So let thy bounty come to us.

4.32.d: दश ते कलशानां हिरण्यानामधीमहि । भूरिदा असि वृत्रहन् ॥
4.32.e: We have obtained, a gift from thee, ten water-ewers wrought of gold:  Thou, Vṛtra-slayer, givest much.

4.32.d: भूरिदा भूरि देहि नो मा दभ्रं भूर्या भर । भूरि घेदिन्द्र दित्ससि ॥
4.32.e: A bounteous Giver, give us much, bring much and not a trifling gift:  Much, Indra, wilt thou fain bestow.

4.32.d: भूरिदा ह्यसि श्रुतः पुरुत्रा शूर वृत्रहन् । आ नो भजस्व राधसि ॥
4.32.e: O Vṛtra-slayer, thou art famed in many a place as bountiful  Hero, thy bounty let us share.

4.32.d: प्र ते बभ्रू विचक्षण शंसामि गोषणो नपात् । माभ्यां गा अनु शिश्रथः ॥
4.32.e: I praise thy pair of Tawny Steeds, wise Son of him who giveth kine  Terrify not the cows with these.

4.32.d: कनीनकेव विद्रधे नवे द्रुपदे अर्भके । बभ्रू यामेषु शोभेते ॥
4.32.e: Like two slight images of girls, unrobed, upon a new-wrought post,  So shine the Bay Steeds in their course.

4.32.d: अरं म उस्रयाम्णेऽरमनुस्रयाम्णे । बभ्रू यामेष्वस्रिधा ॥
4.32.e: For me the Bays are ready when I start, or start not, with the dawn, Innocuous in the ways they take.

4.33.d: प्र ऋभुभ्यो दूतमिव वाचमिष्य उपस्तिरे श्वैतरीं धेनुमीळे । ये वातजूतास्तरणिभिरेवैः परि द्यां सद्यो अपसो बभूवुः ॥
4.33.e: I SEND my voice as herald to the Ṛbhus; I crave the white cow for the overspreading.  Wind-sped, the Skillful Ones in rapid motion have in an instant compassed round the heaven.

4.33.d: यदारमक्रन्नृभवः पितृभ्यां परिविष्टी वेषणा दंसनाभिः । आदिद्देवानामुप सख्यमायन्धीरासः पुष्टिमवहन्मनायै ॥
4.33.e: What time the Rbus had with care and marvels done proper service to assist their Parents,  They won the friendship of the Gods; the Sages carried away the fruit of their devotion.

4.33.d: पुनर्ये चक्रुः पितरा युवाना सना यूपेव जरणा शयाना । ते वाजो विभ्वाँ ऋभुरिन्द्रवन्तो मधुप्सरसो नोऽवन्तु यज्ञम् ॥
4.33.e: May they who made their Parents, who were lying like posts that moulder, young again for ever,—  May Vāja, Vibhvan, Ṛbhu, joined with Indra , protect our sacrifice, the Soma-lovers.

4.33.d: यत्संवत्समृभवो गामरक्षन्यत्संवत्समृभवो मा अपिंशन् । यत्संवत्समभरन्भासो अस्यास्ताभिः शमीभिरमृतत्वमाशुः ॥
4.33.e: As for a year the Ṛbhus kept the Milch-cow, throughout a year fashioned and formed her body,  And through a year's space still sustained her brightness, through these their labours they were made immortal.

4.33.d: ज्येष्ठ आह चमसा द्वा करेति कनीयान्त्रीन्कृणवामेत्याह । कनिष्ठ आह चतुरस्करेति त्वष्ट ऋभवस्तत्पनयद्वचो वः ॥
4.33.e: Two beakers let us make,—thus said the eldest. Let us make three,—this was the younger's sentence.  Four beakers let us make,—thus spoke the youngest. Tvaṣṭar approved this rede of yours, O Ṛbhus.

4.33.d: सत्यमूचुर्नर एवा हि चक्रुरनु स्वधामृभवो जग्मुरेताम् । विभ्राजमानाँश्चमसाँ अहेवावेनत्त्वष्टा चतुरो ददृश्वान् ॥
4.33.e: The men spake truth and even so they acted: this Godlike way of theirs the Ṛbhus followed.  And Tvaṣṭar, when he looked on the four beakers resplendent as the day, was moved with envy.

4.33.d: द्वादश द्यून्यदगोह्यस्यातिथ्ये रणन्नृभवः ससन्तः । सुक्षेत्राकृण्वन्ननयन्त सिन्धून्धन्वातिष्ठन्नोषधीर्निम्नमापः ॥
4.33.e: When for twelve days the Ṛbhus joyed reposing as guests of him who never may be hidden,  They made fair fertile fields, they brought the rivers. Plants spread o’er deserts, waters filled the hollows.

4.33.d: रथं ये चक्रुः सुवृतं नरेष्ठां ये धेनुं विश्वजुवं विश्वरूपाम् । त आ तक्षन्त्वृभवो रयिं नः स्ववसः स्वपसः सुहस्ताः ॥
4.33.e: May they who formed the swift car, bearing Heroes, and the Cow omniform and all-impelling,  Even may they form wealth for us,—the Ṛbhus, dexterous-handed, deft in work and gracious.

4.33.d: अपो ह्येषामजुषन्त देवा अभि क्रत्वा मनसा दीध्यानाः । वाजो देवानामभवत्सुकर्मेन्द्रस्य ऋभुक्षा वरुणस्य विभ्वा ॥
4.33.e: So in their work the Gods had satisfaction, pondering it with thought and mental insight.  The Gods’ expert artificer was Vāja, Indra's Ṛbhukṣan, Varuṇa's was Vibhvan.

4.33.d: ये हरी मेधयोक्था मदन्त इन्द्राय चक्रुः सुयुजा ये अश्वा । ते रायस्पोषं द्रविणान्यस्मे धत्त ऋभवः क्षेमयन्तो न मित्रम् ॥
4.33.e: They who made glad with sacrifice and praises, wrought the two Bays, his docile Steeds, for Indra,—  Ṛbhus, as those who wish a friend to prosper, bestow upon us gear and growth of riches.

4.33.d: इदाह्नः पीतिमुत वो मदं धुर्न ऋते श्रान्तस्य सख्याय देवाः । ते नूनमस्मे ऋभवो वसूनि तृतीये अस्मिन्त्सवने दधात ॥
4.33.e: This day have they set gladdening drink before you. Not without toil are Gods inclined to friendship.  Therefore do ye who are so great, O Ṛbhus, vouchsafe us treasures at this third libation.

4.34.d: ऋभुर्विभ्वा वाज इन्द्रो नो अच्छेमं यज्ञं रत्नधेयोप यात । इदा हि वो धिषणा देव्यह्नामधात्पीतिं सं मदा अग्मता वः ॥
4.34.e: To this our sacrifice come Ṛbhu, Vibhvan, Vāja, and Indra with the gift of riches,  Because this day hath Dhiṣaṇā the Goddess set drink for you: the gladdening draughts have reached you.

4.34.d: विदानासो जन्मनो वाजरत्ना उत ऋतुभिर्ऋभवो मादयध्वम् । सं वो मदा अग्मत सं पुरंधिः सुवीरामस्मे रयिमेरयध्वम् ॥
4.34.e: Knowing your birth and rich in gathered treasure, Ṛbhus, rejoice together with the Ṛtus.  The gladdening draughts and wisdom have approached you: send ye us riches with good store of heroes.

4.34.d: अयं वो यज्ञ ऋभवोऽकारि यमा मनुष्वत्प्रदिवो दधिध्वे । प्र वोऽच्छा जुजुषाणासो अस्थुरभूत विश्वे अग्रियोत वाजाः ॥
4.34.e: For you was made this sacrifice, O Ṛbhus, which ye, like men, won for yourselves aforetime.  To you come all who find in you their pleasure: ye all were—even the two elder—Vājas.

4.34.d: अभूदु वो विधते रत्नधेयमिदा नरो दाशुषे मर्त्याय । पिबत वाजा ऋभवो ददे वो महि तृतीयं सवनं मदाय ॥
4.34.e: Now for the mortal worshipper, O Heroes, for him who served you, was the gift of riches.  Drink, Vājas, Ṛbhus! unto you is offered, to gladden you, the third and great libation.

4.34.d: आ वाजा यातोप न ऋभुक्षा महो नरो द्रविणसो गृणानाः । आ वः पीतयोऽभिपित्वे अह्नामिमा अस्तं नवस्व इव ग्मन् ॥
4.34.e: Come to us, Heroes, Vājas and Ṛbhukṣans, glorified for the sake of mighty treasure.  These draughts approach you as the day is closing, as cows, whose calves are newly-born, their stable.

4.34.d: आ नपातः शवसो यातनोपेमं यज्ञं नमसा हूयमानाः । सजोषसः सूरयो यस्य च स्थ मध्वः पात रत्नधा इन्द्रवन्तः ॥
4.34.e: Come to this sacrifice of ours, ye Children of Strength, invoked with humble adoration.  Drink of this meath, Wealth-givers, joined with Indra with whom ye are in full accord, ye Princes.

4.34.d: सजोषा इन्द्र वरुणेन सोमं सजोषाः पाहि गिर्वणो मरुद्भिः । अग्रेपाभिर्ऋतुपाभिः सजोषा ग्नास्पत्नीभी रत्नधाभिः सजोषाः ॥
4.34.e: Close knit with Varuṇa drink the Soma, Indra; close-knit, Hymn-lover! with the Maruts drink it:  Close-knit with drinkers first, who drink in season; close-knit with heavenly Dames who give us treasures.

4.34.d: सजोषस आदित्यैर्मादयध्वं सजोषस ऋभवः पर्वतेभिः । सजोषसो दैव्येना सवित्रा सजोषसः सिन्धुभी रत्नधेभिः ॥
4.34.e: Rejoice in full accord with the Ādityas, in concord with the Parvatas, O Ṛbhus;  In full accord with Savitar, Divine One; in full accord with floods that pour forth riches.

4.34.d: ये अश्विना ये पितरा य ऊती धेनुं ततक्षुर्ऋभवो ये अश्वा । ये अंसत्रा य ऋधग्रोदसी ये विभ्वो नरः स्वपत्यानि चक्रुः ॥
4.34.e: Ṛbhus, who helped their Parents and the Aśvins, who formed the Milch-cow and the pair of horses,  Made armour, set the heaven and earth asunder,—far- reaching Heroes, they have made good offspring.

4.34.d: ये गोमन्तं वाजवन्तं सुवीरं रयिं धत्थ वसुमन्तं पुरुक्षुम् । ते अग्रेपा ऋभवो मन्दसाना अस्मे धत्त ये च रातिं गृणन्ति ॥
4.34.e: Ye who have wealth in cattle and in booty, in heroes, in rich sustenance and treasure,  Such, O ye Ṛbhus, first to drink, rejoicing, give unto us and those who laud our present.

4.34.d: नापाभूत न वोऽतीतृषामानिःशस्ता ऋभवो यज्ञे अस्मिन् । समिन्द्रेण मदथ सं मरुद्भिः सं राजभी रत्नधेयाय देवाः ॥
4.34.e: Ye were not far: we have not left you thirsting, blameless in this our sacrifice, O Ṛbhus.  Rejoice you with the Maruts and with Indra, with the Kings, Gods! that ye may give us riches.

4.35.d: इहोप यात शवसो नपातः सौधन्वना ऋभवो माप भूत । अस्मिन्हि वः सवने रत्नधेयं गमन्त्विन्द्रमनु वो मदासः ॥
4.35.e: Come hither, O ye Sons of Strength, ye Ṛbhus; stay not afar, ye Children of Sudhanvan.  At this libation is your gift of treasure. Let gladdening draughts approach you after Indra's.

4.35.d: आगन्नृभूणामिह रत्नधेयमभूत्सोमस्य सुषुतस्य पीतिः । सुकृत्यया यत्स्वपस्यया चँ एकं विचक्र चमसं चतुर्धा ॥
4.35.e: Hither is come the Ṛbhus' gift of riches; here was the drinking of the well-pressed Soma,  Since by dexterity and skill as craftsmen ye made the single chalice to be fourfold

4.35.d: व्यकृणोत चमसं चतुर्धा सखे वि शिक्षेत्यब्रवीत । अथैत वाजा अमृतस्य पन्थां गणं देवानामृभवः सुहस्ताः ॥
4.35.e: Ye made fourfold the chalice that wag single: ye spake these words and said, O Friend, assist us;  Then, Vājas! gained the path of life eternal, deft-handed Ṛbhus, to the Gods’ assembly.

4.35.d: किम्मयः स्विच्चमस एष आस यं काव्येन चतुरो विचक्र । अथा सुनुध्वं सवनं मदाय पात ऋभवो मधुनः सोम्यस्य ॥
4.35.e: Out of what substance was that chalice fashioned which ye made fourfold by your art and wisdom?  Now for the gladdening draught press out the liquor, and drink, O Ṛbhus, of die meath of Soma.

4.35.d: शच्याकर्त पितरा युवाना शच्याकर्त चमसं देवपानम् । शच्या हरी धनुतरावतष्टेन्द्रवाहावृभवो वाजरत्नाः ॥
4.35.e: Ye with your cunning made your Parents youthful; the cup, for Gods to drink, ye formed with cunning;  With cunning, Ṛbhus, rich in treasure, fashioned the two swift Tawny Steeds who carry Indra.

4.35.d: यो वः सुनोत्यभिपित्वे अह्नां तीव्रं वाजासः सवनं मदाय । तस्मै रयिमृभवः सर्ववीरमा तक्षत वृषणो मन्दसानाः ॥
4.35.e: Whoso pours out for you, when days are closing, the sharp libation for your joy, O Vājas,  For him, O mighty Ṛbhus, ye, rejoicing, have fashioned wealth with plenteous store of heroes.

4.35.d: प्रातः सुतमपिबो हर्यश्व माध्यंदिनं सवनं केवलं ते । समृभुभिः पिबस्व रत्नधेभिः सखीँर्याँ इन्द्र चकृषे सुकृत्या ॥
4.35.e: Lord of Bay Steeds, at dawn the juice thou drankest: thine, only thine, is the noonday libation.  Now drink thou with the wealth-bestowing Ṛbhus, whom for their skill thou madest friends, O Indra.

4.35.d: ये देवासो अभवता सुकृत्या श्येना इवेदधि दिवि निषेद । ते रत्नं धात शवसो नपातः सौधन्वना अभवतामृतासः ॥
4.35.e: Ye, whom your artist skill hath raised to Godhead have set you down above in heaven like falcons.  So give us riches, Children of Sudhanvan, O Sons of Strength; ye have become immortal.

4.35.d: यत्तृतीयं सवनं रत्नधेयमकृणुध्वं स्वपस्या सुहस्ताः । तदृभवः परिषिक्तं व एतत्सं मदेभिरिन्द्रियेभिः पिबध्वम् ॥
4.35.e: The third libation, that bestoweth treasure, which ye have won by skill, ye dexterous-handed,—  This drink hath been effused for you, O Ṛbhus . drink it with high delight, with joy like Indra's.

4.36.d: अनश्वो जातो अनभीशुरुक्थ्यो३ रथस्त्रिचक्रः परि वर्तते रजः । महत्तद्वो देव्यस्य प्रवाचनं द्यामृभवः पृथिवीं यच्च पुष्यथ ॥
4.36.e: THE car that was not made for horses or for reins, three-wheeled, worthy of lauds, rolls round the firmament.  That is the great announcement of your Deity, that, O ye Ṛbhus, ye sustain the earth and heaven.

4.36.d: रथं ये चक्रुः सुवृतं सुचेतसोऽविह्वरन्तं मनसस्परि ध्यया । ताँ ऊ न्व१स्य सवनस्य पीतय आ वो वाजा ऋभवो वेदयामसि ॥
4.36.e: Ye Sapient Ones who made the lightly-rolling car out of your mind, by thought, the car that never errs,  You, being such, to drink of this drink-offering, you, O ye Vājas, and ye Ṛbhus, we invoke.

4.36.d: तद्वो वाजा ऋभवः सुप्रवाचनं देवेषु विभ्वो अभवन्महित्वनम् । जिव्री यत्सन्ता पितरा सनाजुरा पुनर्युवाना चरथाय तक्षथ ॥
4.36.e: O Vājas, Ṛbhus, reaching far, among the Gods this was your exaltation gloriously declared,  In that your aged Parents, worn with length of days, ye wrought again to youth so that they moved at will.

4.36.d: एकं वि चक्र चमसं चतुर्वयं निश्चर्मणो गामरिणीत धीतिभिः । अथा देवेष्वमृतत्वमानश श्रुष्टी वाजा ऋभवस्तद्व उक्थ्यम् ॥
4.36.e: The chalice that wag single ye have made fourfold, and by your wisdom brought the Cow forth from the hide.  So quickly, mid the Gods, ye gained immortal life. Vājas and Ṛbhus, your great work must be extolled.

4.36.d: ऋभुतो रयिः प्रथमश्रवस्तमो वाजश्रुतासो यमजीजनन्नरः । विभ्वतष्टो विदथेषु प्रवाच्यो यं देवासोऽवथा स विचर्षणिः ॥
4.36.e: Wealth from the Ṛbhus is most glorious in renown, that which the Heroes, famed for vigour, have produced.  In synods must be sung the car which Vibhvan wrought: that which ye favour, Gods! is famed among mankind.

4.36.d: स वाज्यर्वा स ऋषिर्वचस्यया स शूरो अस्ता पृतनासु दुष्टरः । स रायस्पोषं स सुवीर्यं दधे यं वाजो विभ्वाँ ऋभवो यमाविषुः ॥
4.36.e: Strong is the steed, the man a sage in eloquence, the bowman is a hero hard to beat in fight,  Great store of wealth and manly power hath he obtained whom Vāja, Vibhvan, Ṛbhus have looked kindly on.

4.36.d: श्रेष्ठं वः पेशो अधि धायि दर्शतं स्तोमो वाजा ऋभवस्तं जुजुष्टन । धीरासो हि ष्ठा कवयो विपश्चितस्तान्व एना ब्रह्मणा वेदयामसि ॥
4.36.e: To you hath been assigned the fairest ornament, the hymn of praise: Vājas and Ṛbhus, joy therein;  For ye have lore and wisdom and poetic skill: as such, with this our prayer we call on you to come.

4.36.d: यूयमस्मभ्यं धिषणाभ्यस्परि विद्वांसो विश्वा नर्याणि भोजना । द्युमन्तं वाजं वृषशुष्ममुत्तममा नो रयिमृभवस्तक्षता वयः ॥
4.36.e: According to the wishes of our hearts may ye, who have full knowledge of all the delights of men,  Fashion for us, O Ṛbhus, power and splendid wealth, rich in high courage, excellent, and vital strength.

4.36.d: इह प्रजामिह रयिं रराणा इह श्रवो वीरवत्तक्षता नः । येन वयं चितयेमात्यन्यान्तं वाजं चित्रमृभवो ददा नः ॥
4.36.e: Bestowing on us here riches and offspring, here fashion fame for us befitting heroes.  Vouchsafe us wealth of splendid sort, O Ṛbhus, that we may make us more renowned than others.

4.37.d: उप नो वाजा अध्वरमृभुक्षा देवा यात पथिभिर्देवयानैः । यथा यज्ञं मनुषो विक्ष्वा३सु दधिध्वे रण्वाः सुदिनेष्वह्नाम् ॥
4.37.e: COME to our sacrifice, Vājas, Ṛbhukṣans, Gods, by the paths which Gods are wont to travel,  As ye, gay Gods, accept in splendid weather the sacrifice among these folk of Manus.

4.37.d: ते वो हृदे मनसे सन्तु यज्ञा जुष्टासो अद्य घृतनिर्णिजो गुः । प्र वः सुतासो हरयन्त पूर्णाः क्रत्वे दक्षाय हर्षयन्त पीताः ॥
4.37.e: May these rites please you in your heart and spirit; may the drops clothed in oil this day approach you.  May the abundant juices bear you onward to power and strength, and, when imbibed, delight you.

4.37.d: त्र्युदायं देवहितं यथा वः स्तोमो वाजा ऋभुक्षणो ददे वः । जुह्वे मनुष्वदुपरासु विक्षु युष्मे सचा बृहद्दिवेषु सोमम् ॥
4.37.e: Your threefold going near is God-appointed, so praise is given you, Vājas and Ṛbhukṣans.  So, Manus-like, mid younger folk I offer, to you who are aloft in heaven, the Soma.

4.37.d: पीवोअश्वाः शुचद्रथा हि भूतायःशिप्रा वाजिनः सुनिष्काः । इन्द्रस्य सूनो शवसो नपातोऽनु वश्चेत्यग्रियं मदाय ॥
4.37.e: Strong, with fair chains of gold and jaws of iron, ye have a splendid car and well-fed horses.  Ye Sons of Strength, ye progeny of Indra, to you the best is offered to delight you.

4.37.d: ऋभुमृभुक्षणो रयिं वाजे वाजिन्तमं युजम् । इन्द्रस्वन्तं हवामहे सदासातममश्विनम् ॥
4.37.e: Ṛbhukṣans! him, for handy wealth, the mightiest comrade in the fight,  Him, Indra's equal, we invoke, most bounteous ever, rich in steeds.

4.37.d: सेदृभवो यमवथ यूयमिन्द्रश्च मर्त्यम् । स धीभिरस्तु सनिता मेधसाता सो अर्वता ॥
4.37.e: The mortal man whom, Ṛbhus, ye and Indra favour with your help,  Must be successful, by his thoughts, at sacrifice and with the steed.

4.37.d: वि नो वाजा ऋभुक्षणः पथश्चितन यष्टवे । अस्मभ्यं सूरयः स्तुता विश्वा आशास्तरीषणि ॥
4.37.e: O Vājas and Ṛbhukṣans, free for us the paths to sacrifice,  Ye Princes, lauded, that we may press forward to each point of heaven.

4.37.d: तं नो वाजा ऋभुक्षण इन्द्र नासत्या रयिम् । समश्वं चर्षणिभ्य आ पुरु शस्त मघत्तये ॥
4.37.e: O Vājas and Ṛbhukṣans, ye Nāsatyas, Indra, bless this wealth,  And, before other men's, the steed, that ample riches may be won.

4.38.d: उतो हि वां दात्रा सन्ति पूर्वा या पूरुभ्यस्त्रसदस्युर्नितोशे । क्षेत्रासां ददथुरुर्वरासां घनं दस्युभ्यो अभिभूतिमुग्रम् ॥
4.38.e: FROM you two came the gifts in days aforetime which Trasadasyu granted to the Pūrus.  Ye gave the winner of our fields and plough-lands, and the strong smiter who subdued the Dasyus.

4.38.d: उत वाजिनं पुरुनिष्षिध्वानं दधिक्रामु ददथुर्विश्वकृष्टिम् । ऋजिप्यं श्येनं प्रुषितप्सुमाशुं चर्कृत्यमर्यो नृपतिं न शूरम् ॥
4.38.e: And ye gave mighty Dadhikrās, the giver of many gifts, who visiteth all people,  Impetuous hawk, swift and of varied colour, like a brave King whom each true man must honour.

4.38.d: यं सीमनु प्रवतेव द्रवन्तं विश्वः पूरुर्मदति हर्षमाणः । पड्भिर्गृध्यन्तं मेधयुं न शूरं रथतुरं वातमिव ध्रजन्तम् ॥
4.38.e: Whom, as ’twere down a precipice, swift rushing, each Pūru praises and his heart rejoices,—  Springing forth like a hero fain for battle, whirling the car and flying like the tempest.

4.38.d: यः स्मारुन्धानो गध्या समत्सु सनुतरश्चरति गोषु गच्छन् । आविर्ऋजीको विदथा निचिक्यत्तिरो अरतिं पर्याप आयोः ॥
4.38.e: Who gaineth precious booty in the combats and moveth, winning spoil, among the cattle;  Shown in bright colour, looking on the assemblies, beyond the churl, to worship of the living.

4.38.d: उत स्मैनं वस्त्रमथिं न तायुमनु क्रोशन्ति क्षितयो भरेषु । नीचायमानं जसुरिं न श्येनं श्रवश्चाच्छा पशुमच्च यूथम् ॥
4.38.e: Loudly the folk cry after him in battles, as ’twere a thief who steals away a garment;  Speeding to glory, or a herd of cattle, even as a hungry falcon swooping downward.

4.38.d: उत स्मासु प्रथमः सरिष्यन्नि वेवेति श्रेणिभी रथानाम् । स्रजं कृण्वानो जन्यो न शुभ्वा रेणुं रेरिहत्किरणं ददश्वान् ॥
4.38.e: And, fain to come forth first amid these armies, this way and that with rows of cars he rushes,  Gay like a bridesman, making him a garland, tossing the dust, champing the rein that holds him.

4.38.d: उत स्य वाजी सहुरिर्ऋतावा शुश्रूषमाणस्तन्वा समर्ये । तुरं यतीषु तुरयन्नृजिप्योऽधि भ्रुवोः किरते रेणुमृञ्जन् ॥
4.38.e: And that strong Steed, victorious and faithful, obedient with his body in the combat,  Speeding straight on amid the swiftly pressing, casts o’er his brows the dust he tosses upward.

4.38.d: उत स्मास्य तन्यतोरिव द्योर्ऋघायतो अभियुजो भयन्ते । यदा सहस्रमभि षीमयोधीद्दुर्वर्तुः स्मा भवति भीम ऋञ्जन् ॥
4.38.e: And at his thunder, like the roar of heaven, those who attack tremble and are affrighted;  For when he fights against embattled thousands, dread is he in his striving; none may stay him.

4.38.d: उत स्मास्य पनयन्ति जना जूतिं कृष्टिप्रो अभिभूतिमाशोः । उतैनमाहुः समिथे वियन्तः परा दधिक्रा असरत्सहस्रैः ॥
4.38.e: The people praise the overpowering swiftness of this fleet Steed who giveth men abundance.  Of him they say when drawing back from battle. Dadhikrās hath sped forward with his thousands.

4.38.d: आ दधिक्राः शवसा पञ्च कृष्टीः सूर्य इव ज्योतिषापस्ततान । सहस्रसाः शतसा वाज्यर्वा पृणक्तु मध्वा समिमा वचांसि ॥
4.38.e: Dadhikrās hath o’erspread the Fivefold People with vigour, as the Sun lightens the waters.  May the strong Steed who winneth hundreds, thousands, requite with sweetness these my words and praises.

4.39.d: आशुं दधिक्रां तमु नु ष्टवाम दिवस्पृथिव्या उत चर्किराम । उच्छन्तीर्मामुषसः सूदयन्त्वति विश्वानि दुरितानि पर्षन् ॥
4.39.e: Now give we praise to Dadhikrās the rapid, and mention in our laud the Earth and Heaven.  May the Dawns flushing move me to exertion, and bear me safely over every trouble.

4.39.d: महश्चर्कर्म्यर्वतः क्रतुप्रा दधिक्राव्णः पुरुवारस्य वृष्णः । यं पूरुभ्यो दीदिवांसं नाग्निं ददथुर्मित्रावरुणा ततुरिम् ॥
4.39.e: I praise the mighty Steed who fills my spirit, the Stallion Dadhikrāvan rich in bounties,  Whom, swift of foot and shining bright as Agni, ye, Varuṇa and Mitra, gave to Pūrus.

4.39.d: यो अश्वस्य दधिक्राव्णो अकारीत्समिद्धे अग्ना उषसो व्युष्टौ । अनागसं तमदितिः कृणोतु स मित्रेण वरुणेना सजोषाः ॥
4.39.e: Him who hath honoured, when the flame is kindled at break of dawn, the Courser Dadhikrāvan,  Him, of one mind with Varuṇa and Mitra may Aditi make free from all transgression.

4.39.d: दधिक्राव्ण इष ऊर्जो महो यदमन्महि मरुतां नाम भद्रम् । स्वस्तये वरुणं मित्रमग्निं हवामह इन्द्रं वज्रबाहुम् ॥
4.39.e: When we remember mighty Dadhikrāvan our food and strength, then the blest name of Maruts,  Varuṇa, Mitra, we invoke for welfare, and Agni, and the thunder-wielding Indra.

4.39.d: इन्द्रमिवेदुभये वि ह्वयन्त उदीराणा यज्ञमुपप्रयन्तः । दधिक्रामु सूदनं मर्त्याय ददथुर्मित्रावरुणा नो अश्वम् ॥
4.39.e: Both sides invoke him as they call on Indra when they stir forth and turn to sacrificing.  To us have Varuṇa and Mitra granted the Courser Dadhikrās, a guide for mortals.

4.39.d: दधिक्राव्णो अकारिषं जिष्णोरश्वस्य वाजिनः । सुरभि नो मुखा करत्प्र ण आयूंषि तारिषत् ॥
4.39.e: So have I glorified with praise strong Dadhikrāvan, conquering Steed.  Sweet may he make our mouths; may he prolong the days we have to live.

4.40.d: दधिक्राव्ण इदु नु चर्किराम विश्वा इन्मामुषसः सूदयन्तु । अपामग्नेरुषसः सूर्यस्य बृहस्पतेराङ्गिरसस्य जिष्णोः ॥
4.40.e: LET us recite the praise of Dadhikrāvan: may all the Mornings move me to exertion;  Praise of the Lord of Waters, Dawn, and Agni, Bṛhaspati Son of Aṅgiras, and Sūrya.

4.40.d: सत्वा भरिषो गविषो दुवन्यसच्छ्रवस्यादिष उषसस्तुरण्यसत् । सत्यो द्रवो द्रवरः पतंगरो दधिक्रावेषमूर्जं स्वर्जनत् ॥
4.40.e: Brave, seeking war and booty, dwelling with the good and with the swift, may he hasten the food of Dawn.  May he the true, the fleet, the lover of the course, the bird-like Dadhikrāvan, bring food, strength, and light.

4.40.d: उत स्मास्य द्रवतस्तुरण्यतः पर्णं न वेरनु वाति प्रगर्धिनः । श्येनस्येव ध्रजतो अङ्कसं परि दधिक्राव्णः सहोर्जा तरित्रतः ॥
4.40.e: His pinion, rapid runner, fans him m his way, as of a bird that hastens onward to its aim,  And, as it were a falcon's gliding through the air, strikes Dadhikrāvan's side as he speeds on with might.

4.40.d: उत स्य वाजी क्षिपणिं तुरण्यति ग्रीवायां बद्धो अपिकक्ष आसनि । क्रतुं दधिक्रा अनु संतवीत्वत्पथामङ्कांस्यन्वापनीफणत् ॥
4.40.e: Bound by the neck and by the flanks and by the mouth, the vigorous Courser lends new swiftness to his speed.  Drawing himself together, as his strength allows, Dadhikrās springs along the windings of the paths.

4.40.d: हंसः शुचिषद्वसुरन्तरिक्षसद्धोता वेदिषदतिथिर्दुरोणसत् । नृषद्वरसदृतसद्व्योमसदब्जा गोजा ऋतजा अद्रिजा ऋतम् ॥
4.40.e: The Haṁsa homed in light, the Vasu in mid-air, the priest beside the altar, in the house the guest,  Dweller in noblest place, mid men, in truth, in sky, born of flood, kine, truth, mountain, he is holy Law.

4.41.d: इन्द्रा को वां वरुणा सुम्नमाप स्तोमो हविष्माँ अमृतो न होता । यो वां हृदि क्रतुमाँ अस्मदुक्तः पस्पर्शदिन्द्रावरुणा नमस्वान् ॥
4.41.e: WHAT laud, O Indra-Varuṇa, with oblation, hath like the Immortal Priest obtained your favour?  Hath our effectual laud, addressed with homage, touched you, O Indra-Varuṇa, in spirit?

4.41.d: इन्द्रा ह यो वरुणा चक्र आपी देवौ मर्तः सख्याय प्रयस्वान् । स हन्ति वृत्रा समिथेषु शत्रूनवोभिर्वा महद्भिः स प्र शृण्वे ॥
4.41.e: He who with dainty food hath won you, Indra and Varuṇa, Gods, as his allies to friendship,  Slayeth the Vṛtras and his foes in battles, and through your mighty favours is made famous.

4.41.d: इन्द्रा ह रत्नं वरुणा धेष्ठेत्था नृभ्यः शशमानेभ्यस्ता । यदी सखाया सख्याय सोमैः सुतेभिः सुप्रयसा मादयैते ॥
4.41.e: Indra and Varuṇa are most liberal givers of treasure to the men who toil to serve them,  When they, as Friends inclined to friendship, honoured with dainty food, delight in flowing Soma.

4.41.d: इन्द्रा युवं वरुणा दिद्युमस्मिन्नोजिष्ठमुग्रा नि वधिष्टं वज्रम् । यो नो दुरेवो वृकतिर्दभीतिस्तस्मिन्मिमाथामभिभूत्योजः ॥
4.41.e: Indra and Varuṇa, ye hurl, O Mighty, on him your strongest flashing bolt of thunder  Who treats us ill, the robber and oppressor: measure on him your overwhelming vigour.

4.41.d: इन्द्रा युवं वरुणा भूतमस्या धियः प्रेतारा वृषभेव धेनोः । सा नो दुहीयद्यवसेव गत्वी सहस्रधारा पयसा मही गौः ॥
4.41.e: O Indra-Varuṇa, be ye the lovers of this my song, as steers who love the milch-Cow.  Milk may it yield us as, gone forth to pasture, the great Cow pouring out her thousand rivers.

4.41.d: तोके हिते तनय उर्वरासु सूरो दृशीके वृषणश्च पौंस्ये । इन्द्रा नो अत्र वरुणा स्यातामवोभिर्दस्मा परितक्म्यायाम् ॥
4.41.e: For fertile fields, for worthy sons and grandsons, for the Sun's beauty and for steer-like vigour,  May Indra-Varuṇa with gracious favours work marvels for us in the stress of battle.

4.41.d: युवामिद्ध्यवसे पूर्व्याय परि प्रभूती गविषः स्वापी । वृणीमहे सख्याय प्रियाय शूरा मंहिष्ठा पितरेव शम्भू ॥
4.41.e: For you, as Princes, for your ancient kindness, good comrades of the man who seeks for booty,  We choose to us for the dear bond of friendship, most liberal Heroes bringing bliss like parents.

4.41.d: ता वां धियोऽवसे वाजयन्तीराजिं न जग्मुर्युवयूः सुदानू । श्रिये न गाव उप सोममस्थुरिन्द्रं गिरो वरुणं मे मनीषाः ॥
4.41.e: Showing their strength, these hymns for grace, Free-givers I have gone to you, devoted, as to battle.  For glory have they gone, as milk to Soma, to Indra-Varuṇa my thoughts and praises.

4.41.d: इमा इन्द्रं वरुणं मे मनीषा अग्मन्नुप द्रविणमिच्छमानाः । उपेमस्थुर्जोष्टार इव वस्वो रघ्वीरिव श्रवसो भिक्षमाणाः ॥
4.41.e: To Indra and to Varuṇa, desirous of gaining wealth have these my thoughts proceeded.  They have come nigh to you as treasure-lovers, like mares, fleet-footed, eager for the glory.

4.41.d: अश्व्यस्य त्मना रथ्यस्य पुष्टेर्नित्यस्य रायः पतयः स्याम । ता चक्राणा ऊतिभिर्नव्यसीभिरस्मत्रा रायो नियुतः सचन्ताम् ॥
4.41.e: May we ourselves be lords of during riches, of ample sustenance for car and hones.  So may the Twain who work with newest succours bring yoked teams hitherward to us and riches.

4.41.d: आ नो बृहन्ता बृहतीभिरूती इन्द्र यातं वरुण वाजसातौ । यद्दिद्यवः पृतनासु प्रक्रीळान्तस्य वां स्याम सनितार आजेः ॥
4.41.e: Come with your mighty succours, O ye Mighty; come, Indra-Varuṇa, to us in battle.  What time the flashing arrows play in combat, may we through you be winners in the contest.

4.42.d: मम द्विता राष्ट्रं क्षत्रियस्य विश्वायोर्विश्वे अमृता यथा नः । क्रतुं सचन्ते वरुणस्य देवा राजामि कृष्टेरुपमस्य वव्रेः ॥
4.42.e: I AM the royal Ruler, mine is empire, as mine who sway all life are all Immortals.  Varuṇa's will the Gods obey and follow. I am the King of men's most lofty cover.

4.42.d: अहं राजा वरुणो मह्यं तान्यसुर्याणि प्रथमा धारयन्त । क्रतुं सचन्ते वरुणस्य देवा राजामि कृष्टेरुपमस्य वव्रेः ॥
4.42.e: I am King Varuṇa. To me were given these first existing high celestial powers.  Varuṇa's will the Gods obey and follow. I am the King of men's most lofty cover.

4.42.d: अहमिन्द्रो वरुणस्ते महित्वोर्वी गभीरे रजसी सुमेके । त्वष्टेव विश्वा भुवनानि विद्वान्त्समैरयं रोदसी धारयं च ॥
4.42.e: I Varuṇa am Indra: in their greatness, these the two wide deep fairly-fashioned regions,  These the two world-halves have I, even as Tvaṣṭar knowing all beings, joined and held together.

4.42.d: अहमपो अपिन्वमुक्षमाणा धारयं दिवं सदन ऋतस्य । ऋतेन पुत्रो अदितेर्ऋतावोत त्रिधातु प्रथयद्वि भूम ॥
4.42.e: I made to flow the moisture-shedding waters, and set the heaven firm in the scat of Order.  By Law the Son of Aditi, Law Observer, hath spread abroad the world in threefold measure.

4.42.d: मां नरः स्वश्वा वाजयन्तो मां वृताः समरणे हवन्ते । कृणोम्याजिं मघवाहमिन्द्र इयर्मि रेणुमभिभूत्योजाः ॥
4.42.e: Heroes with noble horses, fain for battle, selected warriors, call on me in combat.  I Indra Maghavan, excite the conflict; I stir the dust, Lord of surpassing vigour.

4.42.d: अहं ता विश्वा चकरं नकिर्मा दैव्यं सहो वरते अप्रतीतम् । यन्मा सोमासो ममदन्यदुक्थोभे भयेते रजसी अपारे ॥
4.42.e: All this I did. The Gods’ own conquering power never impedeth me whom none opposeth.  When lauds and Soma juice have made me joyful, both the unbounded regions are affrighted.

4.42.d: विदुष्टे विश्वा भुवनानि तस्य ता प्र ब्रवीषि वरुणाय वेधः । त्वं वृत्राणि शृण्विषे जघन्वान्त्वं वृताँ अरिणा इन्द्र सिन्धून् ॥
4.42.e: All beings know these deeds of thine thou tellest this unto Varuṇa, thou great Disposer!  Thou art renowned as having slain the Vṛtras. Thou madest flow the floods that were obstructed.

4.42.d: अस्माकमत्र पितरस्त आसन्त्सप्त ऋषयो दौर्गहे बध्यमाने । त आयजन्त त्रसदस्युमस्या इन्द्रं न वृत्रतुरमर्धदेवम् ॥
4.42.e: Our fathers then were these, the Seven his, what time the son of Durgaha was captive.  For her they gained by sacrifice Trasadasyu, a demi-god, like Indra, conquering foemen.

4.42.d: पुरुकुत्सानी हि वामदाशद्धव्येभिरिन्द्रावरुणा नमोभिः । अथा राजानं त्रसदस्युमस्या वृत्रहणं ददथुरर्धदेवम् ॥
4.42.e: The spouse of Purukutsa gave oblations to you, O Indra-Varuṇa, with homage.  Then unto her ye gave King Trasadasyu, the demi-god, the slayer of the foeman.

4.42.d: राया वयं ससवांसो मदेम हव्येन देवा यवसेन गावः । तां धेनुमिन्द्रावरुणा युवं नो विश्वाहा धत्तमनपस्फुरन्तीम् ॥
4.42.e: May we, possessing much, delight in riches, Gods in oblations and the kine in pasture;  And that Milch-cow who shrinks not from the milking, O Indra-Varuṇa, give to us daily.

4.43.d: क उ श्रवत्कतमो यज्ञियानां वन्दारु देवः कतमो जुषाते । कस्येमां देवीममृतेषु प्रेष्ठां हृदि श्रेषाम सुष्टुतिं सुहव्याम् ॥
4.43.e: WHO will hear, who of those who merit worship, which of all Gods take pleasure in our homage?  On whose heart shall we lay this laud celestial, rich with fair offerings, dearest to Immortals?

4.43.d: को मृळाति कतम आगमिष्ठो देवानामु कतमः शम्भविष्ठः । रथं कमाहुर्द्रवदश्वमाशुं यं सूर्यस्य दुहितावृणीत ॥
4.43.e: Who will be gracious? Who will come most quickly of all the Gods? Who will  bring bliss most largely?  What car do they call swift with rapid coursers? That which the Daughter of the Sun elected.

4.43.d: मक्षू हि ष्मा गच्छथ ईवतो द्यूनिन्द्रो न शक्तिं परितक्म्यायाम् । दिव आजाता दिव्या सुपर्णा कया शचीनां भवथः शचिष्ठा ॥
4.43.e: So many days do ye come swiftly hither, as Indra to give help in stress of battle.  Descended from the sky, divine, strong-pinioned, by which of all your powers are ye most mighty?

4.43.d: का वां भूदुपमातिः कया न आश्विना गमथो हूयमाना । को वां महश्चित्त्यजसो अभीक उरुष्यतं माध्वी दस्रा न ऊती ॥
4.43.e: What is the prayer that we should bring you, Aśvins, whereby ye come to us when invocated?  Whether of you confronts e’en great betrayal? Lovers of sweetness, Dasras, help and save us.

4.43.d: उरु वां रथः परि नक्षति द्यामा यत्समुद्रादभि वर्तते वाम् । मध्वा माध्वी मधु वां प्रुषायन्यत्सीं वां पृक्षो भुरजन्त पक्वाः ॥
4.43.e: In the wide space your chariot reacheth heaven, what time it turneth hither from the ocean.  Sweets from your sweet shall drop, lovers of sweetness! These have they dressed for you as dainty viands.

4.43.d: सिन्धुर्ह वां रसया सिञ्चदश्वान्घृणा वयोऽरुषासः परि ग्मन् । तदू षु वामजिरं चेति यानं येन पती भवथः सूर्यायाः ॥
4.43.e: Let Sindhu with his wave bedew your horses: in fiery glow have the red birds come hither.  Observed of all was that your rapid going, whereby ye were the Lords of Sūrya's Daughter.

4.43.d: इहेह यद्वां समना पपृक्षे सेयमस्मे सुमतिर्वाजरत्ना । उरुष्यतं जरितारं युवं ह श्रितः कामो नासत्या युवद्रिक् ॥
4.43.e: Whene’er I gratified you here together, your grace was given us, O ye rich in booty.  Protect, ye Twain, the singer of your praises: to you, Nāsatyas, is my wish directed.

4.44.d: तं वां रथं वयमद्या हुवेम पृथुज्रयमश्विना संगतिं गोः । यः सूर्यां वहति वन्धुरायुर्गिर्वाहसं पुरुतमं वसूयुम् ॥
4.44.e: WE will invoke this day your car, far-spreading, O Aśvins, even the gathering, of the sunlight,—  Car praised in hymns, most ample, rich in treasure, fitted with seats, the car that beareth Sūrya.

4.44.d: युवं श्रियमश्विना देवता तां दिवो नपाता वनथः शचीभिः । युवोर्वपुरभि पृक्षः सचन्ते वहन्ति यत्ककुहासो रथे वाम् ॥
4.44.e: Aśvins, ye gained that glory by your Godhead, ye Sons of Heaven, by your own might and power.  Food followeth close upon your bright appearing when stately horses in your chariot draw you.

4.44.d: को वामद्या करते रातहव्य ऊतये वा सुतपेयाय वार्कैः । ऋतस्य वा वनुषे पूर्व्याय नमो येमानो अश्विना ववर्तत् ॥
4.44.e: Who bringeth you to-day for help with offered oblation, or with hymns to drink the juices?  Who, for the sacrifice's ancient lover, turneth you hither, Aśvins, offering homage?

4.44.d: हिरण्ययेन पुरुभू रथेनेमं यज्ञं नासत्योप यातम् । पिबाथ इन्मधुनः सोम्यस्य दधथो रत्नं विधते जनाय ॥
4.44.e: Borne on your golden car, ye omnipresent! come to this sacrifice of ours, Nāsatyas.  Drink of the pleasant liquor of the Soma give riches to the people who adore you.

4.44.d: आ नो यातं दिवो अच्छा पृथिव्या हिरण्ययेन सुवृता रथेन । मा वामन्ये नि यमन्देवयन्तः सं यद्ददे नाभिः पूर्व्या वाम् ॥
4.44.e: Come hitherward to us from earth, from heaven, borne on your golden chariot rolling lightly.  Suffer not other worshippers to stay you here are ye bound by earlier bonds of friendship.

4.44.d: नू नो रयिं पुरुवीरं बृहन्तं दस्रा मिमाथामुभयेष्वस्मे । नरो यद्वामश्विना स्तोममावन्त्सधस्तुतिमाजमीळ्हासो अग्मन् ॥
4.44.e: Now for us both, mete out, O Wonder-Workers, riches exceeding great with store of heroes,  Because the men have sent you praise, O Aśvins, and Ajamīlhas come to the laudation.

4.44.d: इहेह यद्वां समना पपृक्षे सेयमस्मे सुमतिर्वाजरत्ना । उरुष्यतं जरितारं युवं ह श्रितः कामो नासत्या युवद्रिक् ॥
4.44.e: Whene’er I gratified you here together, your grace was given us, O ye rich in booty.  Protect, ye Twain, the singer of your praises: to you, Nāsatyas, is my wish directed.

4.45.d: एष स्य भानुरुदियर्ति युज्यते रथः परिज्मा दिवो अस्य सानवि । पृक्षासो अस्मिन्मिथुना अधि त्रयो दृतिस्तुरीयो मधुनो वि रप्शते ॥
4.45.e: YONDER goes up that light: your chariot is yoked that travels round upon the summit of this heaven.  Within this car are stored three kindred shares of food, and a skin filled with meath is rustling as the fourth.

4.45.d: उद्वां पृक्षासो मधुमन्त ईरते रथा अश्वास उषसो व्युष्टिषु । अपोर्णुवन्तस्तम आ परीवृतं स्व१र्ण शुक्रं तन्वन्त आ रजः ॥
4.45.e: Forth come your viands rich with store of pleasant meath, and cars and horses at the flushing of the dawn,  Stripping the covering from the surrounded gloom, and spreading through mid-air bright radiance like the Sun.

4.45.d: मध्वः पिबतं मधुपेभिरासभिरुत प्रियं मधुने युञ्जाथां रथम् । आ वर्तनिं मधुना जिन्वथस्पथो दृतिं वहेथे मधुमन्तमश्विना ॥
4.45.e: Drink of the meath with lips accustomed to the draught; harness for the meath's sake the chariot that ye love.  Refresh the way ye go, refresh the paths with meath: hither, O Aśvins, bring the skin that holds the meath.

4.45.d: हंसासो ये वां मधुमन्तो अस्रिधो हिरण्यपर्णा उहुव उषर्बुधः । उदप्रुतो मन्दिनो मन्दिनिस्पृशो मध्वो न मक्षः सवनानि गच्छथः ॥
4.45.e: The swans ye have are friendly, rich in store of meath, gold-pinioned, strong to draw, awake at early morn,  Swimming the flood, exultant, fain for draughts that cheer: ye come like flies to our libations of the meath.

4.45.d: स्वध्वरासो मधुमन्तो अग्नय उस्रा जरन्ते प्रति वस्तोरश्विना । यन्निक्तहस्तस्तरणिर्विचक्षणः सोमं सुषाव मधुमन्तमद्रिभिः ॥
4.45.e: Well knowing solemn rites and rich in meath, the fires sing to the morning Aśvins at the break of day,  When with pure hands the prudent energetic priest hath with the stones pressed out the Soma rich in meath.

4.45.d: आकेनिपासो अहभिर्दविध्वतः स्व१र्ण शुक्रं तन्वन्त आ रजः । सूरश्चिदश्वान्युयुजान ईयते विश्वाँ अनु स्वधया चेतथस्पथः ॥
4.45.e: The rays advancing nigh, chasing with day the gloom, spread through the firmament bright radiance like the Sun;  And the Sun harnessing his horses goeth forth: ye through your Godlike nature let his paths be known.

4.45.d: प्र वामवोचमश्विना धियंधा रथः स्वश्वो अजरो यो अस्ति । येन सद्यः परि रजांसि याथो हविष्मन्तं तरणिं भोजमच्छ ॥
4.45.e: Devout in thought I have declared, O Aśvins, your chariot with good steeds, which lasts for ever,  Wherewith ye travel swiftly through the regions to the prompt worshipper who brings oblation.

4.46.d: अग्रं पिबा मधूनां सुतं वायो दिविष्टिषु । त्वं हि पूर्वपा असि ॥
4.46.e: DRINK the best draught of Soma-juice, O Vāyu, at our holy rites:  For thou art he who drinketh first.

4.46.d: शतेना नो अभिष्टिभिर्नियुत्वाँ इन्द्रसारथिः । वायो सुतस्य तृम्पतम् ॥
4.46.e: Come, team-drawn, with thy hundred helps, with Indra, seated in the car,  Vāyu, and drink your fill of juice.

4.46.d: आ वां सहस्रं हरय इन्द्रवायू अभि प्रयः । वहन्तु सोमपीतये ॥
4.46.e: May steeds a thousand bring you both, Indra. and Vāyu, hitherward  To drink the Soma, to the feast.

4.46.d: रथं हिरण्यवन्धुरमिन्द्रवायू स्वध्वरम् । आ हि स्थाथो दिविस्पृशम् ॥
4.46.e: For ye, O Indra-Vāyu, mount the golden-seated car that aids  The sacrifice, that reaches heaven.

4.46.d: रथेन पृथुपाजसा दाश्वांसमुप गच्छतम् । इन्द्रवायू इहा गतम् ॥
4.46.e: On far-refulgent chariot come unto the man who offers gifts:  Come, Indra-Vāyu, hitherward.

4.46.d: इन्द्रवायू अयं सुतस्तं देवेभिः सजोषसा । पिबतं दाशुषो गृहे ॥
4.46.e: Here, Indra-Vāyu, is the juice: drink it, accordant with the Gods,  Within the giver's dwelling-place.

4.46.d: इह प्रयाणमस्तु वामिन्द्रवायू विमोचनम् । इह वां सोमपीतये ॥
4.46.e: Hither, O Indra-Vāyu, be your journey here unyoke your steeds,  Here for your draught of Soma juice.

4.47.d: वायो शुक्रो अयामि ते मध्वो अग्रं दिविष्टिषु । आ याहि सोमपीतये स्पार्हो देव नियुत्वता ॥
4.47.e: Vāyu, the bright is offered thee, best of the meath at holy rites.  Come thou to drink the Soma juice, God, longed-for, on thy team-drawn car.

4.47.d: इन्द्रश्च वायवेषां सोमानां पीतिमर्हथः । युवां हि यन्तीन्दवो निम्नमापो न सध्र्यक् ॥
4.47.e: O Vāyu, thou and Indra are meet drinkers of these Soma-draughts,  For unto you the drops proceed as waters gather to the vale.

4.47.d: वायविन्द्रश्च शुष्मिणा सरथं शवसस्पती । नियुत्वन्ता न ऊतय आ यातं सोमपीतये ॥
4.47.e: O Indra-Vāyu, mighty Twain, speeding together, Lords of Strength,  Come to our succour with your team, that ye may drink the Soma juice.

4.47.d: या वां सन्ति पुरुस्पृहो नियुतो दाशुषे नरा । अस्मे ता यज्ञवाहसेन्द्रवायू नि यच्छतम् ॥
4.47.e: The longed-for teams which ye possess, O Heroes, for the worshipper,  Turn to us, Indra-Vāyu, ye to whom the sacrifice is paid.

4.48.d: विहि होत्रा अवीता विपो न रायो अर्यः । वायवा चन्द्रेण रथेन याहि सुतस्य पीतये ॥
4.48.e: TASTE offerings never tasted yet, as bards enjoy the foeman's wealth.  O Vāyu, on refulgent car come to the drinking of the juice.

4.48.d: निर्युवाणो अशस्तीर्नियुत्वाँ इन्द्रसारथिः । वायवा चन्द्रेण रथेन याहि सुतस्य पीतये ॥
4.48.e: Removing curses, drawn by teams, with Indra, seated by thy side,  O Vāyu, on refulgent car come to the drinking of the juice.

4.48.d: अनु कृष्णे वसुधिती येमाते विश्वपेशसा । वायवा चन्द्रेण रथेन याहि सुतस्य पीतये ॥
4.48.e: The two dark treasuries of wealth that wear  all beauties wait on thee.  O Vāyu, on refulgent car come to the drinking of the juice.

4.48.d: वहन्तु त्वा मनोयुजो युक्तासो नवतिर्नव । वायवा चन्द्रेण रथेन याहि सुतस्य पीतये ॥
4.48.e: May nine-and-ninety harnessed steeds who yoke them at thy will bring thee.  O Vāyu, on refulgent car come to the drinking of the juice.

4.48.d: वायो शतं हरीणां युवस्व पोष्याणाम् । उत वा ते सहस्रिणो रथ आ यातु पाजसा ॥
4.48.e: Harness, O Vāyu, to thy car a hundred well-fed tawny steeds,  Yea, or a thousand steeds, and let thy chariot come to us with might.

4.49.d: इदं वामास्ये हविः प्रियमिन्द्राबृहस्पती । उक्थं मदश्च शस्यते ॥
4.49.e: DEAR is this offering in your mouth, O Indra and Bṛhaspati:  Famed is the laud, the gladdening draught.

4.49.d: अयं वां परि षिच्यते सोम इन्द्राबृहस्पती । चारुर्मदाय पीतये ॥
4.49.e: This lovely Soma is effused, O Indra and Bṛhaspati,  For you, to drink it and rejoice.

4.49.d: आ न इन्द्राबृहस्पती गृहमिन्द्रश्च गच्छतम् । सोमपा सोमपीतये ॥
4.49.e: As Soma-drinkers to our house come, Indra and Bṛhaspati-and Indra-to drink Soma juice.

4.49.d: अस्मे इन्द्राबृहस्पती रयिं धत्तं शतग्विनम् । अश्वावन्तं सहस्रिणम् ॥
4.49.e: Vouchsafe us riches hundredfold, O Indra, and Bṛhaspati,  With store of horses, thousandfold.

4.49.d: इन्द्राबृहस्पती वयं सुते गीर्भिर्हवामहे । अस्य सोमस्य पीतये ॥
4.49.e: O Indra. and Bṛhaspati, we call you when the meath is shed,  With songs, to drink the Soma juice.

4.49.d: सोममिन्द्राबृहस्पती पिबतं दाशुषो गृहे । मादयेथां तदोकसा ॥
4.49.e: Drink, Indra and Bṛhaspati, the Soma in the giver's house:  Delight yourselves abiding there.

4.50.d: यस्तस्तम्भ सहसा वि ज्मो अन्तान्बृहस्पतिस्त्रिषधस्थो रवेण । तं प्रत्नास ऋषयो दीध्यानाः पुरो विप्रा दधिरे मन्द्रजिह्वम् ॥
4.50.e: Him who with might hath propped earth's ends, who sitteth in threefold seat, Bṛhaspati, with thunder,  Him of the pleasant tongue have ancient sages, deep-thinking, holy singers, set before them.

4.50.d: धुनेतयः सुप्रकेतं मदन्तो बृहस्पते अभि ये नस्ततस्रे । पृषन्तं सृप्रमदब्धमूर्वं बृहस्पते रक्षतादस्य योनिम् ॥
4.50.e: Wild in their course, in well-marked wise rejoicing were they, Bṛhaspati, who pressed around us.  Preserve Bṛhaspati, the stall uninjured, this company's raining, ever-moving birthplace.

4.50.d: बृहस्पते या परमा परावदत आ त ऋतस्पृशो नि षेदुः । तुभ्यं खाता अवता अद्रिदुग्धा मध्वः श्चोतन्त्यभितो विरप्शम् ॥
4.50.e: Bṛhaspati, from thy remotest distance have they sat down who love the law eternal.  For thee were dug wells springing from the mountain, which murmuring round about pour streams of sweetness.

4.50.d: बृहस्पतिः प्रथमं जायमानो महो ज्योतिषः परमे व्योमन् । सप्तास्यस्तुविजातो रवेण वि सप्तरश्मिरधमत्तमांसि ॥
4.50.e: Bṛhaspati, when first he had his being from mighty splendour in supremest heaven,  Strong, with his sevenfold mouth, with noise of thunder, with his seven rays, blew and dispersed the darkness.

4.50.d: स सुष्टुभा स ऋक्वता गणेन वलं रुरोज फलिगं रवेण । बृहस्पतिरुस्रिया हव्यसूदः कनिक्रदद्वावशतीरुदाजत् ॥
4.50.e: With the loud-shouting band who sang his praises, with thunder, he destroyed obstructive Vala.  Bṛhaspati thundering drave forth the cattle, the lowing cows who make oblations ready.

4.50.d: एवा पित्रे विश्वदेवाय वृष्णे यज्ञैर्विधेम नमसा हविर्भिः । बृहस्पते सुप्रजा वीरवन्तो वयं स्याम पतयो रयीणाम् ॥
4.50.e: Serve we with sacrifices, gifts, and homage even thus the Steer of all the Gods, the Father.  Bṛhaspati, may we be lords of riches, with noble progeny and store of heroes.

4.50.d: स इद्राजा प्रतिजन्यानि विश्वा शुष्मेण तस्थावभि वीर्येण । बृहस्पतिं यः सुभृतं बिभर्ति वल्गूयति वन्दते पूर्वभाजम् ॥
4.50.e: Surely that King by power and might heroic hath made him lord of all his foes' posses-ions,  Who cherishes Bṛhaspati well-tended, adorns and worships him as foremost sharer.

4.50.d: स इत्क्षेति सुधित ओकसि स्वे तस्मा इळा पिन्वते विश्वदानीम् । तस्मै विशः स्वयमेवा नमन्ते यस्मिन्ब्रह्मा राजनि पूर्व एति ॥
4.50.e: In his own house he dwells in peace and comfort: to him for ever holy food flows richly.  To him the people with free will pay homage-the King with whom the Brahman hath precedence.

4.50.d: अप्रतीतो जयति सं धनानि प्रतिजन्यान्युत या सजन्या । अवस्यवे यो वरिवः कृणोति ब्रह्मणे राजा तमवन्ति देवाः ॥
4.50.e: He, unopposed, is master of the riches of his own subjects and of hostile people.  The Gods uphold that King with their protection who helps the Brahman when he seeks his favour.

4.50.d: इन्द्रश्च सोमं पिबतं बृहस्पतेऽस्मिन्यज्ञे मन्दसाना वृषण्वसू । आ वां विशन्त्विन्दवः स्वाभुवोऽस्मे रयिं सर्ववीरं नि यच्छतम् ॥
4.50.e: Indra, Bṛhaspati, rainers of treasure, rejoicing at this sacrifice drink the Soma.  Let the abundant drops sink deep within you: vouchsafe us riches with full store of heroes.

4.50.d: बृहस्पत इन्द्र वर्धतं नः सचा सा वां सुमतिर्भूत्वस्मे । अविष्टं धियो जिगृतं पुरंधीर्जजस्तमर्यो वनुषामरातीः ॥
4.50.e: Bṛhaspati and Indra, make us prosper may this be your benevolence to us-ward.  Assist our holy thoughts, wake up our spirit: weaken the hatred of our foe and rivals.

4.51.d: इदमु त्यत्पुरुतमं पुरस्ताज्ज्योतिस्तमसो वयुनावदस्थात् । नूनं दिवो दुहितरो विभातीर्गातुं कृणवन्नुषसो जनाय ॥
4.51.e: FORTH from the darkness in the region eastward this most abundant splendid light hatb mounted.  Now verily the far-refulgent Mornings, Daughters of Heaven, bring welfare to the people.

4.51.d: अस्थुरु चित्रा उषसः पुरस्तान्मिता इव स्वरवोऽध्वरेषु । व्यू व्रजस्य तमसो द्वारोच्छन्तीरव्रञ्छुचयः पावकाः ॥
4.51.e: The richly-coloured Dawns have mounted eastward, like pillars planted at our sacrifices,  And, flushing far, splendid and purifying, unbarred the portals of the fold of darkness.

4.51.d: उच्छन्तीरद्य चितयन्त भोजान्राधोदेयायोषसो मघोनीः । अचित्रे अन्तः पणयः ससन्त्वबुध्यमानास्तमसो विमध्ये ॥
4.51.e: Dispelling gloom this day the wealthy Mornings urge liberal givers to present their treasures.  In the unlightened depth of darkness round them let niggard traffickers sleep unawakened.

4.51.d: कुवित्स देवीः सनयो नवो वा यामो बभूयादुषसो वो अद्य । येना नवग्वे अङ्गिरे दशग्वे सप्तास्ये रेवती रेवदूष ॥
4.51.e: O Goddesses, is this your car, I ask you, ancient this day, or is it new, ye Mornings,  Wherewith, rich Dawns, ye seek with wealth Navagva, Daśagva Aṅgira, the seven-toned singer?

4.51.d: यूयं हि देवीर्ऋतयुग्भिरश्वैः परिप्रयाथ भुवनानि सद्यः । प्रबोधयन्तीरुषसः ससन्तं द्विपाच्चतुष्पाच्चरथाय जीवम् ॥
4.51.e: With horses harnessed by eternal Order, Goddesses, swiftly round the worlds ye travel,  Arousing from their rest, O Dawns, the sleeping, and all that lives, man, bird, and beast, to motion.

4.51.d: क्व स्विदासां कतमा पुराणी यया विधाना विदधुर्ऋभूणाम् । शुभं यच्छुभ्रा उषसश्चरन्ति न वि ज्ञायन्ते सदृशीरजुर्याः ॥
4.51.e: Which among these is eldest, and where is she through whom they fixed the Ṛbhus' regulations?  What time the splendid Dawns go forth for splendour, they are not known apart, alike, unwasting.

4.51.d: ता घा ता भद्रा उषसः पुरासुरभिष्टिद्युम्ना ऋतजातसत्याः । यास्वीजानः शशमान उक्थैः स्तुवञ्छंसन्द्रविणं सद्य आप ॥
4.51.e: Blest were these Dawns of old, shining with succour, true with the truth that springs from holy Order;  With whom the toiling worshipper, by praises, hymning and lauding, soon attained to riches.

4.51.d: ता आ चरन्ति समना पुरस्तात्समानतः समना पप्रथानाः । ऋतस्य देवीः सदसो बुधाना गवां न सर्गा उषसो जरन्ते ॥
4.51.e: Hither from eastward all at once they travel, from one place spreading in the selfsame manner.  Awaking, from the seat of holy Order the Godlike Dawns come nigh like troops of cattle.

4.51.d: ता इन्न्वे३व समना समानीरमीतवर्णा उषसश्चरन्ति । गूहन्तीरभ्वमसितं रुशद्भिः शुक्रास्तनूभिः शुचयो रुचानाः ॥
4.51.e: Thus they go forth with undiminished colours, these Mornings similar, in self-same fashion,  Concealing the gigantic might of darkness with radiant bodies bright and pure and shining.

4.51.d: रयिं दिवो दुहितरो विभातीः प्रजावन्तं यच्छतास्मासु देवीः । स्योनादा वः प्रतिबुध्यमानाः सुवीर्यस्य पतयः स्याम ॥
4.51.e: O Goddesses, O Heaven's refulgent Daughters, bestow upon us wealth with store of children.  As from our pleasant place of rest ye rouse us may we be masters of heroic vigour.

4.51.d: तद्वो दिवो दुहितरो विभातीरुप ब्रुव उषसो यज्ञकेतुः । वयं स्याम यशसो जनेषु तद्द्यौश्च धत्तां पृथिवी च देवी ॥
4.51.e: Well-skilled in lore of sacrifice, ye Daughters of Heaven, refulgent Dawns, I thus address you.  May we be glorious among the people. May Heaven vouchsafe us this, and Earth the Goddess,

4.52.d: प्रति ष्या सूनरी जनी व्युच्छन्ती परि स्वसुः । दिवो अदर्शि दुहिता ॥
4.52.e: THIS Lady, giver of delight, after her Sister shining forth, Daughter of Heaven, hath shown herself.-
Unfailing, Mother of the Kine, in colour like a bright red mare,  The Dawn became the Aśvins' Friend.

4.52.d: उत सखास्यश्विनोरुत माता गवामसि । उतोषो वस्व ईशिषे ॥
4.52.e: Yea, and thou art the Aśvins' Friend, the Mother of the Kine art thou:  O Dawn thou rulest over wealth.
Thinking of thee, O joyous One, as her who driveth hate away,  We woke to meet thee with our lauds.

4.52.d: प्रति भद्रा अदृक्षत गवां सर्गा न रश्मयः । ओषा अप्रा उरु ज्रयः ॥
4.52.e: Our eyes behold thy blessed rays like troops of cattle loosed to feed.  Dawn hath filled full the wide expanse.

4.52.d: आपप्रुषी विभावरि व्यावर्ज्योतिषा तमः । उषो अनु स्वधामव ॥
4.52.e: When thou hast filled it, Fulgent One! thou layest bare the gloom with light.  After thy nature aid us, Dawn.

4.52.d: आ द्यां तनोषि रश्मिभिरान्तरिक्षमुरु प्रियम् । उषः शुक्रेण शोचिषा ॥
4.52.e: Thou overspreadest heaven with rays, the dear wide region of mid-air.  With thy bright shining lustre, Dawn.

4.53.d: तद्देवस्य सवितुर्वार्यं महद्वृणीमहे असुरस्य प्रचेतसः । छर्दिर्येन दाशुषे यच्छति त्मना तन्नो महाँ उदयान्देवो अक्तुभिः ॥
4.53.e: OF Savitar the God, the sapient Asura, we crave this great gift which is worthy of our choice,  Wherewith he freely grants his worshiper defence. This with his rays the Great God hath vouchsafed to us.

4.53.d: दिवो धर्ता भुवनस्य प्रजापतिः पिशङ्गं द्रापिं प्रति मुञ्चते कविः । विचक्षणः प्रथयन्नापृणन्नुर्वजीजनत्सविता सुम्नमुक्थ्यम् ॥
4.53.e: Sustainer of the heaven, Lord of the whole world's life, the Sage, he putteth on his golden-coloured mail.  Clear-sighted, spreading far, filling the spacious realm, Savitar hath brought forth bliss that deserveth laud.

4.53.d: आप्रा रजांसि दिव्यानि पार्थिवा श्लोकं देवः कृणुते स्वाय धर्मणे । प्र बाहू अस्राक्सविता सवीमनि निवेशयन्प्रसुवन्नक्तुभिर्जगत् ॥
4.53.e: He hath filled full the regions of the heaven and earth: the God for his own strengthening waketh up the hymn.  Savitar hath stretched out his arms to cherish life, producing with his rays and lulling all that moves.

4.53.d: अदाभ्यो भुवनानि प्रचाकशद्व्रतानि देवः सविताभि रक्षते । प्रास्राग्बाहू भुवनस्य प्रजाभ्यो धृतव्रतो महो अज्मस्य राजति ॥
4.53.e: Lighting all living creatures, ne’er to be deceived, Savitar, God, protects each holy ordinance.  He hath stretched out his arms to all the folk of earth, and, with his laws observed, rules his own mighty course.

4.53.d: त्रिरन्तरिक्षं सविता महित्वना त्री रजांसि परिभुस्त्रीणि रोचना । तिस्रो दिवः पृथिवीस्तिस्र इन्वति त्रिभिर्व्रतैरभि नो रक्षति त्मना ॥
4.53.e: Savitar thrice surrounding with his mightiness mid-air, three regions, and the triple sphere of light,  Sets the three heavens in motion and the threefold earth, and willingly protects us with his triple law.

4.53.d: बृहत्सुम्नः प्रसवीता निवेशनो जगतः स्थातुरुभयस्य यो वशी । स नो देवः सविता शर्म यच्छत्वस्मे क्षयाय त्रिवरूथमंहसः ॥
4.53.e: Most gracious God, who brings to life and lulls to rest, he who controls the world, what moves not and what moves,  May he vouchsafe us shelter,—Savitar the God,—for tranquil life, with triple bar against distress.

4.53.d: आगन्देव ऋतुभिर्वर्धतु क्षयं दधातु नः सविता सुप्रजामिषम् । स नः क्षपाभिरहभिश्च जिन्वतु प्रजावन्तं रयिमस्मे समिन्वतु ॥
4.53.e: With the year's seasons hath Savitar, God, come nigh: may he prosper our home, give food and noble sons.  May he invigorate us through the days and nights, and may he send us opulence with progeny.

4.54.d: अभूद्देवः सविता वन्द्यो नु न इदानीमह्न उपवाच्यो नृभिः । वि यो रत्ना भजति मानवेभ्यः श्रेष्ठं नो अत्र द्रविणं यथा दधत् ॥
4.54.e: Now must we praise and honour Savitar the God: at this time of the day the men must call to him,  Him who distributes wealth to Manu's progeny, that he may grant us here riches most excellent.

4.54.d: देवेभ्यो हि प्रथमं यज्ञियेभ्योऽमृतत्वं सुवसि भागमुत्तमम् । आदिद्दामानं सवितर्व्यूर्णुषेऽनूचीना जीविता मानुषेभ्यः ॥
4.54.e: For thou at first producest for the holy Gods the noblest of all portions, immortality:  Thereafter as a gift to men, O Savitar, thou openest existence, life succeeding life.

4.54.d: अचित्ती यच्चकृमा दैव्ये जने दीनैर्दक्षैः प्रभूती पूरुषत्वता । देवेषु च सवितर्मानुषेषु च त्वं नो अत्र सुवतादनागसः ॥
4.54.e: If we, men as we are, have sinned against the Gods through want of thought, in weakness, or through insolence,  Absolve us from the guilt and make us free from sin, O Savitar, alike among both Gods and men.

4.54.d: न प्रमिये सवितुर्दैव्यस्य तद्यथा विश्वं भुवनं धारयिष्यति । यत्पृथिव्या वरिमन्ना स्वङ्गुरिर्वर्ष्मन्दिवः सुवति सत्यमस्य तत् ॥
4.54.e: None may impede that power of Savitar the God whereby he will maintain the universal world.  What the fair-fingered God brings forth on earth's expanse or in the height of heaven, that work of his stands sure.

4.54.d: इन्द्रज्येष्ठान्बृहद्भ्यः पर्वतेभ्यः क्षयाँ एभ्यः सुवसि पस्त्यावतः । यथायथा पतयन्तो वियेमिर एवैव तस्थुः सवितः सवाय ते ॥
4.54.e: To lofty hills thou sendest those whom Indra leads, and givest fixed abodes with houses unto these.  However they may fly and draw themselves apart, still, Savitar, they stand obeying thy behest.

4.54.d: ये ते त्रिरहन्त्सवितः सवासो दिवेदिवे सौभगमासुवन्ति । इन्द्रो द्यावापृथिवी सिन्धुरद्भिरादित्यैर्नो अदितिः शर्म यंसत् ॥
4.54.e: May the libations poured to thee thrice daily, day after day, O Savitar, bring us blessing.  May Indra, Heaven, Earth, Sindhu with the Waters, Aditi with Ādityas, give us shelter.

4.55.d: को वस्त्राता वसवः को वरूता द्यावाभूमी अदिते त्रासीथां नः । सहीयसो वरुण मित्र मर्तात्को वोऽध्वरे वरिवो धाति देवाः ॥
4.55.e: WHO of you, Vasus, saveth? who protecteth? O Heaven and Earth and Aditi, preserve us,  Varuṇa., Mitra, from the stronger mortal. Gods, which of you at sacrifice giveth comfort?

4.55.d: प्र ये धामानि पूर्व्याण्यर्चान्वि यदुच्छान्वियोतारो अमूराः । विधातारो वि ते दधुरजस्रा ऋतधीतयो रुरुचन्त दस्माः ॥
4.55.e: They who with laud extol the ancient statutes, when they shine forth infallible dividers,  Have ordered as perpetual Ordainers, and beamed as holy-thoughted Wonder-Workers.

4.55.d: प्र पस्त्या३मदितिं सिन्धुमर्कैः स्वस्तिमीळे सख्याय देवीम् । उभे यथा नो अहनी निपात उषासानक्ता करतामदब्धे ॥
4.55.e: The Housewife Goddess, Aditi, and Sindhu, the Goddess Svasti I implore for friendship:  And may the unobstructed Night and Morning both, day and night, provide for our protection.

4.55.d: व्यर्यमा वरुणश्चेति पन्थामिषस्पतिः सुवितं गातुमग्निः । इन्द्राविष्णू नृवदु षु स्तवाना शर्म नो यन्तममवद्वरूथम् ॥
4.55.e: Aryaman, Varuṇa have disclosed the pathway, Agni as Lord of Strength the road to welfare.  Lauded in manly mode may Indra-Viṣṇu grant us their powerful defence and shelter.

4.55.d: आ पर्वतस्य मरुतामवांसि देवस्य त्रातुरव्रि भगस्य । पात्पतिर्जन्यादंहसो नो मित्रो मित्रियादुत न उरुष्येत् ॥
4.55.e: I have besought the favour of the Maruts, of Parvata, of Bhaga God who rescues.  From trouble caused by man the Lord preserve us; from woe sent by his friend let Mitra save us.

4.55.d: नू रोदसी अहिना बुध्न्येन स्तुवीत देवी अप्येभिरिष्टैः । समुद्रं न संचरणे सनिष्यवो घर्मस्वरसो नद्यो३ अप व्रन् ॥
4.55.e: Agree, through these our watery oblations, Goddesses, Heaven and Earth, with Ahibudhnya.  As if to win the sea, the Gharma-heaters have opened, as they come anear, the rivers.

4.55.d: देवैर्नो देव्यदितिर्नि पातु देवस्त्राता त्रायतामप्रयुच्छन् । नहि मित्रस्य वरुणस्य धासिमर्हामसि प्रमियं सान्वग्नेः ॥
4.55.e: May Goddess Aditi with Gods defend us, save us the saviour God with care unceasing.  We dare not stint the sacred food of Mitra and Varuṇa upon the back of Agni.
Agni is Sovran Lord of wealth, Agni of great prosperity:  May he bestow these gifts on us.

4.55.d: उषो मघोन्या वह सूनृते वार्या पुरु । अस्मभ्यं वाजिनीवति ॥
4.55.e: Hither to us, rich pleasant Dawn, bring many things to be desired,  Thou who hast ample store of wealth.

4.55.d: तत्सु नः सविता भगो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा । इन्द्रो नो राधसा गमत् ॥
4.55.e: So then may Bhaga, Savitar, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Indra, with bounty come to us.

4.56.d: मही द्यावापृथिवी इह ज्येष्ठे रुचा भवतां शुचयद्भिरर्कैः । यत्सीं वरिष्ठे बृहती विमिन्वन्रुवद्धोक्षा पप्रथानेभिरेवैः ॥
4.56.e: MAY mighty Heaven and Earth, most meet for honour, be present here with light and gleaming splendours;  When, fixing them apart, vast, most extensive, the Steer roars loudly in far-reaching courses.

4.56.d: देवी देवेभिर्यजते यजत्रैरमिनती तस्थतुरुक्षमाणे । ऋतावरी अद्रुहा देवपुत्रे यज्ञस्य नेत्री शुचयद्भिरर्कैः ॥
4.56.e: The Goddesses with Gods, holy with holy, the Two stand pouring out their rain, exhaustless:  Faithful and guileless, having Gods for children, leaders of sacrifice with shining splendours.

4.56.d: स इत्स्वपा भुवनेष्वास य इमे द्यावापृथिवी जजान । उर्वी गभीरे रजसी सुमेके अवंशे धीरः शच्या समैरत् ॥
4.56.e: Sure in the worlds he was a skilful Craftsman, he who produced these Twain the Earth and Heaven.  Wise, with his power he brought both realms, together spacious and deep, well-fashioned, unsupported.

4.56.d: नू रोदसी बृहद्भिर्नो वरूथैः पत्नीवद्भिरिषयन्ती सजोषाः । उरूची विश्वे यजते नि पातं धिया स्याम रथ्यः सदासाः ॥
4.56.e: O Heaven and Earth, with one accord promoting, with high protection as of Queens, our welfare,  Far-reaching, universal, holy, guard us. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

4.56.d: प्र वां महि द्यवी अभ्युपस्तुतिं भरामहे । शुची उप प्रशस्तये ॥
4.56.e: To both of you, O Heaven and Earth, we bring our lofty song of praise,  Pure Ones! to glorify you both.

4.56.d: पुनाने तन्वा मिथः स्वेन दक्षेण राजथः । ऊह्याथे सनादृतम् ॥
4.56.e: Ye sanctify each other's form, by your own proper might ye rule,  And from of old observe the Law.

4.56.d: मही मित्रस्य साधथस्तरन्ती पिप्रती ऋतम् । परि यज्ञं नि षेदथुः ॥
4.56.e: Furthering and fulfilling, ye, O Mighty, perfect Mitra's Law.  Ye sit around our sacrifice.

4.57.d: क्षेत्रस्य पतिना वयं हितेनेव जयामसि । गामश्वं पोषयित्न्वा स नो मृळातीदृशे ॥
4.57.e: WE through the Master of the Field, even as through a friend, obtain  What nourisheth our kine and steeds. In such may he be good to us.

4.57.d: क्षेत्रस्य पते मधुमन्तमूर्मिं धेनुरिव पयो अस्मासु धुक्ष्व । मधुश्चुतं घृतमिव सुपूतमृतस्य नः पतयो मृळयन्तु ॥
