4.57.e: As the cow yieldeth milk, pour for us freely, Lord of the Field, the wave that beareth sweetness,  Distilling meath, well-purified like butter, and let the. Lords of holy Law be gracious.

4.57.d: मधुमतीरोषधीर्द्याव आपो मधुमन्नो भवत्वन्तरिक्षम् । क्षेत्रस्य पतिर्मधुमान्नो अस्त्वरिष्यन्तो अन्वेनं चरेम ॥
4.57.e: Sweet be the plants for us. the heavens, the waters, and full of sweets for us be air's mid-region.  May the Field's Lord for us be full of sweetness, and may we follow after him uninjured.

4.57.d: शुनं वाहाः शुनं नरः शुनं कृषतु लाङ्गलम् । शुनं वरत्रा बध्यन्तां शुनमष्ट्रामुदिङ्गय ॥
4.57.e: Happily work our steers and men, may the plough furrow happily.  Happily be the traces bound; happily may he ply the goad.

4.57.d: शुनासीराविमां वाचं जुषेथां यद्दिवि चक्रथुः पयः । तेनेमामुप सिञ्चतम् ॥
4.57.e: Śuna and Sīra, welcome ye this laud, and with the milk which ye have made in heaven  Bedew ye both this earth of ours.

4.57.d: अर्वाची सुभगे भव सीते वन्दामहे त्वा । यथा नः सुभगाससि यथा नः सुफलाससि ॥
4.57.e: Auspicious Sītā, come thou near: we venerate and worship thee  That thou mayst bless and prosper us and bring us fruits abundantly.

4.57.d: इन्द्रः सीतां नि गृह्णातु तां पूषानु यच्छतु । सा नः पयस्वती दुहामुत्तरामुत्तरां समाम् ॥
4.57.e: May Indra press the furrow down, may Pūṣan guide its course aright.  May she, as rich in milk, be drained for us through each succeeding year.

4.57.d: शुनं नः फाला वि कृषन्तु भूमिं शुनं कीनाशा अभि यन्तु वाहैः । शुनं पर्जन्यो मधुना पयोभिः शुनासीरा शुनमस्मासु धत्तम् ॥
4.57.e: Happily let the shares turn up the plough-land, happily go the ploughers with the oxen.  With meath and milk Parjanya make us happy. Grant us prosperity, Śuna and Sīra.

4.58.d: समुद्रादूर्मिर्मधुमाँ उदारदुपांशुना सममृतत्वमानट् । घृतस्य नाम गुह्यं यदस्ति जिह्वा देवानाममृतस्य नाभिः ॥
4.58.e: FORTH from the ocean sprang the wave of sweetness: together with the stalk it turned to Amṛta,  That which is holy oil's mysterious title: but the Gods’ tongue is truly Amṛta's centre.

4.58.d: वयं नाम प्र ब्रवामा घृतस्यास्मिन्यज्ञे धारयामा नमोभिः । उप ब्रह्मा शृणवच्छस्यमानं चतुःशृङ्गोऽवमीद्गौर एतत् ॥
4.58.e: Let us declare aloud the name of Ghṛta, and at this sacrifice hold it up with homage.  So let the Brahman hear the praise we utter. This hath the four-horned Buffalo emitted.

4.58.d: चत्वारि शृङ्गा त्रयो अस्य पादा द्वे शीर्षे सप्त हस्तासो अस्य । त्रिधा बद्धो वृषभो रोरवीति महो देवो मर्त्याँ आ विवेश ॥
4.58.e: Four are his horns, three are the feet that bear him; his heads are two, his hands are seven in number.  Bound with a triple bond the Steer roars loudly: the mighty God hath entered in to mortals.

4.58.d: त्रिधा हितं पणिभिर्गुह्यमानं गवि देवासो घृतमन्वविन्दन् । इन्द्र एकं सूर्य एकं जजान वेनादेकं स्वधया निष्टतक्षुः ॥
4.58.e: That oil in triple shape the Gods discovered laid down within the Cow, concealed by Paṇis.  Indra produced one shape, Sūrya another: by their own power they formed the third from Vena.

4.58.d: एता अर्षन्ति हृद्यात्समुद्राच्छतव्रजा रिपुणा नावचक्षे । घृतस्य धारा अभि चाकशीमि हिरण्ययो वेतसो मध्य आसाम् ॥
4.58.e: From inmost reservoir in countless channels flow down these rivers which the foe beholds not.  I look upon the streams of oil descending, and lo! the Golden Reed is there among them.

4.58.d: सम्यक्स्रवन्ति सरितो न धेना अन्तर्हृदा मनसा पूयमानाः । एते अर्षन्त्यूर्मयो घृतस्य मृगा इव क्षिपणोरीषमाणाः ॥
4.58.e: Like rivers our libations flow together, cleansing themselves in inmost heart and spirit.  The streams of holy oil pour swiftly downward like the wild beasts that fly before the bowman.

4.58.d: सिन्धोरिव प्राध्वने शूघनासो वातप्रमियः पतयन्ति यह्वाः । घृतस्य धारा अरुषो न वाजी काष्ठा भिन्दन्नूर्मिभिः पिन्वमानः ॥
4.58.e: As rushing down the rapids of a river, flow swifter than the wind the vigorous currents,  The streams of oil in swelling fluctuation like a red courser bursting through the fences.

4.58.d: अभि प्रवन्त समनेव योषाः कल्याण्य१ः स्मयमानासो अग्निम् । घृतस्य धाराः समिधो नसन्त ता जुषाणो हर्यति जातवेदाः ॥
4.58.e: Like women at a gathering fair to look on and gently smiling, they incline to Agni.  The streams of holy oil attain the fuel, and Jātavedas joyfully receives them.

4.58.d: कन्या इव वहतुमेतवा उ अञ्ज्यञ्जाना अभि चाकशीमि । यत्र सोमः सूयते यत्र यज्ञो घृतस्य धारा अभि तत्पवन्ते ॥
4.58.e: As maidens dock themselves with gay adornment to join the bridal feast, I now behold them.  Where Soma flows and sacrifice is ready, thither the streams of holy oil are running.

4.58.d: अभ्यर्षत सुष्टुतिं गव्यमाजिमस्मासु भद्रा द्रविणानि धत्त । इमं यज्ञं नयत देवता नो घृतस्य धारा मधुमत्पवन्ते ॥
4.58.e: Send to our eulogy a herd of cattle bestow upon us excellent possessions.  Bear to the Gods the sacrifice we offer the streams of oil flow pure and full of sweetness.

4.58.d: धामन्ते विश्वं भुवनमधि श्रितमन्तः समुद्रे हृद्य१न्तरायुषि । अपामनीके समिथे य आभृतस्तमश्याम मधुमन्तं त ऊर्मिम् ॥
4.58.e: The universe depends upon thy power and might within the sea, within the heart, within all life. May we attain that sweetly-flavoured wave of thine, brought, at its gathering, o'er the surfaceof the floods.

5.1.d: अबोध्यग्निः समिधा जनानां प्रति धेनुमिवायतीमुषासम् । यह्वा इव प्र वयामुज्जिहानाः प्र भानवः सिस्रते नाकमच्छ ॥
5.1.e: Agni is wakened by the people's fuel to meet the Dawn who cometh like a milch-cow.  Like young trees shooting up on high their branches, his flames are rising to the vault of heaven.

5.1.d: अबोधि होता यजथाय देवानूर्ध्वो अग्निः सुमनाः प्रातरस्थात् । समिद्धस्य रुशददर्शि पाजो महान्देवस्तमसो निरमोचि ॥
5.1.e: For worship of the Gods the Priest was wakened: at morning gracious Agni hath arisen.  Kindled, his radiant might is made apparent, and the great Deity set free from darkness.

5.1.d: यदीं गणस्य रशनामजीगः शुचिरङ्क्ते शुचिभिर्गोभिरग्निः । आद्दक्षिणा युज्यते वाजयन्त्युत्तानामूर्ध्वो अधयज्जुहूभिः ॥
5.1.e: When he hath stirred the line of his attendants, with the pure milk pure Agni is anointed.  The strength-bestowing gift is then made ready, which spread in front, with tongues, erect, he drinketh.

5.1.d: अग्निमच्छा देवयतां मनांसि चक्षूंषीव सूर्ये सं चरन्ति । यदीं सुवाते उषसा विरूपे श्वेतो वाजी जायते अग्रे अह्नाम् ॥
5.1.e: The spirits of the pious turn together to Agni, as the eyes of all to Sūrya.  He, when both Dawns of different hues have borne him, springs up at daybreak as a strong white charger.

5.1.d: जनिष्ट हि जेन्यो अग्रे अह्नां हितो हितेष्वरुषो वनेषु । दमेदमे सप्त रत्ना दधानोऽग्निर्होता नि षसादा यजीयान् ॥
5.1.e: The noble One was born at days' beginning, laid red in colour mid the well-laid fuel.  Yielding in every house his seven rich treasures, Agni is seated, Priest most skilled in worship.

5.1.d: अग्निर्होता न्यसीदद्यजीयानुपस्थे मातुः सुरभा उ लोके । युवा कविः पुरुनिष्ठ ऋतावा धर्ता कृष्टीनामुत मध्य इद्धः ॥
5.1.e: Agni hath sat him down, a Priest most skilful, on a sweet-smelling place, his Mother's bosom.  Young, faithful, sage, preeminent o’er many, kindled among the folk whom he sustaineth.

5.1.d: प्र णु त्यं विप्रमध्वरेषु साधुमग्निं होतारमीळते नमोभिः । आ यस्ततान रोदसी ऋतेन नित्यं मृजन्ति वाजिनं घृतेन ॥
5.1.e: This Singer excellent at sacrifices, Agni the Priest, they glorify with homage.  Him who spread out both worlds by Law Eternal they balm with oil, strong Steed who never faileth.

5.1.d: मार्जाल्यो मृज्यते स्वे दमूनाः कविप्रशस्तो अतिथिः शिवो नः । सहस्रशृङ्गो वृषभस्तदोजा विश्वाँ अग्ने सहसा प्रास्यन्यान् ॥
5.1.e: He, worshipful House-Friend, in his home is worshipped, our own auspicious guest, lauded by sages.  That strength the Bull with thousand horns possesses. In might, O Agni, thou excellest others.

5.1.d: प्र सद्यो अग्ने अत्येष्यन्यानाविर्यस्मै चारुतमो बभूथ । ईळेन्यो वपुष्यो विभावा प्रियो विशामतिथिर्मानुषीणाम् ॥
5.1.e: Thou quickly passest by all others, Agni, for him to whom thou hast appeared most lovely,  Wondrously fair, adorable, effulgent, the guest of men, the darling of the people.

5.1.d: तुभ्यं भरन्ति क्षितयो यविष्ठ बलिमग्ने अन्तित ओत दूरात् । आ भन्दिष्ठस्य सुमतिं चिकिद्धि बृहत्ते अग्ने महि शर्म भद्रम् ॥
5.1.e: To thee, Most Youthful God! to thee, O Agni from near and far the people bring their tribute.  Mark well the prayer of him who best extols thee. Great, high, auspicious, Agni, is thy shelter.

5.1.d: आद्य रथं भानुमो भानुमन्तमग्ने तिष्ठ यजतेभिः समन्तम् । विद्वान्पथीनामुर्व१न्तरिक्षमेह देवान्हविरद्याय वक्षि ॥
5.1.e: Ascend to-day thy splendid car, O Agni, in splendour, with the Holy Ones around it.  Knowing the paths by mid-air's spacious region bring hither Gods to feast on our oblation.

5.1.d: अवोचाम कवये मेध्याय वचो वन्दारु वृषभाय वृष्णे । गविष्ठिरो नमसा स्तोममग्नौ दिवीव रुक्ममुरुव्यञ्चमश्रेत् ॥
5.1.e: To him adorable, sage, strong and mighty we have sung forth our song of praise and homage.  Gavisthira hath raised with prayer to Agni this laud far-reaching, like gold light to heaven.

5.2.d: कुमारं माता युवतिः समुब्धं गुहा बिभर्ति न ददाति पित्रे । अनीकमस्य न मिनज्जनासः पुरः पश्यन्ति निहितमरतौ ॥
5.2.e: THE youthful Mother keeps the Boy in secret pressed to her close, nor yields him to the Father.  But, when he lies upon the arm, the people see his unfading countenance before them.

5.2.d: कमेतं त्वं युवते कुमारं पेषी बिभर्षि महिषी जजान । पूर्वीर्हि गर्भः शरदो ववर्धापश्यं जातं यदसूत माता ॥
5.2.e: What child is this thou carriest as handmaid, O Youthful One? The Consort-Queen hath borne him.  The Babe unborn increased through many autumns. I saw him born what time his Mother bare him.

5.2.d: हिरण्यदन्तं शुचिवर्णमारात्क्षेत्रादपश्यमायुधा मिमानम् । ददानो अस्मा अमृतं विपृक्वत्किं मामनिन्द्राः कृणवन्ननुक्थाः ॥
5.2.e: I saw him from afar gold-toothed, bright-coloured, hurling his weapons from his habitation,  What time I gave him Amṛta free from mixture. How can the Indraless, the hymnless harm me?

5.2.d: क्षेत्रादपश्यं सनुतश्चरन्तं सुमद्यूथं न पुरु शोभमानम् । न ता अगृभ्रन्नजनिष्ट हि षः पलिक्नीरिद्युवतयो भवन्ति ॥
5.2.e: I saw him moving from the place he dwells in, even as with a herd, brilliantly shining.  These seized him not: he had been born already. They who were grey with age again grow youthful.

5.2.d: के मे मर्यकं वि यवन्त गोभिर्न येषां गोपा अरणश्चिदास । य ईं जगृभुरव ते सृजन्त्वाजाति पश्व उप नश्चिकित्वान् ॥
5.2.e: Who separate my young bull from the cattle, they whose protector was in truth no stranger?  Let those whose hands have seized upon them free them. May he, observant, drive the herd to us-ward.

5.2.d: वसां राजानं वसतिं जनानामरातयो नि दधुर्मर्त्येषु । ब्रह्माण्यत्रेरव तं सृजन्तु निन्दितारो निन्द्यासो भवन्तु ॥
5.2.e: Mid mortal men godless have secreted the King of all who live, home of the people.  So may the prayers of Atri give him freedom. Reproached in turn be those who now reproach him.

5.2.d: शुनश्चिच्छेपं निदितं सहस्राद्यूपादमुञ्चो अशमिष्ट हि षः । एवास्मदग्ने वि मुमुग्धि पाशान्होतश्चिकित्व इह तू निषद्य ॥
5.2.e: Thou from the stake didst loose e’en Śunaḥśepa bound for a thousand; for he prayed with fervour.  So, Agni, loose from us the bonds that bind us, when thou art seated here, O Priest who knowest.

5.2.d: हृणीयमानो अप हि मदैयेः प्र मे देवानां व्रतपा उवाच । इन्द्रो विद्वाँ अनु हि त्वा चचक्ष तेनाहमग्ने अनुशिष्ट आगाम् ॥
5.2.e: Thou hast sped from me, Agni, in thine anger: this the protector of Gods’ Laws hath told me.  Indra who knoweth bent his eye upon thee: by him instructed am I come, O Agni.

5.2.d: वि ज्योतिषा बृहता भात्यग्निराविर्विश्वानि कृणुते महित्वा । प्रादेवीर्मायाः सहते दुरेवाः शिशीते शृङ्गे रक्षसे विनिक्षे ॥
5.2.e: Agni shines far and wide with lofty splendour, and by his greatness makes all things apparent.  He conquers godless and malign enchantments, and sharpens both his horns to gore the Rakṣas.

5.2.d: उत स्वानासो दिवि षन्त्वग्नेस्तिग्मायुधा रक्षसे हन्तवा उ । मदे चिदस्य प्र रुजन्ति भामा न वरन्ते परिबाधो अदेवीः ॥
5.2.e: Loud in the heaven above be Agni's roarings with keen-edged weapons to destroy the demons.  Forth burst his splendours in the Soma's rapture. The godless bands press round but cannot stay him.

5.2.d: एतं ते स्तोमं तुविजात विप्रो रथं न धीरः स्वपा अतक्षम् । यदीदग्ने प्रति त्वं देव हर्याः स्वर्वतीरप एना जयेम ॥
5.2.e: As a skilled craftsman makes a car, a singer I, Mighty One! this hymn for thee have fashioned.  If thou, O Agni, God, accept it gladly, may we obtain thereby the heavenly Waters.

5.2.d: तुविग्रीवो वृषभो वावृधानोऽशत्र्व१र्यः समजाति वेदः । इतीममग्निममृता अवोचन्बर्हिष्मते मनवे शर्म यंसद्धविष्मते मनवे शर्म यंसत् ॥
5.2.e: May he, the strong-necked Steer, waxing in vigour, gather the foeman's wealth with none to check him.  Thus to this Agni have the Immortals spoken. To man who spreads the grass may he grant shelter, grant shelter to the man who brings oblation.

5.3.d: त्वमग्ने वरुणो जायसे यत्त्वं मित्रो भवसि यत्समिद्धः । त्वे विश्वे सहसस्पुत्र देवास्त्वमिन्द्रो दाशुषे मर्त्याय ॥
5.3.e: THOU at thy birth art Varuṇa, O Agni; when thou art kindled thou becomest Mitra.  In thee, O Son of Strength, all Gods are centred. Indra art thou to man who brings oblation.

5.3.d: त्वमर्यमा भवसि यत्कनीनां नाम स्वधावन्गुह्यं बिभर्षि । अञ्जन्ति मित्रं सुधितं न गोभिर्यद्दम्पती समनसा कृणोषि ॥
5.3.e: Aryaman art thou as regardeth maidens mysterious, is thy name, O Self-sustainer.  As a kind friend with streams of milk they balm thee what time thou makest wife and lord one-minded.

5.3.d: तव श्रिये मरुतो मर्जयन्त रुद्र यत्ते जनिम चारु चित्रम् । पदं यद्विष्णोरुपमं निधायि तेन पासि गुह्यं नाम गोनाम् ॥
5.3.e: The Maruts deck their beauty for thy glory, yea, Rudra! for thy birth fair, brightly-coloured.  That which was fixed as Viṣṇu's loftiest station—therewith the secret of the Cows thou guardest.

5.3.d: तव श्रिया सुदृशो देव देवाः पुरू दधाना अमृतं सपन्त । होतारमग्निं मनुषो नि षेदुर्दशस्यन्त उशिजः शंसमायोः ॥
5.3.e: Gods through thy glory, God who art so lovely! granting abundant gifts gained life immortal.  As their own Priest have men established Agni; and serve him fain for praise from him who liveth.

5.3.d: न त्वद्धोता पूर्वो अग्ने यजीयान्न काव्यैः परो अस्ति स्वधावः । विशश्च यस्या अतिथिर्भवासि स यज्ञेन वनवद्देव मर्तान् ॥
5.3.e: There is no priest more skilled than thou in worship; none Self-sustainer pass thee in wisdom.  The man within whose house as guest thou dwellest, O God, by sacrifice shall conquer mortals.

5.3.d: वयमग्ने वनुयाम त्वोता वसूयवो हविषा बुध्यमानाः । वयं समर्ये विदथेष्वह्नां वयं राया सहसस्पुत्र मर्तान् ॥
5.3.e: Aided by thee, O Agni may we conquer through our oblation, fain for wealth, awakened:  May we in battle, in the days’ assemblies, O Son of Strength, by riches conquer mortals.

5.3.d: यो न आगो अभ्येनो भरात्यधीदघमघशंसे दधात । जही चिकित्वो अभिशस्तिमेतामग्ने यो नो मर्चयति द्वयेन ॥
5.3.e: He shall bring evil on the evil-plotter whoever turns against us sin and outrage.  Destroy this calumny of him, O Agni, whoever injures us with double-dealing.

5.3.d: त्वामस्या व्युषि देव पूर्वे दूतं कृण्वाना अयजन्त हव्यैः । संस्थे यदग्न ईयसे रयीणां देवो मर्तैर्वसुभिरिध्यमानः ॥
5.3.e: At this dawn's flushing, God! our ancient fathers served thee with offerings, making thee their envoy,  When, Agni, to the store of wealth thou goest, a God enkindled with good things by mortals.

5.3.d: अव स्पृधि पितरं योधि विद्वान्पुत्रो यस्ते सहसः सून ऊहे । कदा चिकित्वो अभि चक्षसे नोऽग्ने कदाँ ऋतचिद्यातयासे ॥
5.3.e: Save, thou who knowest, draw thy father near thee, who counts as thine own son, O Child of Power.  O sapient Agni, when wilt thou regard us? When, skilled in holy Law, wilt thou direct us?

5.3.d: भूरि नाम वन्दमानो दधाति पिता वसो यदि तज्जोषयासे । कुविद्देवस्य सहसा चकानः सुम्नमग्निर्वनते वावृधानः ॥
5.3.e: Adoring thee he gives thee many a title, when thou, Good Lord! acceptest this as Father.  And doth not Agni, glad in strength of Godhead, gain splendid bliss when he hath waxen mighty?

5.3.d: त्वमङ्ग जरितारं यविष्ठ विश्वान्यग्ने दुरिताति पर्षि । स्तेना अदृश्रन्रिपवो जनासोऽज्ञातकेता वृजिना अभूवन् ॥
5.3.e: Most Youthful Agni, verily thou bearest thy praiser safely over all his troubles.  Thieves have been seen by us and open foemen: unknown have been the plottings of the wicked.

5.3.d: इमे यामासस्त्वद्रिगभूवन्वसवे वा तदिदागो अवाचि । नाहायमग्निरभिशस्तये नो न रीषते वावृधानः परा दात् ॥
5.3.e: To thee these eulogies have been directed: or to the Vasu hath this sin been spoken.  But this our Agni, flaming high, shall never yield us to calumny, to him who wrongs us.

5.4.d: त्वामग्ने वसुपतिं वसूनामभि प्र मन्दे अध्वरेषु राजन् । त्वया वाजं वाजयन्तो जयेमाभि ष्याम पृत्सुतीर्मर्त्यानाम् ॥
5.4.e: O AGNI, King and Lord of wealth and treasures, in thee is my delight at sacrifices.  Through thee may we obtain the strength we long for, and overcome the fierce attacks of mortals.

5.4.d: हव्यवाळग्निरजरः पिता नो विभुर्विभावा सुदृशीको अस्मे । सुगार्हपत्याः समिषो दिदीह्यस्मद्र्य१क्सं मिमीहि श्रवांसि ॥
5.4.e: Agni, Eternal Father, offering-bearer, fair to behold, far-reaching, far-refulgent,  From well-kept household fire beam food to feed us, and measure out to us abundant glory.

5.4.d: विशां कविं विश्पतिं मानुषीणां शुचिं पावकं घृतपृष्ठमग्निम् । नि होतारं विश्वविदं दधिध्वे स देवेषु वनते वार्याणि ॥
5.4.e: The Sage of men, the Lord of human races, pure, purifying Agni, balmed with butter,  Him the Omniscient as your Priest ye stablish: he wins among the Gods things worth the choosing.

5.4.d: जुषस्वाग्न इळया सजोषा यतमानो रश्मिभिः सूर्यस्य । जुषस्व नः समिधं जातवेद आ च देवान्हविरद्याय वक्षि ॥
5.4.e: Agni, enjoy, of one accord with Iḷā, striving in rivalry with beams of Sūrya,  Enjoy, O Jātavedas, this our fuel, and bring the Gods to us to taste oblations.

5.4.d: जुष्टो दमूना अतिथिर्दुरोण इमं नो यज्ञमुप याहि विद्वान् । विश्वा अग्ने अभियुजो विहत्या शत्रूयतामा भरा भोजनानि ॥
5.4.e: As dear House-Friend, guest welcome in the dwelling, to this our sacrifice come thou who knowest.  And, Agni, having scattered all assailants, bring to us the possessions of our foemen.

5.4.d: वधेन दस्युं प्र हि चातयस्व वयः कृण्वानस्तन्वे३ स्वायै । पिपर्षि यत्सहसस्पुत्र देवान्त्सो अग्ने पाहि नृतम वाजे अस्मान् ॥
5.4.e: Drive thou away the Dasyu with thy weapon. As, gaining vital power for thine own body,  O Son of Strength, the Gods thou satisfiest, so in fight save us, most heroic Agni.

5.4.d: वयं ते अग्न उक्थैर्विधेम वयं हव्यैः पावक भद्रशोचे । अस्मे रयिं विश्ववारं समिन्वास्मे विश्वानि द्रविणानि धेहि ॥
5.4.e: May we, O Agni, with our lauds adore thee, and with our gifts, fair-beaming Purifier!  Send to us wealth containing all things precious: bestow upon us every sort of riches.

5.4.d: अस्माकमग्ने अध्वरं जुषस्व सहसः सूनो त्रिषधस्थ हव्यम् । वयं देवेषु सुकृतः स्याम शर्मणा नस्त्रिवरूथेन पाहि ॥
5.4.e: Son of Strength, Agni, dweller in three regions, accept our sacrifice and our oblation.  Among the Gods may we be counted pious: protect us with a triply-guarding shelter.

5.4.d: विश्वानि नो दुर्गहा जातवेदः सिन्धुं न नावा दुरिताति पर्षि । अग्ने अत्रिवन्नमसा गृणानो३ऽस्माकं बोध्यविता तनूनाम् ॥
5.4.e: Over all woes and dangers, Jātavedas, bear us as in a boat across a river.  Praised with our homage even as Atri praised thee, O Agni, be the guardian of our bodies.

5.4.d: यस्त्वा हृदा कीरिणा मन्यमानोऽमर्त्यं मर्त्यो जोहवीमि । जातवेदो यशो अस्मासु धेहि प्रजाभिरग्ने अमृतत्वमश्याम् ॥
5.4.e: As I, remembering thee with grateful spirit, a mortal, call with might on thee Immortal,  Vouchsafe us high renown, O Jātavedas, and may I be immortal by my children.

5.4.d: यस्मै त्वं सुकृते जातवेद उ लोकमग्ने कृणवः स्योनम् । अश्विनं स पुत्रिणं वीरवन्तं गोमन्तं रयिं नशते स्वस्ति ॥
5.4.e: The pious man, O Jātavedas Agni, to whom thou grantest ample room and pleasure,  Gaineth abundant wealth with sons and horses, with heroes and with kine for his well-being.

5.5.d: सुसमिद्धाय शोचिषे घृतं तीव्रं जुहोतन । अग्नये जातवेदसे ॥
5.5.e: To Agni, Jātavedas, to the flame, the well-enkindled God,  Offer thick sacrificial oil.
He, Narāśaṁsa, ne’er beguiled, inspiriteth this sacrifice:  For sage is he, with sweets in hand.

5.5.d: ईळितो अग्न आ वहेन्द्रं चित्रमिह प्रियम् । सुखै रथेभिरूतये ॥
5.5.e: Adored, O Agni, hither bring Indra the Wonderful, the Friend,  On lightly-rolling car to aid.

5.5.d: ऊर्णम्रदा वि प्रथस्वाभ्य१र्का अनूषत । भवा नः शुभ्र सातये ॥
5.5.e: Spread thyself out, thou soft as wool The holy hymns have sung to thee.  Bring gain to us, O beautiful!

5.5.d: देवीर्द्वारो वि श्रयध्वं सुप्रायणा न ऊतये । प्रप्र यज्ञं पृणीतन ॥
5.5.e: Open yourselves, ye Doors Divine, easy of access for our aid:  Fill, more and more, the sacrifice.

5.5.d: सुप्रतीके वयोवृधा यह्वी ऋतस्य मातरा । दोषामुषासमीमहे ॥
5.5.e: Fair strengtheners of vital power, young Mothers of eternal Law,  Morning and Night we supplicate.

5.5.d: वातस्य पत्मन्नीळिता दैव्या होतारा मनुषः । इमं नो यज्ञमा गतम् ॥
5.5.e: On the wind's flight come, glorified, ye two celestial Priests of man  Come ye to this our sacrifice.

5.5.d: इळा सरस्वती मही तिस्रो देवीर्मयोभुवः । बर्हिः सीदन्त्वस्रिधः ॥
5.5.e: Iḷā, Sarasvatī, Mahī, three Goddesses who bring us weal,  Be seated harmless on the grass.

5.5.d: शिवस्त्वष्टरिहा गहि विभुः पोष उत त्मना । यज्ञेयज्ञे न उदव ॥
5.5.e: Rich in all plenty, Tvaṣṭar, come auspicious of thine own accord  Help us in every sacrifice.

5.5.d: यत्र वेत्थ वनस्पते देवानां गुह्या नामानि । तत्र हव्यानि गामय ॥
5.5.e: Vanaspati, wherever thou knowest the Gods’ mysterious names,  Send our oblations thitherward.

5.5.d: स्वाहाग्नये वरुणाय स्वाहेन्द्राय मरुद्भ्यः । स्वाहा देवेभ्यो हविः ॥
5.5.e: To Agni and to Varuṇa, Indra, the Maruts, and the Gods,  With Svāhā be oblation brought.

5.6.d: अग्निं तं मन्ये यो वसुरस्तं यं यन्ति धेनवः । अस्तमर्वन्त आशवोऽस्तं नित्यासो वाजिन इषं स्तोतृभ्य आ भर ॥
5.6.e: I VALUE Agni that good Lord, the home to which the kine return:  Whom fleet-foot coursers seek as home, and strong enduring steeds as home. Bring food to those who sing thy praise.

5.6.d: सो अग्निर्यो वसुर्गृणे सं यमायन्ति धेनवः । समर्वन्तो रघुद्रुवः सं सुजातासः सूरय इषं स्तोतृभ्य आ भर ॥
5.6.e: ’Tis Agni whom we laud as good, to whom the milch-kine come in herds,  To whom the chargers swift of foot, to whom our well-born princes come. Bring food to those who sing thy praise.

5.6.d: अग्निर्हि वाजिनं विशे ददाति विश्वचर्षणिः । अग्नी राये स्वाभुवं स प्रीतो याति वार्यमिषं स्तोतृभ्य आ भर ॥
5.6.e: Agni the God of all mankind, gives, verily, a steed to man.  Agni gives precious gear for wealth, treasure he gives when he is pleased. Bring food to those who sing thy praise.

5.6.d: आ ते अग्न इधीमहि द्युमन्तं देवाजरम् । यद्ध स्या ते पनीयसी समिद्दीदयति द्यवीषं स्तोतृभ्य आ भर ॥
5.6.e: God, Agni, we will kindle thee, rich in thy splendour, fading not,  So that this glorious fuel may send forth by day its light for thee. Bring food to those who sing thy praise.

5.6.d: आ ते अग्न ऋचा हविः शुक्रस्य शोचिषस्पते । सुश्चन्द्र दस्म विश्पते हव्यवाट् तुभ्यं हूयत इषं स्तोतृभ्य आ भर ॥
5.6.e: To thee the splendid, Lord of flame, bright, wondrous, Prince of men, is brought.  Oblation with the holy verse, O Agni, bearer of our gifts.  Bring food to those who sing thy praise.

5.6.d: प्रो त्ये अग्नयोऽग्निषु विश्वं पुष्यन्ति वार्यम् । ते हिन्विरे त इन्विरे त इषण्यन्त्यानुषगिषं स्तोतृभ्य आ भर ॥
5.6.e: These Agnis in the seats of the fire nourish each thing most excellent.  They give delight, they spread abroad, they move themselves continually. Bring food to those who sing thy praise.

5.6.d: तव त्ये अग्ने अर्चयो महि व्राधन्त वाजिनः । ये पत्वभिः शफानां व्रजा भुरन्त गोनामिषं स्तोतृभ्य आ भर ॥
5.6.e: Agni, these brilliant flames of thine wax like strong chargers mightily,  Who with the treadings of their hoofs go swiftly to the stalls of kine. Bring food to those who sing thy praise.

5.6.d: नवा नो अग्न आ भर स्तोतृभ्यः सुक्षितीरिषः । ते स्याम य आनृचुस्त्वादूतासो दमेदम इषं स्तोतृभ्य आ भर ॥
5.6.e: To us who laud thee, Agni, bring fresh food and safe and happy homes.  May we who have sung hymns to thee have thee for envoy in each house. Bring food to those who sing thy praise.

5.6.d: उभे सुश्चन्द्र सर्पिषो दर्वी श्रीणीष आसनि । उतो न उत्पुपूर्या उक्थेषु शवसस्पत इषं स्तोतृभ्य आ भर ॥
5.6.e: Thou, brilliant God, within thy mouth warmest both ladles of the oil.  So fill us also, in our hymns, abundantly, O Lord of Strength. Bring food to those who sing thy praise.

5.6.d: एवाँ अग्निमजुर्यमुर्गीर्भिर्यज्ञेभिरानुषक् । दधदस्मे सुवीर्यमुत त्यदाश्वश्व्यमिषं स्तोतृभ्य आ भर ॥
5.6.e: Thus Agni have we duly served with sacrifices and with hymns.  So may he give us what we crave, store of brave sons and fleet-foot steeds. Bring food to those who sing thy praise.

5.7.d: सखायः सं वः सम्यञ्चमिषं स्तोमं चाग्नये । वर्षिष्ठाय क्षितीनामूर्जो नप्त्रे सहस्वते ॥
5.7.e: OFFER to Agni, O my friends, your seemly food, your seemly praise;  To him supremest o’er the folk, the Son of Strength, the mighty Lord:

5.7.d: कुत्रा चिद्यस्य समृतौ रण्वा नरो नृषदने । अर्हन्तश्चिद्यमिन्धते संजनयन्ति जन्तवः ॥
5.7.e: Him in whose presence, when they meet in full assembly, men rejoice;  Even him whom worthy ones inflame, and living creatures bring to life.

5.7.d: सं यदिषो वनामहे सं हव्या मानुषाणाम् । उत द्युम्नस्य शवस ऋतस्य रश्मिमा ददे ॥
5.7.e: When we present to him the food and sacrificial gifts of men,  He by the might of splendour grasps the holy Ordinance's rein.

5.7.d: स स्मा कृणोति केतुमा नक्तं चिद्दूर आ सते । पावको यद्वनस्पतीन्प्र स्मा मिनात्यजरः ॥
5.7.e: He gives a signal in the night even to him who is afar,  When he, the Bright, unchanged by eld, consumes the sovrans of the wood.

5.7.d: अव स्म यस्य वेषणे स्वेदं पथिषु जुह्वति । अभीमह स्वजेन्यं भूमा पृष्ठेव रुरुहुः ॥
5.7.e: He in whose service on the ways they offer up their drops of sweat,  On him is their high kin have they mounted, as ridges on the earth.

5.7.d: यं मर्त्यः पुरुस्पृहं विदद्विश्वस्य धायसे । प्र स्वादनं पितूनामस्ततातिं चिदायवे ॥
5.7.e: Whom, sought of many, mortal man hath found to be the Stay of all;  He who gives flavour to our food, the home of every man that lives.

5.7.d: स हि ष्मा धन्वाक्षितं दाता न दात्या पशुः । हिरिश्मश्रुः शुचिदन्नृभुरनिभृष्टतविषिः ॥
5.7.e: Even as a herd that crops the grass he shears the field and wilderness,  With flashing teeth and beard of gold, deft with his unabated might.

5.7.d: शुचिः ष्म यस्मा अत्रिवत्प्र स्वधितीव रीयते । सुषूरसूत माता क्राणा यदानशे भगम् ॥
5.7.e: For him, to whom, bright as an axe he, as to Atri, hath flashed forth,  Hath the well-bearing Mother borne, producing when her time is come.

5.7.d: आ यस्ते सर्पिरासुतेऽग्ने शमस्ति धायसे । ऐषु द्युम्नमुत श्रव आ चित्तं मर्त्येषु धाः ॥
5.7.e: Agni to whom the oil is shed by him thou lovest to support,  Bestow upon these mortals fame and splendour and intelligence.

5.7.d: इति चिन्मन्युमध्रिजस्त्वादातमा पशुं ददे । आदग्ने अपृणतोऽत्रिः सासह्याद्दस्यूनिषः सासह्यान्नॄन् ॥
5.7.e: Such zeal hath he, resistless one: he gained the cattle given by thee.  Agni, may Atri overcome the Dasyus who bestow no gifts, subdue the men who give no food.

5.8.d: त्वामग्न ऋतायवः समीधिरे प्रत्नं प्रत्नास ऊतये सहस्कृत । पुरुश्चन्द्रं यजतं विश्वधायसं दमूनसं गृहपतिं वरेण्यम् ॥
5.8.e: O AGNI urged to strength, the men of old who loved the Law enkindled thee,  the Ancient, for their aid,  Thee very bright, and holy, nourisher of all, most excellent, the Friend and Master of the home.

5.8.d: त्वामग्ने अतिथिं पूर्व्यं विशः शोचिष्केशं गृहपतिं नि षेदिरे । बृहत्केतुं पुरुरूपं धनस्पृतं सुशर्माणं स्ववसं जरद्विषम् ॥
5.8.e: Thee, Agni, men have stablished as their guest of old, as Master of the household, thee, with hair of flame;  High-bannered, multiform, distributor of wealth, kind helper, good protector, drier of the floods.

5.8.d: त्वामग्ने मानुषीरीळते विशो होत्राविदं विविचिं रत्नधातमम् । गुहा सन्तं सुभग विश्वदर्शतं तुविष्वणसं सुयजं घृतश्रियम् ॥
5.8.e: The tribes of men praise thee, Agni, who knowest well burnt offerings, the Discerner, lavishest of wealth,  Dwelling in secret, Blest One! visible to all, loud-roaring, skilled in worship, glorified with oil.

5.8.d: त्वामग्ने धर्णसिं विश्वधा वयं गीर्भिर्गृणन्तो नमसोप सेदिम । स नो जुषस्व समिधानो अङ्गिरो देवो मर्तस्य यशसा सुदीतिभिः ॥
5.8.e: Ever to thee, O Agni, as exceeding strong have we drawn nigh with songs and reverence singing hymns.  So be thou pleased with us, Aṅgiras! as a God enkindled by the noble with man's goodly light.

5.8.d: त्वमग्ने पुरुरूपो विशेविशे वयो दधासि प्रत्नथा पुरुष्टुत । पुरूण्यन्ना सहसा वि राजसि त्विषिः सा ते तित्विषाणस्य नाधृषे ॥
5.8.e: Thou, Agni! multiform, God who art lauded much! givest in every house subsistence as of old.  Thou rulest by thy might o’er food of many a sort: that light of thine when blazing may not be opposed.

5.8.d: त्वामग्ने समिधानं यविष्ठ्य देवा दूतं चक्रिरे हव्यवाहनम् । उरुज्रयसं घृतयोनिमाहुतं त्वेषं चक्षुर्दधिरे चोदयन्मति ॥
5.8.e: The Gods, Most Youthful Agni, have made thee, inflamed, the bearer of oblations and the messenger.  Thee, widely-reaching, homed in sacred oil, invoked, effulgent, have they made the Eye that stirs the thought.

5.8.d: त्वामग्ने प्रदिव आहुतं घृतैः सुम्नायवः सुषमिधा समीधिरे । स वावृधान ओषधीभिरुक्षितो३ऽभि ज्रयांसि पार्थिवा वि तिष्ठसे ॥
5.8.e: Men seeking joy have lit thee worshipped from of old, O Agni, with good fuel and with sacred oil.  So thou, bedewed and waxing mighty by the plants, spreadest thyself abroad over the realms of earth.

5.9.d: त्वामग्ने हविष्मन्तो देवं मर्तास ईळते । मन्ये त्वा जातवेदसं स हव्या वक्ष्यानुषक् ॥
5.9.e: BEARING; oblations mortal men, O Agni, worship thee the God.  I deem thee Jātavedas: bear our offerings, thou, unceasingly.

5.9.d: अग्निर्होता दास्वतः क्षयस्य वृक्तबर्हिषः । सं यज्ञासश्चरन्ति यं सं वाजासः श्रवस्यवः ॥
5.9.e: In the man's home who offers gifts, where grass is trimmed, Agni is Priest,  To whom all sacrifices come and strengthenings that win renown.

5.9.d: उत स्म यं शिशुं यथा नवं जनिष्टारणी । धर्तारं मानुषीणां विशामग्निं स्वध्वरम् ॥
5.9.e: Whom, as an infant newly-born, the kindling-sticks have brought to life,  Sustainer of the tribes of men, skilled in well-ordered sacrifice.

5.9.d: उत स्म दुर्गृभीयसे पुत्रो न ह्वार्याणाम् । पुरू यो दग्धासि वनाग्ने पशुर्न यवसे ॥
5.9.e: Yea, very hard art thou to grasp, like offspring of the wriggling snakes,  When thou consumest many woods like an ox, Agni, in the mead.

5.9.d: अध स्म यस्यार्चयः सम्यक्संयन्ति धूमिनः । यदीमह त्रितो दिव्युप ध्मातेव धमति शिशीते ध्मातरी यथा ॥
5.9.e: Whose flames, when thou art sending forth the smoke, completely reach the mark,  When Tṛta in the height of heaven, like as a smelter fanneth thee, e’en as a smelter sharpeneth thee.

5.9.d: तवाहमग्न ऊतिभिर्मित्रस्य च प्रशस्तिभिः । द्वेषोयुतो न दुरिता तुर्याम मर्त्यानाम् ॥
5.9.e: O Agni, by thy succour and by Mitra's friendly furtherance,  May we, averting hate,  subdue  the wickedness of mortal men.

5.9.d: तं नो अग्ने अभी नरो रयिं सहस्व आ भर । स क्षेपयत्स पोषयद्भुवद्वाजस्य सातय उतैधि पृत्सु नो वृधे ॥
5.9.e: O Agni, to our heroes bring such riches, thou victorious God.  May he protect and nourish us, and help in gaining strength: be thou near us in fight for our success.

5.10.d: अग्न ओजिष्ठमा भर द्युम्नमस्मभ्यमध्रिगो । प्र नो राया परीणसा रत्सि वाजाय पन्थाम् ॥
5.10.e: BRING us most mighty splendour thou, Agni, resistless on thy way.  With overflowing store of wealth mark out for us a path to strength.

5.10.d: त्वं नो अग्ने अद्भुत क्रत्वा दक्षस्य मंहना । त्वे असुर्य१मारुहत्क्राणा मित्रो न यज्ञियः ॥
5.10.e: Ours art thou, wondrous Agni, by wisdom and bounteousness of power.  The might of Asuras rests on thee, like Mitra worshipful in act.

5.10.d: त्वं नो अग्न एषां गयं पुष्टिं च वर्धय । ये स्तोमेभिः प्र सूरयो नरो मघान्यानशुः ॥
5.10.e: Agni, increase our means of life, increase the house and home of these,  The men, the princes who have won great riches through our hymns of praise.

5.10.d: ये अग्ने चन्द्र ते गिरः शुम्भन्त्यश्वराधसः । शुष्मेभिः शुष्मिणो नरो दिवश्चिद्येषां बृहत्सुकीर्तिर्बोधति त्मना ॥
5.10.e: Bright Agni, they who deck their songs for thee have horses as their meed.  The men are mighty in their might, they whose high laud, as that of heaven, awakes thee of its own accord.

5.10.d: तव त्ये अग्ने अर्चयो भ्राजन्तो यन्ति धृष्णुया । परिज्मानो न विद्युतः स्वानो रथो न वाजयुः ॥
5.10.e: O Agni, those resplendent flames of thine go valorously forth,  Like lightnings flashing round us, like a rattling car that seeks the spoil.

5.10.d: नू नो अग्न ऊतये सबाधसश्च रातये । अस्माकासश्च सूरयो विश्वा आशास्तरीषणि ॥
5.10.e: Now, Agni, come to succour us; let priests draw nigh to offer gifts;  And let the patrons of our rites subdue all regions of the earth.

5.10.d: त्वं नो अग्ने अङ्गिरः स्तुतः स्तवान आ भर । होतर्विभ्वासहं रयिं स्तोतृभ्यः स्तवसे च न उतैधि पृत्सु नो वृधे ॥
5.10.e: Bring to us, Agni, Aṅgiras, lauded of old and lauded now,  Invoker! wealth to quell the strong, that singers may extol thee. Be near us in fight for our success.

5.11.d: जनस्य गोपा अजनिष्ट जागृविरग्निः सुदक्षः सुविताय नव्यसे । घृतप्रतीको बृहता दिविस्पृशा द्युमद्वि भाति भरतेभ्यः शुचिः ॥
5.11.e: THE watchful Guardian of the people hath been born, Agni, the very strong, for fresh prosperity.  With oil upon his face, with high heaven-touching flame, he shineth splendidly, pure, for the Bharatas.

5.11.d: यज्ञस्य केतुं प्रथमं पुरोहितमग्निं नरस्त्रिषधस्थे समीधिरे । इन्द्रेण देवैः सरथं स बर्हिषि सीदन्नि होता यजथाय सुक्रतुः ॥
5.11.e: Ensign of sacrifice, the earliest Household-Priest, the men have kindled Agni in his threefold seat,  With Indra and the Gods together on the grass let the wise Priest sit to complete the sacrifice.

5.11.d: असम्मृष्टो जायसे मात्रोः शुचिर्मन्द्रः कविरुदतिष्ठो विवस्वतः । घृतेन त्वावर्धयन्नग्न आहुत धूमस्ते केतुरभवद्दिवि श्रितः ॥
5.11.e: Pure , unadorned, from thy two Mothers art thou born: thou camest from Vivasvān as a charming Sage.  With oil they strengthened thee, O Agni, worshipped God: thy banner was the smoke that mounted to the sky.

5.11.d: अग्निर्नो यज्ञमुप वेतु साधुयाग्निं नरो वि भरन्ते गृहेगृहे । अग्निर्दूतो अभवद्धव्यवाहनोऽग्निं वृणाना वृणते कविक्रतुम् ॥
5.11.e: May Agni graciously come to our sacrifice. The men bear Agni here and there in every house.  He hath become an envoy, bearer of our gifts: electing Agni, men choose one exceeding wise.

5.11.d: तुभ्येदमग्ने मधुमत्तमं वचस्तुभ्यं मनीषा इयमस्तु शं हृदे । त्वां गिरः सिन्धुमिवावनीर्महीरा पृणन्ति शवसा वर्धयन्ति च ॥
5.11.e: For thee, O Agni, is this sweetest prayer of mine: dear to thy spirit be this product of my thought.  As great streams fill the river so our song of praise fill thee, and make thee yet more mighty in thy strength.

5.11.d: त्वामग्ने अङ्गिरसो गुहा हितमन्वविन्दञ्छिश्रियाणं वनेवने । स जायसे मथ्यमानः सहो महत्त्वामाहुः सहसस्पुत्रमङ्गिरः ॥
5.11.e: O Agni, the Aṅgirases discovered thee what time thou layest hidden, fleeing back from wood to wood.  Thou by attrition art produced as conquering might, and men, O Aṅgiras, call thee the Son of Strength.

5.12.d: प्राग्नये बृहते यज्ञियाय ऋतस्य वृष्णे असुराय मन्म । घृतं न यज्ञ आस्ये३ सुपूतं गिरं भरे वृषभाय प्रतीचीम् ॥
5.12.e: To Agni, lofty Asura, meet for worship, Steer of eternal Law, my prayer I offer;  I bring my song directed to the Mighty like pure oil for his mouth at sacrifices.

5.12.d: ऋतं चिकित्व ऋतमिच्चिकिद्ध्यृतस्य धारा अनु तृन्धि पूर्वीः । नाहं यातुं सहसा न द्वयेन ऋतं सपाम्यरुषस्य वृष्णः ॥
5.12.e: Mark the Law, thou who knowest, yea, observe it: send forth the full streams of eternal Order.  I use no sorcery with might or falsehood the sacred Law of the Red Steer I follow.

5.12.d: कया नो अग्न ऋतयन्नृतेन भुवो नवेदा उचथस्य नव्यः । वेदा मे देव ऋतुपा ऋतूनां नाहं पतिं सनितुरस्य रायः ॥
5.12.e: How hast thou, follower of the Law eternal, become the knower of a new song, Agni?  The God, the Guardian of the seasons, knows me: the Lord of him who won this wealth I know not.

5.12.d: के ते अग्ने रिपवे बन्धनासः के पायवः सनिषन्त द्युमन्तः । के धासिमग्ने अनृतस्य पान्ति क आसतो वचसः सन्ति गोपाः ॥
5.12.e: Who, Agni, in alliance with thy foeman, what splendid helpers won for them their riches?  Agni, who guard the dwelling-place of falsehood? Who are protectors of the speech of liars?

5.12.d: सखायस्ते विषुणा अग्न एते शिवासः सन्तो अशिवा अभूवन् । अधूर्षत स्वयमेते वचोभिर्ऋजूयते वृजिनानि ब्रुवन्तः ॥
5.12.e: Agni, those friends of thine have turned them from thee: gracious of old, they have become ungracious.  They have deceived themselves by their own speeches, uttering wicked words against the righteous.

5.12.d: यस्ते अग्ने नमसा यज्ञमीट्ट ऋतं स पात्यरुषस्य वृष्णः । तस्य क्षयः पृथुरा साधुरेतु प्रसर्स्राणस्य नहुषस्य शेषः ॥
5.12.e: He who pays sacrifice to thee with homage, O Agni, keeps the Red Steer's Law eternal;  Wide is his dwelling. May the noble offspring of Nahuṣa who wandered forth come hither.

5.13.d: अर्चन्तस्त्वा हवामहेऽर्चन्तः समिधीमहि । अग्ने अर्चन्त ऊतये ॥
5.13.e: WITH songs of praise we call on thee, we kindle thee with songs of praise,  Agni, with songs of praise, for help.

5.13.d: अग्नेः स्तोमं मनामहे सिध्रमद्य दिविस्पृशः । देवस्य द्रविणस्यवः ॥
5.13.e: Eager for wealth, we meditate Agni's effectual praise to-day,  Praise of the God who touches heaven.

5.13.d: अग्निर्जुषत नो गिरो होता यो मानुषेष्वा । स यक्षद्दैव्यं जनम् ॥
5.13.e: May Agni, Priest among mankind, take pleasure in our songs of praise,  And worship the Celestial Folk.

5.13.d: त्वमग्ने सप्रथा असि जुष्टो होता वरेण्यः । त्वया यज्ञं वि तन्वते ॥
5.13.e: Thou, Agni, art spread widely forth, Priest dear and excellent; through thee  Men make the sacrifice complete.

5.13.d: त्वामग्ने वाजसातमं विप्रा वर्धन्ति सुष्टुतम् । स नो रास्व सुवीर्यम् ॥
5.13.e: Singers exalt thee, Agni, well lauded, best giver of our strength:  So grant thou us heroic might.

5.13.d: अग्ने नेमिरराँ इव देवाँस्त्वं परिभूरसि । आ राधश्चित्रमृञ्जसे ॥
5.13.e: Thou Agni, as the felly rings the spokes, encompassest the Gods.  I yearn for bounty manifold.

5.14.d: अग्निं स्तोमेन बोधय समिधानो अमर्त्यम् । हव्या देवेषु नो दधत् ॥
5.14.e: ENKINDLING the Immortal, wake Agni with song of praise: may he bear our oblations to the Gods.

5.14.d: तमध्वरेष्वीळते देवं मर्ता अमर्त्यम् । यजिष्ठं मानुषे जने ॥
5.14.e: At high solemnities mortal men glorify him the Immortal, best  At sacrifice among mankind.

5.14.d: तं हि शश्वन्त ईळते स्रुचा देवं घृतश्चुता । अग्निं हव्याय वोळ्हवे ॥
5.14.e: That he may bear their gifts to heaven, all glorify him Agni, God,  With ladle that distilleth oil.

5.14.d: अग्निर्जातो अरोचत घ्नन्दस्यूञ्ज्योतिषा तमः । अविन्दद्गा अपः स्वः ॥
5.14.e: Agni shone bright when born, with light killing the Dasyus and the dark:  He found the Kine, the Floods, the Sun.

5.14.d: अग्निमीळेन्यं कविं घृतपृष्ठं सपर्यत । वेतु मे शृणवद्धवम् ॥
5.14.e: Serve Agni, God adorable, the Sage whose back is balmed with oil:  Let him approach, and hear my call.
They have exalted Agni, God of all mankind, with oil and hymns  Of praise, devout and eloquent.

5.15.d: प्र वेधसे कवये वेद्याय गिरं भरे यशसे पूर्व्याय । घृतप्रसत्तो असुरः सुशेवो रायो धर्ता धरुणो वस्वो अग्निः ॥
5.15.e: To him, the far-renowned, the wise Ordainer, ancient and glorious, a song I offer.  Enthroned in oil, the Asura, bliss-giver, is Agni, firm support of noble, riches.

5.15.d: ऋतेन ऋतं धरुणं धारयन्त यज्ञस्य शाके परमे व्योमन् । दिवो धर्मन्धरुणे सेदुषो नॄञ्जातैरजाताँ अभि ये ननक्षुः ॥
5.15.e: By holy Law they kept supporting Order, by help of sacrifice, in loftiest heaven,—  They who attained with born men to the unborn, men seated on that stay, heaven's firm sustainer.

5.15.d: अङ्होयुवस्तन्वस्तन्वते वि वयो महद्दुष्टरं पूर्व्याय । स संवतो नवजातस्तुतुर्यात्सिङ्हं न क्रुद्धमभितः परि ष्ठुः ॥
5.15.e: Averting woe, they labour hard to bring him, the ancient, plenteous food as power resistless.  May he, born newly, conquer his assailants: round him they stand as round an angry lion.

5.15.d: मातेव यद्भरसे पप्रथानो जनंजनं धायसे चक्षसे च । वयोवयो जरसे यद्दधानः परि त्मना विषुरूपो जिगासि ॥
5.15.e: When, like a mother, spreading forth to nourish, to cherish and regard each man that liveth,—  Consuming all the strength that thou hast gotten, thou wanderest round, thyself, in varied fashion.

5.15.d: वाजो नु ते शवसस्पात्वन्तमुरुं दोघं धरुणं देव रायः । पदं न तायुर्गुहा दधानो महो राये चितयन्नत्रिमस्पः ॥
5.15.e: May strength preserve the compass of thy vigour, God! that broad stream of thine that beareth riches.  Thou, like a thief who keeps his refuge secret, hast holpen Atri to great wealth, by teaching.

5.16.d: बृहद्वयो हि भानवेऽर्चा देवायाग्नये । यं मित्रं न प्रशस्तिभिर्मर्तासो दधिरे पुरः ॥
5.16.e: GREAT power is in the beam of light, sing praise to, Agni, to the God  Whom men have set in foremost place like Mitra with their eulogies.

5.16.d: स हि द्युभिर्जनानां होता दक्षस्य बाह्वोः । वि हव्यमग्निरानुषग्भगो न वारमृण्वति ॥
5.16.e: He by the splendour of his arms is Priest of every able man.  Agni conveys oblation straight, and deals, as Bhaga deals, his boons.

5.16.d: अस्य स्तोमे मघोनः सख्ये वृद्धशोचिषः । विश्वा यस्मिन्तुविष्वणि समर्ये शुष्ममादधुः ॥
5.16.e: All rests upon the laud and love of him the rich, high-flaming God,  On whom, loud-roaring, men have laid great strength as on a faithful friend.

5.16.d: अधा ह्यग्न एषां सुवीर्यस्य मंहना । तमिद्यह्वं न रोदसी परि श्रवो बभूवतुः ॥
5.16.e: So, Agni, be the Friend of these with liberal gift of hero strength.  Yea, Heaven and Earth have not surpassed this Youthful One in glorious fame.

5.16.d: नू न एहि वार्यमग्ने गृणान आ भर । ये वयं ये च सूरयः स्वस्ति धामहे सचोतैधि पृत्सु नो वृधे ॥
5.16.e: O Agni, quickly come to us, and, glorified, bring precious wealth.  So we and these our princes will assemble for the good of all. Be near in fight to prosper us.

5.17.d: आ यज्ञैर्देव मर्त्य इत्था तव्यांसमूतये । अग्निं कृते स्वध्वरे पूरुरीळीतावसे ॥
5.17.e: GOD, may a mortal call the Strong hither, with solemn rites, to aid,  A man call Agni to protect when sacrifice is well prepared.

5.17.d: अस्य हि स्वयशस्तर आसा विधर्मन्मन्यसे । तं नाकं चित्रशोचिषं मन्द्रं परो मनीषया ॥
5.17.e: Near him thou seemest mightier still in native glory, set to hold  Apart yon flame-hued vault of heaven, lovely beyond the thought of man.

5.17.d: अस्य वासा उ अर्चिषा य आयुक्त तुजा गिरा । दिवो न यस्य रेतसा बृहच्छोचन्त्यर्चयः ॥
5.17.e: Yea, this is by the light of him whom powerful song hath bound to act,  Whose beams of splendour flash on high as though they sprang from heavenly seed.

5.17.d: अस्य क्रत्वा विचेतसो दस्मस्य वसु रथ आ । अधा विश्वासु हव्योऽग्निर्विक्षु प्र शस्यते ॥
5.17.e: Wealth loads the Wonder-Worker's car through his, the very wise One's power.  Then, meet to be invoked among all tribes, is Agni glorified.

5.17.d: नू न इद्धि वार्यमासा सचन्त सूरयः । ऊर्जो नपादभिष्टये पाहि शग्धि स्वस्तय उतैधि पृत्सु नो वृधे ॥
5.17.e: Now, too, the princes shall obtain excellent riches by our lips.  Protect us for our welfare: lend thy succour, O thou Son of Strength. Be near in fight to prosper us.

5.18.d: प्रातरग्निः पुरुप्रियो विशः स्तवेतातिथिः । विश्वानि यो अमर्त्यो हव्या मर्तेषु रण्यति ॥
5.18.e: AT dawn let Agni, much-beloved guest of the house, be glorified;  Immortal who delights in all oblations brought by mortal men.

5.18.d: द्विताय मृक्तवाहसे स्वस्य दक्षस्य मंहना । इन्दुं स धत्त आनुषक्स्तोता चित्ते अमर्त्य ॥
5.18.e: For Dvita who receives through wealth of native strength maimed offerings,  Thy praiser even gains at once the Soma-drops, Immortal Gods!

5.18.d: तं वो दीर्घायुशोचिषं गिरा हुवे मघोनाम् । अरिष्टो येषां रथो व्यश्वदावन्नीयते ॥
5.18.e: Nobles, with song I call that car of yours that shines with lengthened life,  For, God who givest steeds! that car hither and thither goes unharmed.

5.18.d: चित्रा वा येषु दीधितिरासन्नुक्था पान्ति ये । स्तीर्णं बर्हिः स्वर्णरे श्रवांसि दधिरे परि ॥
5.18.e: They who have varied ways of thought, who guard the lauds within their lips,  And strew the grass before the light, have decked themselves with high renown.

5.18.d: ये मे पञ्चाशतं ददुरश्वानां सधस्तुति । द्युमदग्ने महि श्रवो बृहत्कृधि मघोनां नृवदमृत नृणाम् ॥
5.18.e: Immortal Agni, give the chiefs, heroes who institute the rite,  Heroes’ illustrious, lofty fame, who at the synod met for praise presented me with fifty steeds.

5.19.d: अभ्यवस्थाः प्र जायन्ते प्र वव्रेर्वव्रिश्चिकेत । उपस्थे मातुर्वि चष्टे ॥
5.19.e: ONE state begets another state: husk is made visible from husk:  Within his Mother's side he speaks.

5.19.d: जुहुरे वि चितयन्तोऽनिमिषं नृम्णं पान्ति । आ दृळ्हां पुरं विविशुः ॥
5.19.e: Discerning, have they offered gifts: they guard the strength that never wastes.  To a strong fort have they pressed in.

5.19.d: आ श्वैत्रेयस्य जन्तवो द्युमद्वर्धन्त कृष्टयः । निष्कग्रीवो बृहदुक्थ एना मध्वा न वाजयुः ॥
5.19.e: Śvaitreya's people, all his men, have gloriously increased in might.  A gold chain Bṛhaduktha wears, as, through this Soma, seeking spoil.

5.19.d: प्रियं दुग्धं न काम्यमजामि जाम्योः सचा । घर्मो न वाजजठरोऽदब्धः शश्वतो दभः ॥
5.19.e: I bring, as ’twere, the longed-for milk, the dear milk of the Sister-Pair.  Like to a caldron filled with food is he, unconquered, conquering all.

5.19.d: क्रीळन्नो रश्म आ भुवः सं भस्मना वायुना वेविदानः । ता अस्य सन्धृषजो न तिग्माः सुसंशिता वक्ष्यो वक्षणेस्थाः ॥
5.19.e: Beam of light, come to us in sportive fashion, finding thyself close to the wind that fans thee.  These flames of his are wasting flames, like arrows keen-pointed, sharpened, on his breast.

5.20.d: यमग्ने वाजसातम त्वं चिन्मन्यसे रयिम् । तं नो गीर्भिः श्रवाय्यं देवत्रा पनया युजम् ॥
5.20.e: AGNI, best winner of the spoil, cause us to praise before the Gods  As our associate meet for lauds, wealth which thou verily deemest wealth.

5.20.d: ये अग्ने नेरयन्ति ते वृद्धा उग्रस्य शवसः । अप द्वेषो अप ह्वरोऽन्यव्रतस्य सश्चिरे ॥
5.20.e: Agni, the great who ward not off the anger of thy power and might  Stir up the wrath and hatred due to one who holds an alien creed.

5.20.d: होतारं त्वा वृणीमहेऽग्ने दक्षस्य साधनम् । यज्ञेषु पूर्व्यं गिरा प्रयस्वन्तो हवामहे ॥
5.20.e: Thee, Agni, would we choose as Priest, the perfecter of strength and skill;  We who bring sacred food invoke with song thee Chief at holy rites.

5.20.d: इत्था यथा त ऊतये सहसावन्दिवेदिवे । राय ऋताय सुक्रतो गोभिः ष्याम सधमादो वीरैः स्याम सधमादः ॥
5.20.e: Here as is needful for thine aid we toil, O Conqueror, day by day,  For wealth, for Law. May we rejoice, Most Wise One! at the feast, with kine, rejoice, with heroes, at the feast.

5.21.d: मनुष्वत्त्वा नि धीमहि मनुष्वत्समिधीमहि । अग्ने मनुष्वदङ्गिरो देवान्देवयते यज ॥
5.21.e: WE stablish thee as Manus used, as Manus used we kindle thee.  Like Manus, for the pious man , Aṅgiras, Agni, worship Gods.

5.21.d: त्वं हि मानुषे जनेऽग्ने सुप्रीत इध्यसे । स्रुचस्त्वा यन्त्यानुषक्सुजात सर्पिरासुते ॥
5.21.e: For well, O Agni, art thou pleased when thou art kindled mid mankind.  Straight go the ladles unto thee, thou highborn God whose food is oil.

5.21.d: त्वां विश्वे सजोषसो देवासो दूतमक्रत । सपर्यन्तस्त्वा कवे यज्ञेषु देवमीळते ॥
5.21.e: Thee have all Gods of one accord established as their messenger.  Serving at sacrifices men adore thee as a God, O Sage.

5.21.d: देवं वो देवयज्ययाग्निमीळीत मर्त्यः । समिद्धः शुक्र दीदिह्यृतस्य योनिमासदः ससस्य योनिमासदः ॥
5.21.e: Let mortal man adore your God, Agni, with worship due to Gods.  Shine forth enkindled, Radiant One. Sit in the chamber of the Law, sit in the chamber of the food.

5.22.d: प्र विश्वसामन्नत्रिवदर्चा पावकशोचिषे । यो अध्वरेष्वीड्यो होता मन्द्रतमो विशि ॥
5.22.e: LIKE Atri, Viśvasāman! sing to him of purifying light,  Who must be praised in holy rites, the Priest most welcome in the house.

5.22.d: न्य१ग्निं जातवेदसं दधाता देवमृत्विजम् । प्र यज्ञ एत्वानुषगद्या देवव्यचस्तमः ॥
5.22.e: Set Jātavedas in his place, Agni the God and Minister.  Let sacrifice proceed to-day duly, comprising all the Gods.

5.22.d: चिकित्विन्मनसं त्वा देवं मर्तास ऊतये । वरेण्यस्य तेऽवस इयानासो अमन्महि ॥
5.22.e: All mortals come to thee for aid, the God of most observant mind.  Of thine excelling favour we bethink us as we long for it.

5.22.d: अग्ने चिकिद्ध्य१स्य न इदं वचः सहस्य । तं त्वा सुशिप्र दम्पते स्तोमैर्वर्धन्त्यत्रयो गीर्भिः शुम्भन्त्यत्रयः ॥
5.22.e: Mark with attention this our speech, O Agni, thou victorious One.  Thee, Strong-jawed! as the homestead's Lord, the Atris with their lauds exalt, the Atris beautify with songs.

5.23.d: अग्ने सहन्तमा भर द्युम्नस्य प्रासहा रयिम् । विश्वा यश्चर्षणीरभ्या३सा वाजेषु सासहत् ॥
5.23.e: By thy fair splendour's mighty power, O Agni, bring victorious wealth,  Wealth that o’ercometh all mankind, and, near us, conquereth in fight.

5.23.d: तमग्ने पृतनाषहं रयिं सहस्व आ भर । त्वं हि सत्यो अद्भुतो दाता वाजस्य गोमतः ॥
5.23.e: Victorious Agni, bring to us the wealth that vanquisheth in war;  For thou art wonderful and true, giver of strength in herds of kine.

5.23.d: विश्वे हि त्वा सजोषसो जनासो वृक्तबर्हिषः । होतारं सद्मसु प्रियं व्यन्ति वार्या पुरु ॥
5.23.e: For all the folk with one accord, whose sacred grass is trimmed and strewn,  Invite thee to their worship-halls, as a dear Priest, for choicest wealth.

5.23.d: स हि ष्मा विश्वचर्षणिरभिमाति सहो दधे । अग्न एषु क्षयेष्वा रेवन्नः शुक्र दीदिहि द्युमत्पावक दीदिहि ॥
5.23.e: For he, the God of all men, hath gotten him might that quelleth foes.  O Agni, in these homes shine forth, bright God! for our prosperity, shine, Purifier! splendidly.

5.24.d: अग्ने त्वं नो अन्तम उत त्राता शिवो भवा वरूथ्यः ॥
5.24.e: O AGNI, be our nearest Friend, be thou a kind deliverer and a gracious Friend.

5.24.d: वसुरग्निर्वसुश्रवा अच्छा नक्षि द्युमत्तमं रयिं दाः ॥
5.24.e: Excellent Agni, come thou nigh to us, and give us wealth most splendidly renowned.

5.24.d: स नो बोधि श्रुधी हवमुरुष्या णो अघायतः समस्मात् ॥
5.24.e: So hear us, listen to this call of ours, and keep us far from every sinful man.

5.24.d: तं त्वा शोचिष्ठ दीदिवः सुम्नाय नूनमीमहे सखिभ्यः ॥
5.24.e: To thee then, O Most Bright, O Radiant God, we come with prayer for happiness for our friends.

5.25.d: अच्छा वो अग्निमवसे देवं गासि स नो वसुः । रासत्पुत्र ऋषूणामृतावा पर्षति द्विषः ॥
5.25.e: I WILL sing near, for grace, your God Agni, for he is good to us.  Son of the Brands, may he give gifts, and, righteous, save us from the foe.

5.25.d: स हि सत्यो यं पूर्वे चिद्देवासश्चिद्यमीधिरे । होतारं मन्द्रजिह्वमित्सुदीतिभिर्विभावसुम् ॥
5.25.e: For he is true, whom men of old enkindled, and the Gods themselves,  The Priest with the delicious tongue, rich with the light of glorious beams.

5.25.d: स नो धीती वरिष्ठया श्रेष्ठया च सुमत्या । अग्ने रायो दिदीहि नः सुवृक्तिभिर्वरेण्य ॥
5.25.e: With wisdom that surpasseth all, with gracious will most excellent,  O Agni, worthy of our choice, shine wealth on us through hymns of praise.

5.25.d: अग्निर्देवेषु राजत्यग्निर्मर्तेष्वाविशन् । अग्निर्नो हव्यवाहनोऽग्निं धीभिः सपर्यत ॥
5.25.e: Agni is King, for he extends to mortals and to Gods alike.  Agni is bearer of our gifts. Worship ye Agni with your thoughts.

5.25.d: अग्निस्तुविश्रवस्तमं तुविब्रह्माणमुत्तमम् । अतूर्तं श्रावयत्पतिं पुत्रं ददाति दाशुषे ॥
5.25.e: Agni gives to the worshipper a son, the best, of mightiest fame,  Of deep devotion, ne’er subdued, bringer of glory to his sire.

5.25.d: अग्निर्ददाति सत्पतिं सासाह यो युधा नृभिः । अग्निरत्यं रघुष्यदं जेतारमपराजितम् ॥
5.25.e: Agni bestows the hero-lord who conquers with the men in fight.  Agni bestows the fleet-foot steed, the victor never overcome.

5.25.d: यद्वाहिष्ठं तदग्नये बृहदर्च विभावसो । महिषीव त्वद्रयिस्त्वद्वाजा उदीरते ॥
5.25.e: The mightiest song is Agni's: shine on high, thou who art rich in light.  Like the Chief Consort of a King, riches and strength proceed from thee.

5.25.d: तव द्युमन्तो अर्चयो ग्रावेवोच्यते बृहत् । उतो ते तन्यतुर्यथा स्वानो अर्त त्मना दिवः ॥
5.25.e: Resplendent are thy rays of light: loud is thy voice like pressing-stones.  Yea, of itself thy thunder goes forth like the roaring of the heaven.

5.25.d: एवाँ अग्निं वसूयवः सहसानं ववन्दिम । स नो विश्वा अति द्विषः पर्षन्नावेव सुक्रतुः ॥
5.25.e: Thus, seeking riches, have we paid homage to Agni Conqueror.  May he, most wise, as with a ship, carry us over all our foes.

5.26.d: अग्ने पावक रोचिषा मन्द्रया देव जिह्वया । आ देवान्वक्षि यक्षि च ॥
5.26.e: O AGNI, Holy and Divine, with splendour and thy pleasant tongue  Bring hither and adore the Gods.

5.26.d: तं त्वा घृतस्नवीमहे चित्रभानो स्वर्दृशम् । देवाँ आ वीतये वह ॥
5.26.e: We pray thee, thou who droppest oil, bright-rayed! who lookest on the Sun,  Bring the Gods hither to the feast.

5.26.d: वीतिहोत्रं त्वा कवे द्युमन्तं समिधीमहि । अग्ने बृहन्तमध्वरे ॥
5.26.e: We have enkindled thee, O Sage, bright caller of the Gods to feast.  O Agni, great in Sacrifice.

5.26.d: अग्ने विश्वेभिरा गहि देवेभिर्हव्यदातये । होतारं त्वा वृणीमहे ॥
5.26.e: O Agni, come with all the Gods, come to our sacrificial gift:  We choose thee as Invoking Priest.

5.26.d: यजमानाय सुन्वत आग्ने सुवीर्यं वह । देवैरा सत्सि बर्हिषि ॥
5.26.e: Bring, Agni, to the worshipper who pours the juice, heroic strength:  Sit with the Gods upon the grass.

5.26.d: समिधानः सहस्रजिदग्ने धर्माणि पुष्यसि । देवानां दूत उक्थ्यः ॥
5.26.e: Victor of thousands, Agni, thou, enkindled, cherishest the laws,  Laud-worthy, envoy of the Gods.

5.26.d: न्य१ग्निं जातवेदसं होत्रवाहं यविष्ठ्यम् । दधाता देवमृत्विजम् ॥
5.26.e: Set Agni Jātavedas down, the bearer of our sacred gifts,  MostYouthful, God and Minister.

5.26.d: प्र यज्ञ एत्वानुषगद्या देवव्यचस्तमः । स्तृणीत बर्हिरासदे ॥
5.26.e: Duly proceed our sacrifice, comprising all the Gods, to-day:  Strew holy grass to be their seat.

5.26.d: एदं मरुतो अश्विना मित्रः सीदन्तु वरुणः । देवासः सर्वया विशा ॥
5.26.e: So may the Maruts sit thereon, the Aśvins, Mitra, Varuṇa:  The Gods with all their company.

5.27.d: अनस्वन्ता सत्पतिर्मामहे मे गावा चेतिष्ठो असुरो मघोनः । त्रैवृष्णो अग्ने दशभिः सहस्रैर्वैश्वानर त्र्यरुणश्चिकेत ॥
5.27.e: THE Godlike hero, famousest of nobles, hath granted me two oxen with a wagon.  Trvrsan's son Tryaruna hath distinguished himself, Vaiśvānara Agni! with ten thousands.

5.27.d: यो मे शता च विंशतिं च गोनां हरी च युक्ता सुधुरा ददाति । वैश्वानर सुष्टुतो वावृधानोऽग्ने यच्छ त्र्यरुणाय शर्म ॥
5.27.e: Protect Tryaruna, as thou art waxing strong and art highly praised, Vaiśvānara Agni!  Who granteth me a hundred kine and twenty, and two bay horses, good at draught, and harnessed.

5.27.d: एवा ते अग्ने सुमतिं चकानो नविष्ठाय नवमं त्रसदस्युः । यो मे गिरस्तुविजातस्य पूर्वीर्युक्तेनाभि त्र्यरुणो गृणाति ॥
5.27.e: So Trasadasyu served thee, God Most Youthful, craving thy favour for the ninth time, Agni;  Tryaruya who with attentive spirit accepteth many a song from me the mighty.

5.27.d: यो म इति प्रवोचत्यश्वमेधाय सूरये । दददृचा सनिं यते ददन्मेधामृतायते ॥
5.27.e: He who declares his wish to me, to Asvamedha, to the Prince,  Pays him who with his verse seeks gain, gives power to him who keeps the Law.

5.27.d: यस्य मा परुषाः शतमुद्धर्षयन्त्युक्षणः । अश्वमेधस्य दानाः सोमा इव त्र्याशिरः ॥
5.27.e: From whom a hundred oxen, all of speckled hue, delight my heart,  The gifts of Asvamedha, like thrice-mingled draughts of Soma juice.

5.27.d: इन्द्राग्नी शतदाव्न्यश्वमेधे सुवीर्यम् । क्षत्रं धारयतं बृहद्दिवि सूर्यमिवाजरम् ॥
5.27.e: To Asvamedha who bestows a hundred gifts grant hero power,  O Indra-Agni! lofty rule like the unwasting Sun in heaven.

5.28.d: समिद्धो अग्निर्दिवि शोचिरश्रेत्प्रत्यङ्ङुषसमुर्विया वि भाति । एति प्राची विश्ववारा नमोभिर्देवाँ ईळाना हविषा घृताची ॥
5.28.e: AGNI inflamed hath sent to heaven his lustre: he shines forth widely turning unto Morning.  Eastward the ladle goes that brings all blessing, praising the Godswith homage and oblation.

5.28.d: समिध्यमानो अमृतस्य राजसि हविष्कृण्वन्तं सचसे स्वस्तये । विश्वं स धत्ते द्रविणं यमिन्वस्यातिथ्यमग्ने नि च धत्त इत्पुरः ॥
5.28.e: Enkindled, thou art King of the immortal world: him who brings offerings thou attendest for his weal.  He whom thou urgest on makes all possessions his: he sets before thee, Agni, gifts that guests may claim.

5.28.d: अग्ने शर्ध महते सौभगाय तव द्युम्नान्युत्तमानि सन्तु । सं जास्पत्यं सुयममा कृणुष्व शत्रूयतामभि तिष्ठा महांसि ॥
5.28.e: Show thyself strong for mighty bliss, O Agni, most excellent be thine effulgent splendours.  Make easy to maintain our household lordship, and overcome the might of those who hate us.

5.28.d: समिद्धस्य प्रमहसोऽग्ने वन्दे तव श्रियम् । वृषभो द्युम्नवाँ असि समध्वरेष्विध्यसे ॥
5.28.e: Thy glory, Agni, I adore, kindled, exalted in thy strength.  A Steer of brilliant splendour, thou art lighted well at sacred rites.

5.28.d: समिद्धो अग्न आहुत देवान्यक्षि स्वध्वर । त्वं हि हव्यवाळसि ॥
5.28.e: Agni, invoked and kindled, serve the Gods, thou skilled in sacrifice:  For thou art bearer of our gifts.

5.28.d: आ जुहोता दुवस्यताग्निं प्रयत्यध्वरे । वृणीध्वं हव्यवाहनम् ॥
5.28.e: Invoke and worship Agni while the sacrificial rite proceeds:  For offering-bearer choose ye him.

5.29.d: त्र्यर्यमा मनुषो देवताता त्री रोचना दिव्या धारयन्त । अर्चन्ति त्वा मरुतः पूतदक्षास्त्वमेषामृषिरिन्द्रासि धीरः ॥
5.29.e: MAN'S worship of the Gods hath three great lustres, and three celestial lights have they established  The Maruts gifted with pure strength adore thee, for thou, O Indra, art their sapient Ṛṣi.

5.29.d: अनु यदीं मरुतो मन्दसानमार्चन्निन्द्रं पपिवांसं सुतस्य । आदत्त वज्रमभि यदहिं हन्नपो यह्वीरसृजत्सर्तवा उ ॥
5.29.e: What time the Maruts sang their song to Indra, joyous when he had drunk of Soma juices,  He grasped his thunderbolt to slay the Dragon, and loosed, that they might flow, the youthful Waters.

5.29.d: उत ब्रह्माणो मरुतो मे अस्येन्द्रः सोमस्य सुषुतस्य पेयाः । तद्धि हव्यं मनुषे गा अविन्ददहन्नहिं पपिवाँ इन्द्रो अस्य ॥
5.29.e: And, O ye Brahmans, Maruts, so may Indra drink draughts of this my carefully pressed Soma;  For this oblation found for man the cattle, and Indra, having quaffed it, slew the Dragon.

5.29.d: आद्रोदसी वितरं वि ष्कभायत्संविव्यानश्चिद्भियसे मृगं कः । जिगर्तिमिन्द्रो अपजर्गुराणः प्रति श्वसन्तमव दानवं हन् ॥
5.29.e: Then heaven and earth he sundered and supported: wrapped even in these he struck the Beast with terror.  So Indra forced the Engulfer to disgorgement, and slew the Dānava. panting against him.

5.29.d: अध क्रत्वा मघवन्तुभ्यं देवा अनु विश्वे अददुः सोमपेयम् । यत्सूर्यस्य हरितः पतन्तीः पुरः सतीरुपरा एतशे कः ॥
5.29.e: Thus all the Gods, O Maghavan, delivered to thee of their free will the draught of Soma;  When thou for Etaśa didst cause to tarry the flying mares of Sūrya racing forward.

5.29.d: नव यदस्य नवतिं च भोगान्त्साकं वज्रेण मघवा विवृश्चत् । अर्चन्तीन्द्रं मरुतः सधस्थे त्रैष्टुभेन वचसा बाधत द्याम् ॥
5.29.e: When Maghavan with the thunderbolt demolished his nine-and-ninety castles all together,  The Maruts, where they met, glorified Indra: ye with the Tṛṣṭup hymn obstructed heaven.

5.29.d: सखा सख्ये अपचत्तूयमग्निरस्य क्रत्वा महिषा त्री शतानि । त्री साकमिन्द्रो मनुषः सरांसि सुतं पिबद्वृत्रहत्याय सोमम् ॥
5.29.e: As friend to aid a friend, Agni dressed quickly three hundred buffaloes, even as he willed it.  And Indra, from man's gift, for Vṛtra's slaughter, drank ofr at once three lakes of pressed-out Soma.

5.29.d: त्री यच्छता महिषाणामघो मास्त्री सरांसि मघवा सोम्यापाः । कारं न विश्वे अह्वन्त देवा भरमिन्द्राय यदहिं जघान ॥
5.29.e: When thou three hundred buffaloes' flesh hadst eaten, and drunk, as Maghavan, three lakes of Soma,  All the Gods raised as ’twere a shout of triumph to Indra praise because he slew the Dragon.

5.29.d: उशना यत्सहस्यै३रयातं गृहमिन्द्र जूजुवानेभिरश्वैः । वन्वानो अत्र सरथं ययाथ कुत्सेन देवैरवनोर्ह शुष्णम् ॥
5.29.e: What time ye came with strong steeds swiftly speeding, O Uśanā and Indra, to the dwelling,  Thou camest thither -conquering together with Kutsa and the Gods: thou slewest Śuṣṇa.

5.29.d: प्रान्यच्चक्रमवृहः सूर्यस्य कुत्सायान्यद्वरिवो यातवेऽकः । अनासो दस्यूँरमृणो वधेन नि दुर्योण आवृणङ्मृध्रवाचः ॥
5.29.e: One car-wheel of the Sun thou rolledst forward, and one thou settest free to move for Kutsa.  Thou slewest noseless Dasyus with thy weapon, and in their home o’erthrewest hostile speakers.

5.29.d: स्तोमासस्त्वा गौरिवीतेरवर्धन्नरन्धयो वैदथिनाय पिप्रुम् । आ त्वामृजिश्वा सख्याय चक्रे पचन्पक्तीरपिबः सोममस्य ॥
5.29.e: The lauds of Gauriviti made thee mighty to Vidathin's son, as prey, thou gavest Pipru.  Rjisivan drew thee into friendship dressing the sacred food, and thou hast drunk his Soma.

5.29.d: नवग्वासः सुतसोमास इन्द्रं दशग्वासो अभ्यर्चन्त्यर्कैः । गव्यं चिदूर्वमपिधानवन्तं तं चिन्नरः शशमाना अप व्रन् ॥
5.29.e: Navagvas and Dasgvas with libations of Soma juice sing hymns of praise to Indra.  Labouring at their task the men laid open the stall of Kine though firmly closed and fastened.

5.29.d: कथो नु ते परि चराणि विद्वान्वीर्या मघवन्या चकर्थ । या चो नु नव्या कृणवः शविष्ठ प्रेदु ता ते विदथेषु ब्रवाम ॥
5.29.e: How shall I serve thee, Maghavan, though knowing full well what hero deeds thou hast accomplished?  And the fresh deeds which thou wilt do, Most Mighty! these, too, will we tell forth in sacred synods.

5.29.d: एता विश्वा चकृवाँ इन्द्र भूर्यपरीतो जनुषा वीर्येण । या चिन्नु वज्रिन्कृणवो दधृष्वान्न ते वर्ता तविष्या अस्ति तस्याः ॥
5.29.e: Resistless from of old through hero courage, thou hast done all these many acts, O Indra.  What thou wilt do in bravery, Thunder-wielder! none is there who may hinder this thy prowess.

5.29.d: इन्द्र ब्रह्म क्रियमाणा जुषस्व या ते शविष्ठ नव्या अकर्म । वस्त्रेव भद्रा सुकृता वसूयू रथं न धीरः स्वपा अतक्षम् ॥
5.29.e: Indra, accept the prayers which now are offered, accept the new prayers, Mightiest! which we utter.  Like fair and well-made robes, I, seeking riches, as a deft craftsman makes a car, have wrought them.

5.30.d: क्व१ स्य वीरः को अपश्यदिन्द्रं सुखरथमीयमानं हरिभ्याम् । यो राया वज्री सुतसोममिच्छन्तदोको गन्ता पुरुहूत ऊती ॥
5.30.e: WHERE is that Hero? Who hath looked on Indra borne on light-rolling car by Tawny Coursers,  Who, Thunderer, seeks with wealth the Soma-presser, and to his house goes, much-invoked, to aid him?

5.30.d: अवाचचक्षं पदमस्य सस्वरुग्रं निधातुरन्वायमिच्छन् । अपृच्छमन्याँ उत ते म आहुरिन्द्रं नरो बुबुधाना अशेम ॥
5.30.e: I have beheld his strong and secret dwelling, longing have sought the Founder's habitation.  I asked of others, and they said in answer, May we, awakened men, attain to Indra.

5.30.d: प्र नु वयं सुते या ते कृतानीन्द्र ब्रवाम यानि नो जुजोषः । वेददविद्वाञ्छृणवच्च विद्वान्वहतेऽयं मघवा सर्वसेनः ॥
5.30.e: We will tell, Indra, when we pour libation, what mighty deeds thou hast performed to please us.  Let him who knows not learn, who knows them listen: hither rides Maghavan with all his army.

5.30.d: स्थिरं मनश्चकृषे जात इन्द्र वेषीदेको युधये भूयसश्चित् । अश्मानं चिच्छवसा दिद्युतो वि विदो गवामूर्वमुस्रियाणाम् ॥
5.30.e: Indra, when born, thou madest firm thy spirit: alone thou seekest war to fight with many.  With might thou clavest e’en the rock asunder, and foundest out the stable of the Milch-kine.

5.30.d: परो यत्त्वं परम आजनिष्ठाः परावति श्रुत्यं नाम बिभ्रत् । अतश्चिदिन्द्रादभयन्त देवा विश्वा अपो अजयद्दासपत्नीः ॥
5.30.e: When thou wast born supremest at a distance, bearing a name renowned in far-off regions,  Since then e’en Gods have been afraid of Indra: he conquered all the floods which served the Dāsa.

5.30.d: तुभ्येदेते मरुतः सुशेवा अर्चन्त्यर्कं सुन्वन्त्यन्धः । अहिमोहानमप आशयानं प्र मायाभिर्मायिनं सक्षदिन्द्रः ॥
5.30.e: These blissful Maruts sing their psalm to praise thee, and pour to thee libation of the Soma.  Indra with wondrous powers subdued the Dragon, the guileful lurker who beset the waters.

5.30.d: वि षू मृधो जनुषा दानमिन्वन्नहन्गवा मघवन्त्संचकानः । अत्रा दासस्य नमुचेः शिरो यदवर्तयो मनवे गातुमिच्छन् ॥
5.30.e: Thou, Maghavan, from the first didst scatter foemen, speeding, while joying in the milk, the Giver.  There, seeking man's prosperity, thou torest away the head of Namuci the Dāsa.

5.30.d: युजं हि मामकृथा आदिदिन्द्र शिरो दासस्य नमुचेर्मथायन् । अश्मानं चित्स्वर्यं१ वर्तमानं प्र चक्रियेव रोदसी मरुद्भ्यः ॥
5.30.e: Pounding the head of Namuci the Dāsa, me, too thou madest thine associate, Indra!  Yea, and the rolling stone that is in heaven both worlds, as on a car, brought to the Maruts.

5.30.d: स्त्रियो हि दास आयुधानि चक्रे किं मा करन्नबला अस्य सेनाः । अन्तर्ह्यख्यदुभे अस्य धेने अथोप प्रैद्युधये दस्युमिन्द्रः ॥
5.30.e: Women for weapons hath the Dāsa taken, What injury can his feeble armies To me?  Well he distinguished his two different voices, and Indra then advanced to fight the Dasyu.

5.30.d: समत्र गावोऽभितोऽनवन्तेहेह वत्सैर्वियुता यदासन् । सं ता इन्द्रो असृजदस्य शाकैर्यदीं सोमासः सुषुता अमन्दन् ॥
5.30.e: Divided from their calves the Cows went lowing around, on every side, hither and thither.  These Indra re-united with his helpers, what time the well-pressed Soma made him joyful.

5.30.d: यदीं सोमा बभ्रुधूता अमन्दन्नरोरवीद्वृषभः सादनेषु । पुरंदरः पपिवाँ इन्द्रो अस्य पुनर्गवामददादुस्रियाणाम् ॥
5.30.e: What time the Somas mixed by Babhru cheered him, loud the Steer bellowed in his habitations.  So Indra drank thereof, the Fort-destroyer, and gave him guerdon, in return, of milch-kine.

5.30.d: भद्रमिदं रुशमा अग्ने अक्रन्गवां चत्वारि ददतः सहस्रा । ऋणंचयस्य प्रयता मघानि प्रत्यग्रभीष्म नृतमस्य नृणाम् ॥
5.30.e: This good deed have the Rusamas done, Agni! that they have granted me four thousand cattle.  We have received Rnancaya's wealth, of heroes the most heroic, which was freely offered.

5.30.d: सुपेशसं माव सृजन्त्यस्तं गवां सहस्रै रुशमासो अग्ने । तीव्रा इन्द्रमममन्दुः सुतासोऽक्तोर्व्युष्टौ परितक्म्यायाः ॥
5.30.e: The Rusamas, O Agni, sent me homeward with fair adornment and with kine in thousands.  The strong libations have made Indra joyful, when night, whose course was ending, changed to morning.

5.30.d: औच्छत्सा रात्री परितक्म्या याँ ऋणंचये राजनि रुशमानाम् । अत्यो न वाजी रघुरज्यमानो बभ्रुश्चत्वार्यसनत्सहस्रा ॥
5.30.e: Night, well-nigh ended, at Rnancaya's coming, King of the Rusamas, was changed to morning.  Like a strong courser, fleet of foot, urged onward, Babhru hath gained four thousand as his guerdon.

5.30.d: चतुःसहस्रं गव्यस्य पश्वः प्रत्यग्रभीष्म रुशमेष्वग्ने । घर्मश्चित्तप्तः प्रवृजे य आसीदयस्मयस्तम्वादाम विप्राः ॥
5.30.e: We have received four thousand head of cattle presented by the Rusamas, O Agni.  And we, the singers, have received the caldron of metal which was heated for Pravargya.

5.31.d: इन्द्रो रथाय प्रवतं कृणोति यमध्यस्थान्मघवा वाजयन्तम् । यूथेव पश्वो व्युनोति गोपा अरिष्टो याति प्रथमः सिषासन् ॥
5.31.e: MAGHAVAN Indra turns his chariot downward, the strength-displaying car which he hath mounted.  Even as a herdsman driveth forth his cattle, he goeth, first, uninjured, fain for treasure.

5.31.d: आ प्र द्रव हरिवो मा वि वेनः पिशङ्गराते अभि नः सचस्व । नहि त्वदिन्द्र वस्यो अन्यदस्त्यमेनाँश्चिज्जनिवतश्चकर्थ ॥
5.31.e: Haste to us, Lord of Bays; be not ungracious: visit us, lover of gold-hued oblation.  There is naught else better than thou art, Indra: e’en to the wifeless hast thou given spouses.

5.31.d: उद्यत्सहः सहस आजनिष्ट देदिष्ट इन्द्र इन्द्रियाणि विश्वा । प्राचोदयत्सुदुघा वव्रे अन्तर्वि ज्योतिषा संववृत्वत्तमोऽवः ॥
5.31.e: When out of strength arose the strength that conquers, Indra displayed all powers that he possesses.  Forth from the cave he drove the milky mothers, and with the light laid bare investing darkness.

5.31.d: अनवस्ते रथमश्वाय तक्षन्त्वष्टा वज्रं पुरुहूत द्युमन्तम् । ब्रह्माण इन्द्रं महयन्तो अर्कैरवर्धयन्नहये हन्तवा उ ॥
5.31.e: Anus have wrought a chariot for thy Courser, and Tvaṣṭar, Much-invoked! thy bolt that glitters.  The Brahmans with their songs exalting Indra increased his strength that he might slaughter Ahi.

5.31.d: वृष्णे यत्ते वृषणो अर्कमर्चानिन्द्र ग्रावाणो अदितिः सजोषाः । अनश्वासो ये पवयोऽरथा इन्द्रेषिता अभ्यवर्तन्त दस्यून् ॥
5.31.e: When heroes sang their laud to thee the Hero, Indra! and stones and Aditi accordant,  Without or steed or chariot were the fellies which, sped by Indra, rolled upon the Dasytis.

5.31.d: प्र ते पूर्वाणि करणानि वोचं प्र नूतना मघवन्या चकर्थ । शक्तीवो यद्विभरा रोदसी उभे जयन्नपो मनवे दानुचित्राः ॥
5.31.e: I will declare thine exploits wrought aforetime, and, Maghavan, thy deeds of late achievement,  When, Lord of Might, thou sunderedst earth and heaven, winning for man the moistly-gleaming waters.

5.31.d: तदिन्नु ते करणं दस्म विप्राहिं यद्घ्नन्नोजो अत्रामिमीथाः । शुष्णस्य चित्परि माया अगृभ्णाः प्रपित्वं यन्नप दस्यूँरसेधः ॥
5.31.e: This is thy deed, e’en this, Wonderful! Singer! that, slaying Ahi, here thy strength thou showedst,  Didst check and stay e’en gusna's wiles and magic, and, drawing nigh, didst chase away the Dasytis.

5.31.d: त्वमपो यदवे तुर्वशायारमयः सुदुघाः पार इन्द्र । उग्रमयातमवहो ह कुत्सं सं ह यद्वामुशनारन्त देवाः ॥
5.31.e: Thou, Indra, on the farther bank forYadu and Turvaga didst stay the gushing waters.  Ye both assailed the fierce: thou barest Kutsa: when Gods and Uśanā came to you together.

5.31.d: इन्द्राकुत्सा वहमाना रथेना वामत्या अपि कर्णे वहन्तु । निः षीमद्भ्यो धमथो निः षधस्थान्मघोनो हृदो वरथस्तमांसि ॥
5.31.e: Let the steeds bring you both, Indra and Kutsa, borne on the chariot within hearing-distance.  Ye blew him from the waters, from his dwelling, and chased the darkness from the noble's spirit.

5.31.d: वातस्य युक्तान्त्सुयुजश्चिदश्वान्कविश्चिदेषो अजगन्नवस्युः । विश्वे ते अत्र मरुतः सखाय इन्द्र ब्रह्माणि तविषीमवर्धन् ॥
5.31.e: Even this sage hath come looking for succour even to Vāta's docile harnessed horses.  Here are the Maruts, all, thy dear companions: prayers have increased thy power and might, O Indra.

5.31.d: सूरश्चिद्रथं परितक्म्यायां पूर्वं करदुपरं जूजुवांसम् । भरच्चक्रमेतशः सं रिणाति पुरो दधत्सनिष्यति क्रतुं नः ॥
5.31.e: When night was near its close he carried forward e’en the Sun's chariot backward in its running.  Etaga brought his wheel and firmly stays it: setting it eastward he shall give us courage.

5.31.d: आयं जना अभिचक्षे जगामेन्द्रः सखायं सुतसोममिच्छन् । वदन्ग्रावाव वेदिं भ्रियाते यस्य जीरमध्वर्यवश्चरन्ति ॥
5.31.e: This Indra, O ye men, hath come to see you, seeking a friend who hath expressed the Soma.  The creaking stone is laid upon the altar, and the Adhvaryus come to turn it quickly.

5.31.d: ये चाकनन्त चाकनन्त नू ते मर्ता अमृत मो ते अंह आरन् । वावन्धि यज्यूँरुत तेषु धेह्योजो जनेषु येषु ते स्याम ॥
5.31.e: Let mortals who were happy still be happy; let them not come to sorrow, O Immortal.  Love thou the pious, and to these thy people-with whom may we be numbered-give thou vigour.

5.32.d: अदर्दरुत्समसृजो वि खानि त्वमर्णवान्बद्बधानाँ अरम्णाः । महान्तमिन्द्र पर्वतं वि यद्वः सृजो वि धारा अव दानवं हन् ॥
5.32.e: 1ṬHE well thou clavest, settest free the fountains, and gavest rest to floods that were obstructed.  Thou, Indra, laying the great mountain open, slaying the Dānava, didst loose the torrents.

5.32.d: त्वमुत्साँ ऋतुभिर्बद्बधानाँ अरंह ऊधः पर्वतस्य वज्रिन् । अहिं चिदुग्र प्रयुतं शयानं जघन्वाँ इन्द्र तविषीमधत्थाः ॥
5.32.e: The fountain-depths obstructed in their seasons, thou, Thunderer! madest flow, the mountain's udder.  Strong Indra, thou by slaying e’en the Dragon that lay extended there hast shown thy vigour.

5.32.d: त्यस्य चिन्महतो निर्मृगस्य वधर्जघान तविषीभिरिन्द्रः । य एक इदप्रतिर्मन्यमान आदस्मादन्यो अजनिष्ट तव्यान् ॥
5.32.e: Indra with violence smote down the weapon,  yea, even of that wild and mighty creature.  Although he deemed himself alone unequalled, another had been born e’en yet more potent.

5.32.d: त्यं चिदेषां स्वधया मदन्तं मिहो नपातं सुवृधं तमोगाम् । वृषप्रभर्मा दानवस्य भामं वज्रेण वज्री नि जघान शुष्णम् ॥
5.32.e: Him, whom the heavenly food of these delighted, child of the mist, strong waxing, couched in darkness,  Him the bolt-hurling Thunderer with his lightning smote down and slew, the Dānava's wrath-fire, Śuṣṇa.

5.32.d: त्यं चिदस्य क्रतुभिर्निषत्तममर्मणो विददिदस्य मर्म । यदीं सुक्षत्र प्रभृता मदस्य युयुत्सन्तं तमसि हर्म्ये धाः ॥
5.32.e: Though he might ne’er be wounded still his vitals felt that, the God's bolt, which his powers supported,  When, after offered draughts, Strong Lord, thou laidest him, fain to battle, in the pit in darkness.

5.32.d: त्यं चिदित्था कत्पयं शयानमसूर्ये तमसि वावृधानम् । तं चिन्मन्दानो वृषभः सुतस्योच्चैरिन्द्रो अपगूर्या जघान ॥
5.32.e: Him as he lay there huge in length extended, still waxing in the gloom which no sun lightened,  Him, after loud-voiced threats, the Hero Indra, rejoicing in the poured libation, slaughtered.

5.32.d: उद्यदिन्द्रो महते दानवाय वधर्यमिष्ट सहो अप्रतीतम् । यदीं वज्रस्य प्रभृतौ ददाभ विश्वस्य जन्तोरधमं चकार ॥
5.32.e: When 'gainst the mighty Dānava his weapon Indra uplifted, power which none could combat,  When at the hurling of his bolt he smote him, he made him lower than all living creatures.

5.32.d: त्यं चिदर्णं मधुपं शयानमसिन्वं वव्रं मह्याददुग्रः । अपादमत्रं महता वधेन नि दुर्योण आवृणङ्मृध्रवाचम् ॥
5.32.e: The fierce God seized that huge and restless coiler, insatiate, drinker of the sweets, recumbent,  And with his mighty weapon in his dwelling smote down the footless evil-speaking ogre.

5.32.d: को अस्य शुष्मं तविषीं वरात एको धना भरते अप्रतीतः । इमे चिदस्य ज्रयसो नु देवी इन्द्रस्यौजसो भियसा जिहाते ॥
5.32.e: Who may arrest his strength or cheek his vigour? Alone, resistless, he bears off all riches.  Even these Twain, these Goddesses, through terror of Indra's might, retire from his dominion.

5.32.d: न्यस्मै देवी स्वधितिर्जिहीत इन्द्राय गातुरुशतीव येमे । सं यदोजो युवते विश्वमाभिरनु स्वधाव्ने क्षितयो नमन्त ॥
5.32.e: E’en the Celestial Axe bows down before him, and the Earth, lover-like, gives way to Indra.  As he imparts all vigour to these people, straightway the folk bend them to him the Godlike.

5.32.d: एकं नु त्वा सत्पतिं पाञ्चजन्यं जातं शृणोमि यशसं जनेषु । तं मे जगृभ्र आशसो नविष्ठं दोषा वस्तोर्हवमानास इन्द्रम् ॥
5.32.e: I hear that thou wast born sole Lord of heroes of the Five Races, famed among the people.  As such my wishes have most lately grasped him, invoking Indra both at eve and morning.

5.32.d: एवा हि त्वामृतुथा यातयन्तं मघा विप्रेभ्यो ददतं शृणोमि । किं ते ब्रह्माणो गृहते सखायो ये त्वाया निदधुः काममिन्द्र ॥
5.32.e: So, too, I hear of thee as in due season urging to action and enriching singers.  What have thy friends received from thee, the Brahmans who, faithful, rest their hopes on thee, O Indra?

5.33.d: महि महे तवसे दीध्ये नॄनिन्द्रायेत्था तवसे अतव्यान् । यो अस्मै सुमतिं वाजसातौ स्तुतो जने समर्यश्चिकेत ॥
5.33.e: GREAT praise to Indra, great and strong mid heroes, I ponder thus, the feeble to the Mighty,  Who with his band shows favour to this people, when lauded, in the fight where spoil is gathered.

5.33.d: स त्वं न इन्द्र धियसानो अर्कैर्हरीणां वृषन्योक्त्रमश्रेः । या इत्था मघवन्ननु जोषं वक्षो अभि प्रार्यः सक्षि जनान् ॥
5.33.e: So made attentive by our hymns, Steer! Indra! thou fastenedst the girth of thy Bay Coursers,  Which, Maghavan, at thy will thou drivest hither. With these subdue for us the men who hate us.

5.33.d: न ते त इन्द्राभ्य१स्मदृष्वायुक्तासो अब्रह्मता यदसन् । तिष्ठा रथमधि तं वज्रहस्ता रश्मिं देव यमसे स्वश्वः ॥
5.33.e: They were not turned to us-wtrd, lofty Indra! while yet through lack of prayer they stood unharnessed.  Ascend this chariot, thou whose hand wields thunder, and draw the rein, O Lord of noble horses.

5.33.d: पुरू यत्त इन्द्र सन्त्युक्था गवे चकर्थोर्वरासु युध्यन् । ततक्षे सूर्याय चिदोकसि स्वे वृषा समत्सु दासस्य नाम चित् ॥
5.33.e: Thou, because many lauds are thine, O Indra, wast active warring in the fields  for cattle.  For Sūrya in his own abode thou, Hero, formedst in fights even a Dāsa's nature.

5.33.d: वयं ते त इन्द्र ये च नरः शर्धो जज्ञाना याताश्च रथाः । आस्माञ्जगम्यादहिशुष्म सत्वा भगो न हव्यः प्रभृथेषु चारुः ॥
5.33.e: Thine are we, Indra; thine are all these people, conscious of might, whose cars are set in motion.  Some hero come to us, O Strong as Ahi beauteous in war, to be invoked like Bhaga.

5.33.d: पपृक्षेण्यमिन्द्र त्वे ह्योजो नृम्णानि च नृतमानो अमर्तः । स न एनीं वसवानो रयिं दाः प्रार्यः स्तुषे तुविमघस्य दानम् ॥
5.33.e: Strength much to be desired is in thee, Indra: the Immortal dances forth his hero exploits.  Such, Lord of Treasure, give us splendid riches. I praise the Friend's gift, his whose wealth is mighty.

5.33.d: एवा न इन्द्रोतिभिरव पाहि गृणतः शूर कारून् । उत त्वचं ददतो वाजसातौ पिप्रीहि मध्वः सुषुतस्य चारोः ॥
5.33.e: Thus favour us, O Indra, with ihy succour; Hero, protect the bards who sing thy praises.  Be friendly in the fray to those who offer the skin of beautiful and well-pressed Soma.

5.33.d: उत त्ये मा पौरुकुत्स्यस्य सूरेस्त्रसदस्योर्हिरणिनो रराणाः । वहन्तु मा दश श्येतासो अस्य गैरिक्षितस्य क्रतुभिर्नु सश्चे ॥
5.33.e: And these ten steeds which Trasadasyu gives me, the goldrich chief, the son of Purukutsa,  Resplendent in their brightness shall convey me. Gairiksita willed it and so came I hither.

5.33.d: उत त्ये मा मारुताश्वस्य शोणाः क्रत्वामघासो विदथस्य रातौ । सहस्रा मे च्यवतानो ददान आनूकमर्यो वपुषे नार्चत् ॥
5.33.e: And these, bestowed as sacrificial guerdon, the powerful tawny steeds of Marutasva;  And thousands which kind Cyavatana gave me, abundantly bestowed for my adornment.

5.33.d: उत त्ये मा ध्वन्यस्य जुष्टा लक्ष्मण्यस्य सुरुचो यतानाः । मह्ना रायः संवरणस्य ऋषेर्व्रजं न गावः प्रयता अपि ग्मन् ॥
5.33.e: And these commended horses, bright and active, by Dhvanya son of Laksmana presented,  Came unto me, as cows into the Ṛṣi Samvarana's stall, with magnitude of riches.

5.34.d: अजातशत्रुमजरा स्वर्वत्यनु स्वधामिता दस्ममीयते । सुनोतन पचत ब्रह्मवाहसे पुरुष्टुताय प्रतरं दधातन ॥
5.34.e: BOUNDLESS and wasting not, the heavenly food of Gods goes to the foeless One, doer of wondrous deeds.  Press out, make ready, offer gifts with special zeal to him whom many laud, accepter of the prayer.

5.34.d: आ यः सोमेन जठरमपिप्रतामन्दत मघवा मध्वो अन्धसः । यदीं मृगाय हन्तवे महावधः सहस्रभृष्टिमुशना वधं यमत् ॥
5.34.e: He who filled full his belly with the Soma's juice, Maghavan, was delighted with the meath's sweet draught,  When Uśanā, that he might slay the monstrous beast, gave him the mighty weapon with a thousand points.

5.34.d: यो अस्मै घ्रंस उत वा य ऊधनि सोमं सुनोति भवति द्युमाँ अह । अपाप शक्रस्ततनुष्टिमूहति तनूशुभ्रं मघवा यः कवासखः ॥
5.34.e: Illustrious is the man whoever presseth out Soma for him in sunshine or in cloud and rain.  The mighty Maghavan who is the sage's Friend advanceth more and more his beauteous progeny.

5.34.d: यस्यावधीत्पितरं यस्य मातरं यस्य शक्रो भ्रातरं नात ईषते । वेतीद्वस्य प्रयता यतंकरो न किल्बिषादीषते वस्व आकरः ॥
5.34.e: The Strong God doth not flee away from him whose sire, whose mother or whose brother he hath done to death.  He, the Avenger, seeketh this man's offered gifts: this God, the source of riches, doth not flee from sin.

5.34.d: न पञ्चभिर्दशभिर्वष्ट्यारभं नासुन्वता सचते पुष्यता चन । जिनाति वेदमुया हन्ति वा धुनिरा देवयुं भजति गोमति व्रजे ॥
5.34.e: He seeks no enterprise with five or ten to aid, nor stays with him who pours no juice though prospering well.  The Shaker conquers or slays in this way or that, and to the pious gives a stable full of kine.

5.34.d: वित्वक्षणः समृतौ चक्रमासजोऽसुन्वतो विषुणः सुन्वतो वृधः । इन्द्रो विश्वस्य दमिता विभीषणो यथावशं नयति दासमार्यः ॥
5.34.e: Exceeding strong in war he stays the chariot wheel, and, hating him who pours not, prospers him who pours.  Indra the terrible, tamer of every man, as Ārya leads away the Dāsa at his will.

5.34.d: समीं पणेरजति भोजनं मुषे वि दाशुषे भजति सूनरं वसु । दुर्गे चन ध्रियते विश्व आ पुरु जनो यो अस्य तविषीमचुक्रुधत् ॥
5.34.e: He gathers up for plunder all the niggard’s gear: excellent wealth he gives to him who offers gifts.  Not even in wide stronghold may all the folk stand firm who have provoked to anger his surpassing might.

5.34.d: सं यज्जनौ सुधनौ विश्वशर्धसाववेदिन्द्रो मघवा गोषु शुभ्रिषु । युजं ह्य१न्यमकृत प्रवेपन्युदीं गव्यं सृजते सत्वभिर्धुनिः ॥
5.34.e: When Indra Maghavan hath marked two wealthy men fighting for beauteous cows with all their followers,  He who stirs all things takes one as his close ally, and, Shaker, with his Heroes, sends the kine to him.

5.34.d: सहस्रसामाग्निवेशिं गृणीषे शत्रिमग्न उपमां केतुमर्यः । तस्मा आपः संयतः पीपयन्त तस्मिन्क्षत्रममवत्त्वेषमस्तु ॥
5.34.e: Agni! I laud the liberal Agnivesi, Satri the type and standard of the pious.  May the collected waters yield him plenty, and his be powerful and bright dominion.

5.35.d: यस्ते साधिष्ठोऽवस इन्द्र क्रतुष्टमा भर । अस्मभ्यं चर्षणीसहं सस्निं वाजेषु दुष्टरम् ॥
5.35.e: INDRA, for our assistance bring that most effectual power of thine,  Which conquers men for us, and wins the spoil, invincible in fight.
