5.35.d: यदिन्द्र ते चतस्रो यच्छूर सन्ति तिस्रः । यद्वा पञ्च क्षितीनामवस्तत्सु न आ भर ॥
5.35.e: Indra, whatever aids be thine, four be they, or, O Hero, three,  Or those of the Five Tribes of men, bring quickly all that help to us.

5.35.d: आ तेऽवो वरेण्यं वृषन्तमस्य हूमहे । वृषजूतिर्हि जज्ञिष आभूभिरिन्द्र तुर्वणिः ॥
5.35.e: The aid most excellent of thee the Mightiest hitherward we call,  For thou wast born with hero might, conquering, Indra, with the Strong.

5.35.d: वृषा ह्यसि राधसे जज्ञिषे वृष्णि ते शवः । स्वक्षत्रं ते धृषन्मनः सत्राहमिन्द्र पौंस्यम् ॥
5.35.e: Mighty to prosper us wast thou born, and mighty is the strength thou hast.  In native power thy soul is firm: thy valour, Indra, slays a host.

5.35.d: त्वं तमिन्द्र मर्त्यममित्रयन्तमद्रिवः । सर्वरथा शतक्रतो नि याहि शवसस्पते ॥
5.35.e: O Śatakratu, Lord of Strength, O Indra, Caster of the Stone.  With all thy chariot's force assail the man who shows himself thy foe.

5.35.d: त्वामिद्वृत्रहन्तम जनासो वृक्तबर्हिषः । उग्रं पूर्वीषु पूर्व्यं हवन्ते वाजसातये ॥
5.35.e: For, Mightiest Vṛtra-slayer, thee, fierce, foremost among many, folk  Whose sacred grass is trimmed invite to battle where the spoil is won.

5.35.d: अस्माकमिन्द्र दुष्टरं पुरोयावानमाजिषु । सयावानं धनेधने वाजयन्तमवा रथम् ॥
5.35.e: Indra, do thou protect our car that mingles foremost in the fights,  That bears its part in every fray, invincible and seeking spoil.

5.35.d: अस्माकमिन्द्रेहि नो रथमवा पुरंध्या । वयं शविष्ठ वार्यं दिवि श्रवो दधीमहि दिवि स्तोमं मनामहे ॥
5.35.e: Come to us, Indra, and protect our car with thine intelligence.  May we, O Mightiest One, obtain excellent fame at break of day, and meditate our hymn at dawn.

5.36.d: स आ गमदिन्द्रो यो वसूनां चिकेतद्दातुं दामनो रयीणाम् । धन्वचरो न वंसगस्तृषाणश्चकमानः पिबतु दुग्धमंशुम् ॥
5.36.e: MAY Indra come to us, he who knows rightly to give forth treasures from his store of riches.  Even as a thirsty steer who roams the deserts may he drink eagerly the milked-out Soma.

5.36.d: आ ते हनू हरिवः शूर शिप्रे रुहत्सोमो न पर्वतस्य पृष्ठे । अनु त्वा राजन्नर्वतो न हिन्वन्गीर्भिर्मदेम पुरुहूत विश्वे ॥
5.36.e: Lord of Bay Horses, Hero, may the Soma rise to thy cheeks and jaws like mountain-ridges.  May we, O King, as he who driveth coursers, all joy in thee with hymns, invoked of many!

5.36.d: चक्रं न वृत्तं पुरुहूत वेपते मनो भिया मे अमतेरिदद्रिवः । रथादधि त्वा जरिता सदावृध कुविन्नु स्तोषन्मघवन्पुरूवसुः ॥
5.36.e: Invoked of many, Caster of the Stone my heart quakes like a rolling wheel for fear of penury.  Shall not Puruvasu the singer give thee praise, O ever-prospering Maghavan, mounted on thy car?

5.36.d: एष ग्रावेव जरिता त इन्द्रेयर्ति वाचं बृहदाशुषाणः । प्र सव्येन मघवन्यंसि रायः प्र दक्षिणिद्धरिवो मा वि वेनः ॥
5.36.e: Like the press-stone is this thy praiser, Indra. Loudly he lifts his voice with strong endeavour.  With thy left hand, O Maghavan, give us riches: with thy right, Lord of Bays, be not reluctant.

5.36.d: वृषा त्वा वृषणं वर्धतु द्यौर्वृषा वृषभ्यां वहसे हरिभ्याम् । स नो वृषा वृषरथः सुशिप्र वृषक्रतो वृषा वज्रिन्भरे धाः ॥
5.36.e: May the strong Heaven make thee the Strong wax stronger: Strong, thou art borne by thy two strong Bay Horses.  So, fair of cheek, with mighty chariot, mighty, uphold us, strong-willed, thunderarmed, in battle.

5.36.d: यो रोहितौ वाजिनौ वाजिनीवान्त्रिभिः शतैः सचमानावदिष्ट । यूने समस्मै क्षितयो नमन्तां श्रुतरथाय मरुतो दुवोया ॥
5.36.e: Maruts, let all the people in obeisance bow down before this youthful Srutaratha,  Who, rich in steeds, gave me two dark red horses together with three hundred head of cattle.

5.37.d: सं भानुना यतते सूर्यस्याजुह्वानो घृतपृष्ठः स्वञ्चाः । तस्मा अमृध्रा उषसो व्युच्छान्य इन्द्राय सुनवामेत्याह ॥
5.37.e: BEDEWED with holy oil and meetly worshipped, the Swift One vies with Sūrya's beam in splendour.  For him may mornings dawn without cessation who saith, Let us press Soma out for Indra.

5.37.d: समिद्धाग्निर्वनवत्स्तीर्णबर्हिर्युक्तग्रावा सुतसोमो जराते । ग्रावाणो यस्येषिरं वदन्त्ययदध्वर्युर्हविषाव सिन्धुम् ॥
5.37.e: With kindled fire and strewn grass let him worship, and, Soma-presser, sing with stones adjusted:  And let the priest whose press-stones ring forth loudly, go down with his oblation to the river.

5.37.d: वधूरियं पतिमिच्छन्त्येति य ईं वहाते महिषीमिषिराम् । आस्य श्रवस्याद्रथ आ च घोषात्पुरू सहस्रा परि वर्तयाते ॥
5.37.e: This wife is coming near who loves her husband who carries to his home a vigorous consort.  Here may his car seek fame, here loudly thunder, and his wheel make a thousand revolutions.

5.37.d: न स राजा व्यथते यस्मिन्निन्द्रस्तीव्रं सोमं पिबति गोसखायम् । आ सत्वनैरजति हन्ति वृत्रं क्षेति क्षितीः सुभगो नाम पुष्यन् ॥
5.37.e: No troubles vex that King in whose home Indra drinks the sharp Soma juice with milk commingled.  With heroes he drives near, he slays the foeman: Blest, cherishing that name, he guards his people.

5.37.d: पुष्यात्क्षेमे अभि योगे भवात्युभे वृतौ संयती सं जयाति । प्रियः सूर्ये प्रियो अग्ना भवाति य इन्द्राय सुतसोमो ददाशत् ॥
5.37.e: May he support in peace and win in battle: he masters both the hosts that meet together.  Dear shall he be to Sūrya, dear to Agni, who with pressed Soma offers gifts to India.

5.38.d: उरोष्ट इन्द्र राधसो विभ्वी रातिः शतक्रतो । अधा नो विश्वचर्षणे द्युम्ना सुक्षत्र मंहय ॥
5.38.e: WIDE, Indra Śatakratu, spreads the bounty of thine ample grace:  So, Lord of fair dominion, Friend of all men, give us splendid wealth.

5.38.d: यदीमिन्द्र श्रवाय्यमिषं शविष्ठ दधिषे । पप्रथे दीर्घश्रुत्तमं हिरण्यवर्ण दुष्टरम् ॥
5.38.e: The food which, Mightiest Indra, thou possessest worthy of renown  Is bruited as most widely famed, invincible, O Golden-hued!

5.38.d: शुष्मासो ये ते अद्रिवो मेहना केतसापः । उभा देवावभिष्टये दिवश्च ग्मश्च राजथः ॥
5.38.e: O Darter of the Stone, the powers which readily obey thy will,—  Divinities, both thou and they, ye rule, to guard them, earth and heaven.

5.38.d: उतो नो अस्य कस्य चिद्दक्षस्य तव वृत्रहन् । अस्मभ्यं नृम्णमा भरास्मभ्यं नृमणस्यसे ॥
5.38.e: And from whatever power of thine, O Vṛtra-slayer, it may be,  Bring thou to us heroic strength: thou hast a man's regard for us.

5.38.d: नू त आभिरभिष्टिभिस्तव शर्मञ्छतक्रतो । इन्द्र स्याम सुगोपाः शूर स्याम सुगोपाः ॥
5.38.e: In thy protection, with these aids of thine, O Lord of Hundred Powers,  Indra, may we be guarded well, Hero, may we be guarded well.

5.39.d: यदिन्द्र चित्र मेहनास्ति त्वादातमद्रिवः । राधस्तन्नो विदद्वस उभयाहस्त्या भर ॥
5.39.e: STONE-DARTING Indra. Wondrous One, what wealth is richly given from thee,  That bounty, Treasure-Finder! bring filling both thy hands, to us.

5.39.d: यन्मन्यसे वरेण्यमिन्द्र द्युक्षं तदा भर । विद्याम तस्य ते वयमकूपारस्य दावने ॥
5.39.e: Bring what thou deemest worth the wish, O Indra, that which is in heaven.  So may we know thee as thou art, boundless in thy munificence.

5.39.d: यत्ते दित्सु प्रराध्यं मनो अस्ति श्रुतं बृहत् । तेन दृळ्हा चिदद्रिव आ वाजं दर्षि सातये ॥
5.39.e: Thy lofty spirit, far-renowned as fain to give and prompt to win,—  With this thou rendest e’en the firm, Stone-Darter! so to gain thee strength.

5.39.d: मंहिष्ठं वो मघोनां राजानं चर्षणीनाम् । इन्द्रमुप प्रशस्तये पूर्वीभिर्जुजुषे गिरः ॥
5.39.e: Singers with many songs have made Indra propitious to their fame,  Him who is King of human kind, most liberal of your wealthy ones.

5.39.d: अस्मा इत्काव्यं वच उक्थमिन्द्राय शंस्यम् । तस्मा उ ब्रह्मवाहसे गिरो वर्धन्त्यत्रयो गिरः शुम्भन्त्यत्रयः ॥
5.39.e: To him, to Indra must be sung the poet's word, the hymn of praise.  To him, accepter of the prayer, the Atris raise their songs on high, the Atris beautify their songs.

5.40.d: आ याह्यद्रिभिः सुतं सोमं सोमपते पिब । वृषन्निन्द्र वृषभिर्वृत्रहन्तम ॥
5.40.e: COME thou to what the stones have pressed, drink Soma, O thou Soma's Lord,  Indra best Vṛtra-slayer Strong One, with the Strong.

5.40.d: वृषा ग्रावा वृषा मदो वृषा सोमो अयं सुतः । वृषन्निन्द्र वृषभिर्वृत्रहन्तम ॥
5.40.e: Strong is the stone, the draught is strong, strong is this Soma that is pressed,  Indra, best Vṛtra-slayer, Strong One with the Strong.

5.40.d: वृषा त्वा वृषणं हुवे वज्रिञ्चित्राभिरूतिभिः । वृषन्निन्द्र वृषभिर्वृत्रहन्तम ॥
5.40.e: As strong I call on thee the Strong, O Thunder-armed, with various aids,  Indra, best Vṛtra-slayer, Strong One with the Strong.

5.40.d: ऋजीषी वज्री वृषभस्तुराषाट् छुष्मी राजा वृत्रहा सोमपावा । युक्त्वा हरिभ्यामुप यासदर्वाङ्माध्यंदिने सवने मत्सदिन्द्रः ॥
5.40.e: Impetuous, Thunderer, Strong, quelling the mighty, King, potent, Vṛtra-slayer, Soma-drinker,  May he come hither with his yoked Bay Horses; may Indra gladden him at the noon libation.

5.40.d: यत्त्वा सूर्य स्वर्भानुस्तमसाविध्यदासुरः । अक्षेत्रविद्यथा मुग्धो भुवनान्यदीधयुः ॥
5.40.e: O Sūrya, when the Asura's descendant Svarbhanu, pierced thee through and through with darkness,  All creatures looked like one who is bewildered, who knoweth not the place where he is standing.

5.40.d: स्वर्भानोरध यदिन्द्र माया अवो दिवो वर्तमाना अवाहन् । गूळ्हं सूर्यं तमसापव्रतेन तुरीयेण ब्रह्मणाविन्ददत्रिः ॥
5.40.e: What time thou smotest down Svarbhanu's magic that spread itself beneath the sky, O Indra,  By his fourth sacred prayer Atri disoovered Sūrya concealed in gloom that stayed his function.

5.40.d: मा मामिमं तव सन्तमत्र इरस्या द्रुग्धो भियसा नि गारीत् । त्वं मित्रो असि सत्यराधास्तौ मेहावतं वरुणश्च राजा ॥
5.40.e: Let not the oppressor with this dread, through anger swallow me up, for I am thine, O Atri.  Mitra art thou, the sender of true blessings: thou and King Varuṇa be both my helpers.

5.40.d: ग्राव्णो ब्रह्मा युयुजानः सपर्यन्कीरिणा देवान्नमसोपशिक्षन् । अत्रिः सूर्यस्य दिवि चक्षुराधात्स्वर्भानोरप माया अघुक्षत् ॥
5.40.e: The Brahman Atri, as he set the press-stones, serving the Gods with praise and adoration,  Established in the heaven the eye of Sūrya, and caused Svarbhanu's magic arts to vanish.

5.40.d: यं वै सूर्यं स्वर्भानुस्तमसाविध्यदासुरः । अत्रयस्तमन्वविन्दन्नह्य१न्ये अशक्नुवन् ॥
5.40.e: The Atris found the Sun again, him whom Svarbhanu of the brood  Of Asuras had pierced with gloom. This none besides had power to do.

5.41.d: को नु वां मित्रावरुणावृतायन्दिवो वा महः पार्थिवस्य वा दे । ऋतस्य वा सदसि त्रासीथां नो यज्ञायते वा पशुषो न वाजान् ॥
5.41.e: WHO, Mitra-Varuṇa, is your pious servant to give you gifts from earth or mighty heaven?  Preserve us in the seat of holy Order, and give the offerer power that winneth cattle.

5.41.d: ते नो मित्रो वरुणो अर्यमायुरिन्द्र ऋभुक्षा मरुतो जुषन्त । नमोभिर्वा ये दधते सुवृक्तिं स्तोमं रुद्राय मीळ्हुषे सजोषाः ॥
5.41.e: May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, and Āyu, Indra Ṛbhukṣan, and the Maruts, love us,  And they who of one mind with bounteous Rudra accept the hymn and laud with adorations.

5.41.d: आ वां येष्ठाश्विना हुवध्यै वातस्य पत्मन्रथ्यस्य पुष्टौ । उत वा दिवो असुराय मन्म प्रान्धांसीव यज्यवे भरध्वम् ॥
5.41.e: You will I call to feed the car-horse, Aśvins, with the wind's flight swiftest of those who travel:  Or also to the Asura of heaven, Worshipful, bring a hymn as ’twere libation.

5.41.d: प्र सक्षणो दिव्यः कण्वहोता त्रितो दिवः सजोषा वातो अग्निः । पूषा भगः प्रभृथे विश्वभोजा आजिं न जग्मुराश्वश्वतमाः ॥
5.41.e: The heavenly Victor, he whose priest is Kaṇva, Tṛta with Dyaus accordant, Vāta, Agni,  All-feeding Pūṣan, Bhaga sought the oblation, as they whose steeds are fleetest seek the contest.

5.41.d: प्र वो रयिं युक्ताश्वं भरध्वं राय एषेऽवसे दधीत धीः । सुशेव एवैरौशिजस्य होता ये व एवा मरुतस्तुराणाम् ॥
5.41.e: Bring ye your riches forward borne on horses: let thought be framed for help and gain of treasure.  Blest he the priest of Auśija through courses, the courses which are yours the fleet, O Maruts.

5.41.d: प्र वो वायुं रथयुजं कृणुध्वं प्र देवं विप्रं पनितारमर्कैः । इषुध्यव ऋतसापः पुरंधीर्वस्वीर्नो अत्र पत्नीरा धिये धुः ॥
5.41.e: Bring hither him who yokes the car, your Vāyu, who praises with his songs, the God and Singer;  And, praying and devout, noble and prudent, may the Gods’ Spouses in their thoughts retain us.

5.41.d: उप व एषे वन्द्येभिः शूषैः प्र यह्वी दिवश्चितयद्भिरर्कैः । उषासानक्ता विदुषीव विश्वमा हा वहतो मर्त्याय यज्ञम् ॥
5.41.e: I speed to you with powers that should be honoured, with songs distinguishing Heaven's mighty Daughters,  Morning and Night, the Two, as ’twere all-knowing: these bring the sacrifice unto the mortal.

5.41.d: अभि वो अर्चे पोष्यावतो नॄन्वास्तोष्पतिं त्वष्टारं रराणः । धन्या सजोषा धिषणा नमोभिर्वनस्पतीँरोषधी राय एषे ॥
5.41.e: You I extol, the nourishers of heroes bringing you gifts, Vastospati and Tvaṣṭar-  Rich Dhiṣaṇā accords through our obeisance - andTrees and Plants, for the swift gain of riches.

5.41.d: तुजे नस्तने पर्वताः सन्तु स्वैतवो ये वसवो न वीराः । पनित आप्त्यो यजतः सदा नो वर्धान्नः शंसं नर्यो अभिष्टौ ॥
5.41.e: Ours be the Parvatas, even they, for offspring, free-moving, who are Heroes like the Vasus.  May holy Āptya, Friend of man, exalted, strengthen our word for ever and be near us.

5.41.d: वृष्णो अस्तोषि भूम्यस्य गर्भं त्रितो नपातमपां सुवृक्ति । गृणीते अग्निरेतरी न शूषैः शोचिष्केशो नि रिणाति वना ॥
5.41.e: Tṛta praised him, germ of the earthly hero, with pure songs him the Offspring of the Waters.  Agn; with might neighs loudly like a charger: he of the flaming hair destroys the forests.

5.41.d: कथा महे रुद्रियाय ब्रवाम कद्राये चिकितुषे भगाय । आप ओषधीरुत नोऽवन्तु द्यौर्वना गिरयो वृक्षकेशाः ॥
5.41.e: How shall we speak to the great might of Rudra? How speak to Bhaga who takes thought for riches?  May Plants, the Waters, and the Sky preserve us, and Woods and Mountains with their trees for tresses.

5.41.d: शृणोतु न ऊर्जां पतिर्गिरः स नभस्तरीयाँ इषिरः परिज्मा । शृण्वन्त्वापः पुरो न शुभ्राः परि स्रुचो बबृहाणस्याद्रेः ॥
5.41.e: May the swift Wanderer, Lord of refreshments listen to our songs, who speeds throuih cloudy heaven:  And may the Waters, bright like castles, hear us, as they flow onward from the cloven mountain.

5.41.d: विदा चिन्नु महान्तो ये व एवा ब्रवाम दस्मा वार्यं दधानाः । वयश्चन सुभ्व१ आव यन्ति क्षुभा मर्तमनुयतं वधस्नैः ॥
5.41.e: We know your ways, ye Mighty Ones receiving choice meed, ye Wonderful, we will proclaim it.  Even strong birds descend not to the mortal who strives to reach them with swift blow and weapons.

5.41.d: आ दैव्यानि पार्थिवानि जन्मापश्चाच्छा सुमखाय वोचम् । वर्धन्तां द्यावो गिरश्चन्द्राग्रा उदा वर्धन्तामभिषाता अर्णाः ॥
5.41.e: Celestial and terrestrial generations, and Waters will I summon to the feasting.  May days with bright dawns cause my songs to prosper, and may the conquered streams increase their waters.

5.41.d: पदेपदे मे जरिमा नि धायि वरूत्री वा शक्रा या पायुभिश्च । सिषक्तु माता मही रसा नः स्मत्सूरिभिर्ऋजुहस्त ऋजुवनिः ॥
5.41.e: Duly to each one hath my laud been offered. Strong be Varūtrī with her powers to succour.  May the great Mother Rasā here befriend us, straight-handed, with the princes, striving forward.

5.41.d: कथा दाशेम नमसा सुदानूनेवया मरुतो अच्छोक्तौ प्रश्रवसो मरुतो अच्छोक्तौ । मा नोऽहिर्बुध्न्यो रिषे धादस्माकं भूदुपमातिवनिः ॥
5.41.e: How may we serve the Liberal Ones with worship, the Maruts swift of course in invocation, the Maruts far-renowned in invocation?  Let not the Dragon of the Deep annoy us, and gladly may he welcome our addresses.

5.41.d: इति चिन्नु प्रजायै पशुमत्यै देवासो वनते मर्त्यो व आ देवासो वनते मर्त्यो वः । अत्रा शिवां तन्वो धासिमस्या जरां चिन्मे निर्ऋतिर्जग्रसीत ॥
5.41.e: Thus thinking, O ye Gods, the mortal wins you to give him increase of his herds of cattle: the mortal wins him, O ye Gods, your favour.  Here he wins wholesome food to feed this body: as for mine old age, Nirrti consume it

5.41.d: तां वो देवाः सुमतिमूर्जयन्तीमिषमश्याम वसवः शसा गोः । सा नः सुदानुर्मृळयन्ती देवी प्रति द्रवन्ती सुविताय गम्याः ॥
5.41.e: O Gods, may we obtain from you this favour, strengthening food through the Cow's praise, ye Vasus.  May she who gives good gifts, the gracious Goddes. s, come speeding nigh to us for our well-being.

5.41.d: अभि न इळा यूथस्य माता स्मन्नदीभिरुर्वशी वा गृणातु । उर्वशी वा बृहद्दिवा गृणानाभ्यूर्ण्वाना प्रभृथस्यायोः ॥
5.41.e: May Iḷā, Mother of the herds of cattle, and Urvasi with all the streams accept us;  May Urvasi in lofty heaven accepting, as she partakes the oblation of the living,

5.41.d: सिषक्तु न ऊर्जव्यस्य पुष्टेः ॥
5.41.e: Visit us while she shares Urjavya's food.

5.42.d: प्र शंतमा वरुणं दीधिती गीर्मित्रं भगमदितिं नूनमश्याः । पृषद्योनिः पञ्चहोता शृणोत्वतूर्तपन्था असुरो मयोभुः ॥
5.42.e: Now may our sweetest song with deep devotion reach Varuṇa, Mitra, Aditi, and Bhaga.  May the Five Priests' Lord, dwelling in oblations, bliss-giving Asura, hear, whose paths are open.

5.42.d: प्रति मे स्तोममदितिर्जगृभ्यात्सूनुं न माता हृद्यं सुशेवम् । ब्रह्म प्रियं देवहितं यदस्त्यहं मित्रे वरुणे यन्मयोभु ॥
5.42.e: May Aditi welcome, even as a mother her dear heart-gladdening son, my song that lauds her.  The prayer they love, bliss-giving, God-appointed, I offer unto Varuṇa and Mitra.

5.42.d: उदीरय कवितमं कवीनामुनत्तैनमभि मध्वा घृतेन । स नो वसूनि प्रयता हितानि चन्द्राणि देवः सविता सुवाति ॥
5.42.e: In spirit him, the Sagest of the Sages; with sacrificial oil and meath bedew him  So then let him, God Savitar, provide us excellent, ready, and resplendent treasures.

5.42.d: समिन्द्र णो मनसा नेषि गोभिः सं सूरिभिर्हरिवः सं स्वस्ति । सं ब्रह्मणा देवहितं यदस्ति सं देवानां सुमत्या यज्ञियानाम् ॥
5.42.e: With willing mind, Indra, vouchsafe us cattle, prosperity, Lord of Bays! and pious patrons;  And, with the sacred prayer by Gods appointed, give us the holy Deities' lovingkindness.

5.42.d: देवो भगः सविता रायो अंश इन्द्रो वृत्रस्य संजितो धनानाम् । ऋभुक्षा वाज उत वा पुरंधिरवन्तु नो अमृतासस्तुरासः ॥
5.42.e: God Bhaga, Savitar who deals forth riches, Indra, and they who conquer Vṛtra's treasures,  And Vāja and Ṛbhukṣan and Purandhi, the Mighty and Immortal Ones, protect us!

5.42.d: मरुत्वतो अप्रतीतस्य जिष्णोरजूर्यतः प्र ब्रवामा कृतानि । न ते पूर्वे मघवन्नापरासो न वीर्यं१ नूतनः कश्चनाप ॥
5.42.e: Let us declare his deeds, the undecaying unrivalled Victor whom the Maruts follow.  None of old times, O Maghavan, nor later, none of these days hath reached thy hero prowess.

5.42.d: उप स्तुहि प्रथमं रत्नधेयं बृहस्पतिं सनितारं धनानाम् । यः शंसते स्तुवते शम्भविष्ठः पुरूवसुरागमज्जोहुवानम् ॥
5.42.e: Praise him the Chief who gives the boon of riches, Bṛhaspati distributor of treasures,  Who, blessing most the man who sings and praises, comes with abundant wealth to his invoker.

5.42.d: तवोतिभिः सचमाना अरिष्टा बृहस्पते मघवानः सुवीराः । ये अश्वदा उत वा सन्ति गोदा ये वस्त्रदाः सुभगास्तेषु रायः ॥
5.42.e: Tended, Bṛhaspati, with thy protections, the princes are unharmed and girt by heroes.  Wealth that brings bliss is found among the givers of horses and of cattle and of raiment.

5.42.d: विसर्माणं कृणुहि वित्तमेषां ये भुञ्जते अपृणन्तो न उक्थैः । अपव्रतान्प्रसवे वावृधानान्ब्रह्मद्विषः सूर्याद्यावयस्व ॥
5.42.e: Make their wealth flee who, through our hymns enjoying their riches, yield us not an ample guerdon.  Far from the sun keep those who hate devotion, the godless, prospering in their vocation.

5.42.d: य ओहते रक्षसो देववीतावचक्रेभिस्तं मरुतो नि यात । यो वः शमीं शशमानस्य निन्दात्तुच्छ्यान्कामान्करते सिष्विदानः ॥
5.42.e: With wheelless chariots drive down him, O Maruts, who at the feasts of Gods regards the demons.  May he, though bathed in sweat, form empty wishes, who blames his sacred rite who toils to serve you.

5.42.d: तमु ष्टुहि यः स्विषुः सुधन्वा यो विश्वस्य क्षयति भेषजस्य । यक्ष्वा महे सौमनसाय रुद्रं नमोभिर्देवमसुरं दुवस्य ॥
5.42.e: Praise him whose bow is strong and sure his arrow, him who is Lord of every balm that bealeth.  Worship thou Rudra for his great good favour: adore the Asura, God, with salutations.

5.42.d: दमूनसो अपसो ये सुहस्ता वृष्णः पत्नीर्नद्यो विभ्वतष्टाः । सरस्वती बृहद्दिवोत राका दशस्यन्तीर्वरिवस्यन्तु शुभ्राः ॥
5.42.e: May the House-friends, the cunning-handed Artists, may the Steer's Wives, the streams carved out by Vibhvan,  And may the fair Ones honour and befriend us, Sarasvatī, Brhaddiva, and Rākā.

5.42.d: प्र सू महे सुशरणाय मेधां गिरं भरे नव्यसीं जायमानाम् । य आहना दुहितुर्वक्षणासु रूपा मिनानो अकृणोदिदं नः ॥
5.42.e: My newest song, thought that now springs within me, I offer to the Great, the Sure Protector,  Who made for us this All, in fond love laying each varied form within his Daughter's bosom.

5.42.d: प्र सुष्टुतिः स्तनयन्तं रुवन्तमिळस्पतिं जरितर्नूनमश्याः । यो अब्दिमाँ उदनिमाँ इयर्ति प्र विद्युता रोदसी उक्षमाणः ॥
5.42.e: Now, even now, may thy fair praise, O Singer, attain Idaspati who roars and thunders,  Who, rich in clouds and waters with his lightning speeds forth bedewing both the earth and heaven.

5.42.d: एष स्तोमो मारुतं शर्धो अच्छा रुद्रस्य सूनूँर्युवन्यूँरुदश्याः । कामो राये हवते मा स्वस्त्युप स्तुहि पृषदश्वाँ अयासः ॥
5.42.e: May this my laud attain the troop of Maruts, those who are youths in act, the Sons of Rudra.  The wish calls me to riches and well-being: praise the unwearied Ones whose steeds are dappled.

5.42.d: प्रैष स्तोमः पृथिवीमन्तरिक्षं वनस्पतीँरोषधी राये अश्याः । देवोदेवः सुहवो भूतु मह्यं मा नो माता पृथिवी दुर्मतौ धात् ॥
5.42.e: May this my laud reach earth and air's mid-region, and forest trees and plants to win me riches.  May every Deity be swift to listen, and Mother Earth with no ill thought regard me.
Gods, may we dwell in free untroubled bliss.

5.42.d: समश्विनोरवसा नूतनेन मयोभुवा सुप्रणीती गमेम । आ नो रयिं वहतमोत वीराना विश्वान्यमृता सौभगानि ॥
5.42.e: May we obtain the Aśvins' newest favour, and gain their health-bestowing happy guidance.  Bring riches hither unto us, and heroes, and all felicity and joy, Immortals!

5.43.d: आ धेनवः पयसा तूर्ण्यर्था अमर्धन्तीरुप नो यन्तु मध्वा । महो राये बृहतीः सप्त विप्रो मयोभुवो जरिता जोहवीति ॥
5.43.e: MAY the Milch-cows who hasten to their object come harmless unto us with liquid sweetness.  The Singer, lauding, calls, for ample riches, the Seven Mighty Ones who bring enjoyment.

5.43.d: आ सुष्टुती नमसा वर्तयध्यै द्यावा वाजाय पृथिवी अमृध्रे । पिता माता मधुवचाः सुहस्ता भरेभरे नो यशसावविष्टाम् ॥
5.43.e: With reverence and fair praise will I bring hither, for sake of strength, exhaustless Earth and Heaven.  Father and Mother, sweetof speech, fairhanded, may they, far-famed, in every fight protect us.

5.43.d: अध्वर्यवश्चकृवांसो मधूनि प्र वायवे भरत चारु शुक्रम् । होतेव नः प्रथमः पाह्यस्य देव मध्वो ररिमा ते मदाय ॥
5.43.e: Adhvaryus, make the sweet libations ready, and bring the beautiful bright juice to Vāyu.  God, as our Priest, be thou the first to drink it: we give thee of the mead to make thee joyful.

5.43.d: दश क्षिपो युञ्जते बाहू अद्रिं सोमस्य या शमितारा सुहस्ता । मध्वो रसं सुगभस्तिर्गिरिष्ठां चनिश्चदद्दुदुहे शुक्रमंशुः ॥
5.43.e: Two arms-the Soma's dexterous immo. lators-and the ten fingers set and fix the press-stone.  The stalk hath poured, fair with its spreading branches, the mead's bright glittering juice that dwells on mountains.

5.43.d: असावि ते जुजुषाणाय सोमः क्रत्वे दक्षाय बृहते मदाय । हरी रथे सुधुरा योगे अर्वागिन्द्र प्रिया कृणुहि हूयमानः ॥
5.43.e: The Soma hath been pressed for thee, its lover, to give thee power and might and high enjoyment.  Invoked, turn hither in thy car, O Indra, at need, thy two well-trained and dear Bay Horses.

5.43.d: आ नो महीमरमतिं सजोषा ग्नां देवीं नमसा रातहव्याम् । मधोर्मदाय बृहतीमृतज्ञामाग्ने वह पथिभिर्देवयानैः ॥
5.43.e: Bring by God-traversed paths, accordant, Agni, the great Aramati, Celestial Lady,  Exalted, worshipped with our gifts and homage, who knoweth holy Law, to drink sweet Soma.

5.43.d: अञ्जन्ति यं प्रथयन्तो न विप्रा वपावन्तं नाग्निना तपन्तः । पितुर्न पुत्र उपसि प्रेष्ठ आ घर्मो अग्निमृतयन्नसादि ॥
5.43.e: As on his father's lap the son, the darling, so on the fire is set the sacred caldron,  Which holy singers deck, as if extending and heating that which holds the fatty membrane.

5.43.d: अच्छा मही बृहती शंतमा गीर्दूतो न गन्त्वश्विना हुवध्यै । मयोभुवा सरथा यातमर्वाग्गन्तं निधिं धुरमाणिर्न नाभिम् ॥
5.43.e: Hither, as herald to invite the Aśvins, come the great lofty song, most sweet and pleasant!  Come in one car, joy-givers! to the banquet, like the bolt binding pole and nave, come hither.

5.43.d: प्र तव्यसो नमउक्तिं तुरस्याहं पूष्ण उत वायोरदिक्षि । या राधसा चोदितारा मतीनां या वाजस्य द्रविणोदा उत त्मन् ॥
5.43.e: I have declared this speech of adoration to mightiest Pūṣan and victorious Vāyu,  Who by their bounty are the hymns' inspirers, and of themselves give power as a possession.

5.43.d: आ नामभिर्मरुतो वक्षि विश्वाना रूपेभिर्जातवेदो हुवानः । यज्ञं गिरो जरितुः सुष्टुतिं च विश्वे गन्त मरुतो विश्व ऊती ॥
5.43.e: Invoked by us bring hither, jatavedas the Maruts all under their names and figures.  Come to the sacrifice with aid all Maruts, all to the songs and praises of the singer!

5.43.d: आ नो दिवो बृहतः पर्वतादा सरस्वती यजता गन्तु यज्ञम् । हवं देवी जुजुषाणा घृताची शग्मां नो वाचमुशती शृणोतु ॥
5.43.e: From high heaven may Sarasvatī the Holy visit our sacrifice, and from the mountain.  Eager, propitious, may the balmy Goddess hear our effectual speech, our invocation.

5.43.d: आ वेधसं नीलपृष्ठं बृहन्तं बृहस्पतिं सदने सादयध्वम् । सादद्योनिं दम आ दीदिवांसं हिरण्यवर्णमरुषं सपेम ॥
5.43.e: Set in his seat the God whose back is dusky, Bṛhaspati the lofty, the Disposer.  Him let us worship, set within the dwelling, the red, the golden-hued, the allresplendent.

5.43.d: आ धर्णसिर्बृहद्दिवो रराणो विश्वेभिर्गन्त्वोमभिर्हुवानः । ग्ना वसान ओषधीरमृध्रस्त्रिधातुशृङ्गो वृषभो वयोधाः ॥
5.43.e: May the Sustainer, high in heaven, come hither, the Bounteous One, invoked, with all his favours,  Dweller with Dames divine, with plants, unwearied, the Steer with triple horn, the life-bestower.

5.43.d: मातुष्पदे परमे शुक्र आयोर्विपन्यवो रास्पिरासो अग्मन् । सुशेव्यं नमसा रातहव्याः शिशुं मृजन्त्यायवो न वासे ॥
5.43.e: The tuneful eloquent priests of him who liveth have sought the Mother's bright and loftiest station.  As living men, with offered gifts and homage they deck the most auspicious Child to clothe him.

5.43.d: बृहद्वयो बृहते तुभ्यमग्ने धियाजुरो मिथुनासः सचन्त । देवोदेवः सुहवो भूतु मह्यं मा नो माता पृथिवी दुर्मतौ धात् ॥
5.43.e: Agni, great vital power is thine, the mighty: pairs waxing old in their devotion seek thee.  May every Deity be swift to listen, and Mother Earth with no ill thought regard me.
Gods, may we dwell in free untroubled bliss.

5.43.d: समश्विनोरवसा नूतनेन मयोभुवा सुप्रणीती गमेम । आ नो रयिं वहतमोत वीराना विश्वान्यमृता सौभगानि ॥
5.43.e: May we obtain the Aśvins' newest favour, and gain their health-bestowing happy guidance.  Bring riches hither unto us, and heroes, and all felicity and joy, Immortals!

5.44.d: तं प्रत्नथा पूर्वथा विश्वथेमथा ज्येष्ठतातिं बर्हिषदं स्वर्विदम् । प्रतीचीनं वृजनं दोहसे गिराशुं जयन्तमनु यासु वर्धसे ॥
5.44.e: As in the first old times, as all were wont, as now, he draweth forth the power turned hitherward with song,  The Princedom throned on holy grass, who findeth light, swift, conquering in the' plants wherein he waxeth strong.

5.44.d: श्रिये सुदृशीरुपरस्य याः स्वर्विरोचमानः ककुभामचोदते । सुगोपा असि न दभाय सुक्रतो परो मायाभिर्ऋत आस नाम ते ॥
5.44.e: Shining to him who leaves heaven's regions undisturbed, which to his sheen who is beneath show fair in light,  Good guardian art thou, not to be deceived, Most Wise! Far from deceits thy name dwelleth in holy Law.

5.44.d: अत्यं हविः सचते सच्च धातु चारिष्टगातुः स होता सहोभरिः । प्रसर्स्राणो अनु बर्हिर्वृषा शिशुर्मध्ये युवाजरो विस्रुहा हितः ॥
5.44.e: Truth waits upon oblation present and to come: naught checks him in his way, this vic tory- bringing Priest:  The Mighty Child who glides along the sacred grass, the undecaying Youth set in the midst of plants.

5.44.d: प्र व एते सुयुजो यामन्निष्टये नीचीरमुष्मै यम्य ऋतावृधः । सुयन्तुभिः सर्वशासैरभीशुभिः क्रिविर्नामानि प्रवणे मुषायति ॥
5.44.e: These come, well-yoked, to you for furtherance in the rite: down come the twinborn strengtheners of Law for him,  With reins easily guided and commanding all. In the deep fall the hide stealeth away their names.

5.44.d: संजर्भुराणस्तरुभिः सुतेगृभं वयाकिनं चित्तगर्भासु सुस्वरुः । धारवाकेष्वृजुगाथ शोभसे वर्धस्व पत्नीरभि जीवो अध्वरे ॥
5.44.e: Thou, moving beauteously in visibly pregnant ones, snatching with trees the branching plant that grasps the juice,  Shinest, true Singer! mid the upholders of the voice. Increase thy Consorts thou, lively at sacrifice.

5.44.d: यादृगेव ददृशे तादृगुच्यते सं छायया दधिरे सिध्रयाप्स्वा । महीमस्मभ्यमुरुषामुरु ज्रयो बृहत्सुवीरमनपच्युतं सहः ॥
5.44.e: Like as he is beheld such is he said to be.  They with effectual splendour in the floods have made  Earth yield us room enough and amply wide extent, great might invincible, with store of hero sons.

5.44.d: वेत्यग्रुर्जनिवान्वा अति स्पृधः समर्यता मनसा सूर्यः कविः । घ्रंसं रक्षन्तं परि विश्वतो गयमस्माकं शर्म वनवत्स्वावसुः ॥
5.44.e: Sūrya the Sage, as if unwedded, with a Spouse, in battle-loving spirit moveth o’er the foes.  May he, self-excellent, grant us a sheltering home, a house that wards the fierce heat off on every side.

5.44.d: ज्यायांसमस्य यतुनस्य केतुन ऋषिस्वरं चरति यासु नाम ते । यादृश्मिन्धायि तमपस्यया विदद्य उ स्वयं वहते सो अरं करत् ॥
5.44.e: Thy name, sung forth by Ṛṣis in these hymns of ours, goes to the loftier One with this swift mover's light.  By skill he wins the boon whereon his heart is set: he who bestirs himself shall bring the thing to pass.

5.44.d: समुद्रमासामव तस्थे अग्रिमा न रिष्यति सवनं यस्मिन्नायता । अत्रा न हार्दि क्रवणस्य रेजते यत्रा मतिर्विद्यते पूतबन्धनी ॥
5.44.e: The chief and best of these abideth in the sea, nor doth libation fail wherein it is prolonged.  The heart of him who praiseth trembleth not in fear there where the hymn is found connected with the pure.

5.44.d: स हि क्षत्रस्य मनसस्य चित्तिभिरेवावदस्य यजतस्य सध्रेः । अवत्सारस्य स्पृणवाम रण्वभिः शविष्ठं वाजं विदुषा चिदर्ध्यम् ॥
5.44.e: For it is he: with though to of Ksatra, Manasa, of Yajata, and Sadhri, and Evavada,  With Avatsara's sweet songs will we strive to win the mightiest strength which even he who knows should gain.

5.44.d: श्येन आसामदितिः कक्ष्यो३ मदो विश्ववारस्य यजतस्य मायिनः । समन्यमन्यमर्थयन्त्येतवे विदुर्विषाणं परिपानमन्ति ते ॥
5.44.e: The Hawk is their full source, girth-stretching rapturous drink of Visvavara, of Mayin, and Yajata.  They ever seek a fresh draught so that they may come, know when thy time to halt and drink thy fill is near.

5.44.d: सदापृणो यजतो वि द्विषो वधीद्बाहुवृक्तः श्रुतवित्तर्यो वः सचा । उभा स वरा प्रत्येति भाति च यदीं गणं भजते सुप्रयावभिः ॥
5.44.e: Sadaprna the holy, Tarya, Srutavit, and Bahuvrkta, joined with you, have slain the foes.  He gains his wish in both the worlds and brightly shines-when he adores the host with well-advancing steeds.

5.44.d: सुतम्भरो यजमानस्य सत्पतिर्विश्वासामूधः स धियामुदञ्चनः । भरद्धेनू रसवच्छिश्रिये पयोऽनुब्रुवाणो अध्येति न स्वपन् ॥
5.44.e: The worshipper's defender is Sutambhara, producer and uplifter of all holy thoughts.  The milch-cow brought, sweet-flavoured milk was dealt around. Who speaks the bidding text knows this, not he who sleeps.

5.44.d: यो जागार तमृचः कामयन्ते यो जागार तमु सामानि यन्ति । यो जागार तमयं सोम आह तवाहमस्मि सख्ये न्योकाः ॥
5.44.e: The sacred hymns love him who wakes and watches: to him who watches come the Sāma verses.  This Soma saith unto the man who watches, I rest and have my dwelling in thy friendship.

5.44.d: अग्निर्जागार तमृचः कामयन्तेऽग्निर्जागार तमु सामानि यन्ति । अग्निर्जागार तमयं सोम आह तवाहमस्मि सख्ये न्योकाः ॥
5.44.e: Agni is watchful, and the gcas love him; Agni is watchful, Sāma verses seek him.  Agni is watchful, to him saith this Soma, I rest and have my dwelling in thy friendship.

5.45.d: विदा दिवो विष्यन्नद्रिमुक्थैरायत्या उषसो अर्चिनो गुः । अपावृत व्रजिनीरुत्स्वर्गाद्वि दुरो मानुषीर्देव आवः ॥
5.45.e: BARDS of approaching Dawn who know the heavens are come with hymns to throw the mountain open.  The Sun hath risen and oped the stable portals: the doors of men, too, hath the God thrown open.

5.45.d: वि सूर्यो अमतिं न श्रियं सादोर्वाद्गवां माता जानती गात् । धन्वर्णसो नद्य१ः खादोअर्णाः स्थूणेव सुमिता दृंहत द्यौः ॥
5.45.e: Sūrya hath spread his light as splendour: hither came the Cows' Mother, conscious, from the stable,  To streams that flow with biting waves to deserts; and heaven is stablished like a firm-set pillar.

5.45.d: अस्मा उक्थाय पर्वतस्य गर्भो महीनां जनुषे पूर्व्याय । वि पर्वतो जिहीत साधत द्यौराविवासन्तो दसयन्त भूम ॥
5.45.e: This laud hath won the burden of the mountain. To aid the ancient birth of mighty waters  The mountain parted, Heaven performed his office. The worshippers were worn with constant serving.

5.45.d: सूक्तेभिर्वो वचोभिर्देवजुष्टैरिन्द्रा न्व१ग्नी अवसे हुवध्यै । उक्थेभिर्हि ष्मा कवयः सुयज्ञा आविवासन्तो मरुतो यजन्ति ॥
5.45.e: With hymns and God-loved words will I invoke you, Indra and Agni, to obtain your favour,  For verily sages, skilled in sacrificing, worship the Maruts and with lauds invite them.

5.45.d: एतो न्व१द्य सुध्यो३ भवाम प्र दुच्छुना मिनवामा वरीयः । आरे द्वेषांसि सनुतर्दधामायाम प्राञ्चो यजमानमच्छ ॥
5.45.e: This day approach us: may our thoughts be holy, far from us let us cast away misfortune.  Let us keep those who hate us at a distance, and haste to meet the man who sacrifices.

5.45.d: एता धियं कृणवामा सखायोऽप या माताँ ऋणुत व्रजं गोः । यया मनुर्विशिशिप्रं जिगाय यया वणिग्वङ्कुरापा पुरीषम् ॥
5.45.e: Come, let us carry out, O friends, the purpose wherewith the Mother threw the Cow's stall open,  That wherewith Manu conquered Visisipra, wherewith the wandering merchant gained heaven's water.

5.45.d: अनूनोदत्र हस्तयतो अद्रिरार्चन्येन दश मासो नवग्वाः । ऋतं यती सरमा गा अविन्दद्विश्वानि सत्याङ्गिराश्चकार ॥
5.45.e: Here, urged by hands, loudly hath rung the press-stone wherewith Navagvas through ten months sang praises.  Saramā went aright and found the cattle. Aṅgiras gave effect to all their labours.

5.45.d: विश्वे अस्या व्युषि माहिनायाः सं यद्गोभिरङ्गिरसो नवन्त । उत्स आसां परमे सधस्थ ऋतस्य पथा सरमा विदद्गाः ॥
5.45.e: When at the dawning of this mighty Goddess, Aṅgirases all sang forth with the cattle,—  Their spring is in the loftiest place of meeting,—Saramā found the kine by Order's pathway.

5.45.d: आ सूर्यो यातु सप्ताश्वः क्षेत्रं यदस्योर्विया दीर्घयाथे । रघुः श्येनः पतयदन्धो अच्छा युवा कविर्दीदयद्गोषु गच्छन् ॥
5.45.e: Borne by his Coursers Seven may Sūrya visit the field that spreadeth wide for his long journey.  Down on the Soma swooped the rapid Falcon. Bright was the young Sage moving mid his cattle.

5.45.d: आ सूर्यो अरुहच्छुक्रमर्णोऽयुक्त यद्धरितो वीतपृष्ठाः । उद्ना न नावमनयन्त धीरा आशृण्वतीरापो अर्वागतिष्ठन् ॥
5.45.e: Sūrya hath mounted to the shining ocean when he hath yoked his fair-backed Tawny Horses.  The wise have drawn him like a ship through water: the floods obedient have descended hither.

5.45.d: धियं वो अप्सु दधिषे स्वर्षां ययातरन्दश मासो नवग्वाः । अया धिया स्याम देवगोपा अया धिया तुतुर्यामात्यंहः ॥
5.45.e: I lay upon the Floods your hymn, lightwinning, wherewith Navagvas their ten months completed.  Through this our hymn may we have Gods to guard us: through this our hymn pass safe beyond affliction.

5.46.d: हयो न विद्वाँ अयुजि स्वयं धुरि तां वहामि प्रतरणीमवस्युवम् । नास्या वश्मि विमुचं नावृतं पुनर्विद्वान्पथः पुरएत ऋजु नेषति ॥
5.46.e: WELL knowing I have bound me, horselike, to the pole: I carry that which bears as on and gives us help.  I seek for no release, no turning back therefrom. May he who knows the way, the Leader, guide me straight.

5.46.d: अग्न इन्द्र वरुण मित्र देवाः शर्धः प्र यन्त मारुतोत विष्णो । उभा नासत्या रुद्रो अध ग्नाः पूषा भगः सरस्वती जुषन्त ॥
5.46.e: O Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, and Mitra, give, O ye Gods, and Marut host, and Viṣṇu.  May both Nāsatyas, Rudra, heavenly Matrons, Pūṣan, Sarasvatī, Bhaga, accept us.

5.46.d: इन्द्राग्नी मित्रावरुणादितिं स्वः पृथिवीं द्यां मरुतः पर्वताँ अपः । हुवे विष्णुं पूषणं ब्रह्मणस्पतिं भगं नु शंसं सवितारमूतये ॥
5.46.e: Indra and Agni, Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the Waters, Mountains, Maruts, Sky, and Earth and Heaven,  Viṣṇu I call, Pūṣan, and Brahmaṇaspati, and Bhaga, Samsa, Savitar that they may help.

5.46.d: उत नो विष्णुरुत वातो अस्रिधो द्रविणोदा उत सोमो मयस्करत् । उत ऋभव उत राये नो अश्विनोत त्वष्टोत विभ्वानु मंसते ॥
5.46.e: May Viṣṇu also and Vāta who injures none, and Soma granter of possessions give us joy;  And may the Ṛbhus and the Aśvins, Tvaṣṭar and Vibhvan remember us so that we may have wealth.

5.46.d: उत त्यन्नो मारुतं शर्ध आ गमद्दिविक्षयं यजतं बर्हिरासदे । बृहस्पतिः शर्म पूषोत नो यमद्वरूथ्यं१ वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा ॥
5.46.e: So may the band of Maruts dwelling in the sky, the holy, come to us to sit on sacred grass;  Bṛhaspati and Pūṣan grant us sure defence, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman guard and shelter us.

5.46.d: उत त्ये नः पर्वतासः सुशस्तयः सुदीतयो नद्य१स्त्रामणे भुवन् । भगो विभक्ता शवसावसा गमदुरुव्यचा अदितिः श्रोतु मे हवम् ॥
5.46.e: And may the Mountains famed in noble eulogies, and the fair-gleaming Rivers keep us safe from harm.  May Bhaga the Dispenser come with power and grace, and far-pervading Aditi listen to my call.

5.46.d: देवानां पत्नीरुशतीरवन्तु नः प्रावन्तु नस्तुजये वाजसातये । याः पार्थिवासो या अपामपि व्रते ता नो देवीः सुहवाः शर्म यच्छत ॥
5.46.e: May the Gods’ Spouses aid us of their own freewill, aid us to offspring and the winning of the spoil.  Grant us protection, O ye gracious Goddesses, ye who are on the earth or in the waters' realm.

5.46.d: उत ग्ना व्यन्तु देवपत्नीरिन्द्राण्य१ग्नाय्यश्विनी राट् । आ रोदसी वरुणानी शृणोतु व्यन्तु देवीर्य ऋतुर्जनीनाम् ॥
5.46.e: May the Dames, wives of Gods, enjoy our presents, Rat, Aśvini, Agnāyī, and Indrāṇī.  May Rodasī and Varuṇānī hear us, and Goddesses come at the Matrons' season.

5.47.d: प्रयुञ्जती दिव एति ब्रुवाणा मही माता दुहितुर्बोधयन्ती । आविवासन्ती युवतिर्मनीषा पितृभ्य आ सदने जोहुवाना ॥
5.47.e: URGING to toil and making proclamation, seeking Heaven's Daughter comes the Mighty Mother:  She comes, the youthful Hymn, unto the Fathers, inviting to her home and loudly calling.

5.47.d: अजिरासस्तदप ईयमाना आतस्थिवांसो अमृतस्य नाभिम् । अनन्तास उरवो विश्वतः सीं परि द्यावापृथिवी यन्ति पन्थाः ॥
5.47.e: Swift in their motion, hasting to their duty, reaching the central point of life immortal,  On every side about the earth and heaven go forth the spacious paths without a limit.

5.47.d: उक्षा समुद्रो अरुषः सुपर्णः पूर्वस्य योनिं पितुरा विवेश । मध्ये दिवो निहितः पृश्निरश्मा वि चक्रमे रजसस्पात्यन्तौ ॥
5.47.e: Steer, Sea, Red Bird with strong wings, he hath entered the dwelling-place of the Primeval Father.  A gay-hued Stone set in the midst of heaven, he hath gone forth and guards mid-air's two limits.

5.47.d: चत्वार ईं बिभ्रति क्षेमयन्तो दश गर्भं चरसे धापयन्ते । त्रिधातवः परमा अस्य गावो दिवश्चरन्ति परि सद्यो अन्तान् ॥
5.47.e: Four bear him up and give him rest and quiet, and ten invigorate the Babe for travel.  His kine most excellent, of threefold nature, pass swiftly round the boundaries of heaven.

5.47.d: इदं वपुर्निवचनं जनासश्चरन्ति यन्नद्यस्तस्थुरापः । द्वे यदीं बिभृतो मातुरन्ये इहेह जाते यम्या३ सबन्धू ॥
5.47.e: Wondrous, O people, is the mystic knowledge that while the waters stand the streams are flowing:  That, separate from his Mother, Two support him, closely-united, twins, here made apparent.

5.47.d: वि तन्वते धियो अस्मा अपांसि वस्त्रा पुत्राय मातरो वयन्ति । उपप्रक्षे वृषणो मोदमाना दिवस्पथा वध्वो यन्त्यच्छ ॥
5.47.e: For him they lenghten prayers and acts of worship: the Mothers weave garments for him their offspring.  Rejoicing, for the Steer's impregning contact, his Spouses move on paths or heaven to meet him.

5.47.d: तदस्तु मित्रावरुणा तदग्ने शं योरस्मभ्यमिदमस्तु शस्तम् । अशीमहि गाधमुत प्रतिष्ठां नमो दिवे बृहते सादनाय ॥
5.47.e: Be this our praise, O Varuṇa and Mitra may this be health and force to us, O Agni.  May we obtain firm ground and room for resting: Glory to Heaven, the lofty habitation!

5.48.d: कदु प्रियाय धाम्ने मनामहे स्वक्षत्राय स्वयशसे महे वयम् । आमेन्यस्य रजसो यदभ्र आँ अपो वृणाना वितनोति मायिनी ॥
5.48.e: WHAT may we meditate for the beloved Power, mighty in native strength and glorious in itself,  Which as a magic energy seeking waters spreads even to theimmeasurable middle region's cloud?

5.48.d: ता अत्नत वयुनं वीरवक्षणं समान्या वृतया विश्वमा रजः । अपो अपाचीरपरा अपेजते प्र पूर्वाभिस्तिरते देवयुर्जनः ॥
5.48.e: O'er all the region with their uniform advance these have spread out the lore that giveth heroes strength.  Back, with their course reversed, the others pass away: the pious lengthens life with those that are before.

5.48.d: आ ग्रावभिरहन्येभिरक्तुभिर्वरिष्ठं वज्रमा जिघर्ति मायिनि । शतं वा यस्य प्रचरन्त्स्वे दमे संवर्तयन्तो वि च वर्तयन्नहा ॥
5.48.e: With pressing-stones and with the bright beams of the day he hurls his broadest bolt against the Guileful One.  Even he whose hundred wander in his own abode, driving the days afar and bringing them again.

5.48.d: तामस्य रीतिं परशोरिव प्रत्यनीकमख्यं भुजे अस्य वर्पसः । सचा यदि पितुमन्तमिव क्षयं रत्नं दधाति भरहूतये विशे ॥
5.48.e: I, to enjoy the beauty of his form, behold that rapid rush of his as ’twere an axe's edge,  What time he gives the man who calls on him in fight wealth like a dwelling-house filled full with store of food.

5.48.d: स जिह्वया चतुरनीक ऋञ्जते चारु वसानो वरुणो यतन्नरिम् । न तस्य विद्म पुरुषत्वता वयं यतो भगः सविता दाति वार्यम् ॥
5.48.e: Four-faced and nobly clad, Varuṇa, urging on the pious to his task, stirs himself with the tongue.  Naught by our human nature do we know of him, him from whom Bhaga Savitar bestows the boon.

5.49.d: देवं वो अद्य सवितारमेषे भगं च रत्नं विभजन्तमायोः । आ वां नरा पुरुभुजा ववृत्यां दिवेदिवे चिदश्विना सखीयन् ॥
5.49.e: THIS day I bring God Savitar to meet you, and Bhaga who allots the wealth of mortals.  You, Aśvins, Heroes rich in treasures, daily seeking your friendship fain would I turn hither.

5.49.d: प्रति प्रयाणमसुरस्य विद्वान्त्सूक्तैर्देवं सवितारं दुवस्य । उप ब्रुवीत नमसा विजानञ्ज्येष्ठं च रत्नं विभजन्तमायोः ॥
5.49.e: Knowing full well the Asura's time of coming, worship God Savitar with hymns and praises.  Let him who rightly knoweth speak with homage to him who dealeth out man's noblest treasure.

5.49.d: अदत्रया दयते वार्याणि पूषा भगो अदितिर्वस्त उस्रः । इन्द्रो विष्णुर्वरुणो मित्रो अग्निरहानि भद्रा जनयन्त दस्माः ॥
5.49.e: Not for reward doth Pūṣan send his blessings, Bhaga, or Aditi: his garb is splendour.  May Indra, Visniu, Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni produce auspicious days, the Wonder-Workers.

5.49.d: तन्नो अनर्वा सविता वरूथं तत्सिन्धव इषयन्तो अनु ग्मन् । उप यद्वोचे अध्वरस्य होता रायः स्याम पतयो वाजरत्नाः ॥
5.49.e: Sending the shelter which we ask, the foeless Savitar and the Rivers shall approach us.  When I, the sacrifice's priest, invite them, may we he lords of wealth and rich possessions.

5.49.d: प्र ये वसुभ्य ईवदा नमो दुर्ये मित्रे वरुणे सूक्तवाचः । अवैत्वभ्वं कृणुता वरीयो दिवस्पृथिव्योरवसा मदेम ॥
5.49.e: They who devote such worship to the Vasus, singing their hymns to Varuṇa and Mitra,  Vouchsafe them ample room, far off be danger. Through grace of Heaven and Earth may we be happy.

5.50.d: विश्वो देवस्य नेतुर्मर्तो वुरीत सख्यम् । विश्वो राय इषुध्यति द्युम्नं वृणीत पुष्यसे ॥
5.50.e: LET every mortal man elect the friendship of the guiding God.  Each one solicits him for wealth and seeks renown to prosper him.

5.50.d: ते ते देव नेतर्ये चेमाँ अनुशसे । ते राया ते ह्या३पृचे सचेमहि सचथ्यैः ॥
5.50.e: These, leading God, are thine, and these here ready to speak after us.  As such may we attain to wealth and wait with services on thee.

5.50.d: अतो न आ नॄनतिथीनतः पत्नीर्दशस्यत । आरे विश्वं पथेष्ठां द्विषो युयोतु यूयुविः ॥
5.50.e: So further honour as our guests the Hero Gods and then the Dames.  May he remove and keep afar our foes and all who block our path.

5.50.d: यत्र वह्निरभिहितो दुद्रवद्द्रोण्यः पशुः । नृमणा वीरपस्त्योऽर्णा धीरेव सनिता ॥
5.50.e: Where fire is set, and swiftly runs the victim dwelling in the trough,  He wins, with heroes in his home, friendly to man, like constant streams.

5.50.d: एष ते देव नेता रथस्पतिः शं रयिः । शं राये शं स्वस्तय इषःस्तुतो मनामहे देवस्तुतो मनामहे ॥
5.50.e: May these thy riches, Leader God! that rule the car, be blest to us,  Yea, blest to us for wealth and weal. This will we ponder praising strength, this ponder as we praise the God.

5.51.d: अग्ने सुतस्य पीतये विश्वैरूमेभिरा गहि । देवेभिर्हव्यदातये ॥
5.51.e: WITH all assistants, Agni, come hither to drink the Soma-juice;  With Gods unto our sacred gifts.

5.51.d: ऋतधीतय आ गत सत्यधर्माणो अध्वरम् । अग्नेः पिबत जिह्वया ॥
5.51.e: Come to the sacrifice, O ye whose ways are right, whose laws are true,  And drink the draught with Agni's tongue.

5.51.d: विप्रेभिर्विप्र सन्त्य प्रातर्यावभिरा गहि । देवेभिः सोमपीतये ॥
5.51.e: O Singer, with the singers, O Gracious, with those who move at dawn,  Come to the Soma-draught with Gods.

5.51.d: अयं सोमश्चमू सुतोऽमत्रे परि षिच्यते । प्रिय इन्द्राय वायवे ॥
5.51.e: To Indra and to Vāyu dear, this Soma, by the mortar pressed,  Is now poured forth to fill the jar.

5.51.d: वायवा याहि वीतये जुषाणो हव्यदातये । पिबा सुतस्यान्धसो अभि प्रयः ॥
5.51.e: Vāyu, come hither to the feast, wellpleased unto our sacred gifts:  Drink of the Soma juice effused come to the food.

5.51.d: इन्द्रश्च वायवेषां सुतानां पीतिमर्हथः । ताञ्जुषेथामरेपसावभि प्रयः ॥
5.51.e: Ye, Indra, Vāyu, well deserve to drink the juices pressed by us.  Gladly accept them, spotless Pair come to the food.

5.51.d: सुता इन्द्राय वायवे सोमासो दध्याशिरः । निम्नं न यन्ति सिन्धवोऽभि प्रयः ॥
5.51.e: For Indra and for Vāyu pressed are Soma juices blent with curd,  As rivers to the lowland flow: come to the food.

5.51.d: सजूर्विश्वेभिर्देवेभिरश्विभ्यामुषसा सजूः । आ याह्यग्ने अत्रिवत्सुते रण ॥
5.51.e: Associate with all the Gods, come, with the Aśvins and with Dawn,  Agni, as erst with Atri, so enjoy the juice.

5.51.d: सजूर्मित्रावरुणाभ्यां सजूः सोमेन विष्णुना । आ याह्यग्ने अत्रिवत्सुते रण ॥
5.51.e: Associate with Varuṇa, with Mitra, Soma, Viṣṇu, come,  Agni, as erstwith Atri, so enjoy the juice.

5.51.d: सजूरादित्यैर्वसुभिः सजूरिन्द्रेण वायुना । आ याह्यग्ने अत्रिवत्सुते रण ॥
5.51.e: Associate with Vasus, with Ādityas, Indra, Viyu, come, Agni as erst with Atri, so enjoy the juice.

5.51.d: स्वस्ति नो मिमीतामश्विना भगः स्वस्ति देव्यदितिरनर्वणः । स्वस्ति पूषा असुरो दधातु नः स्वस्ति द्यावापृथिवी सुचेतुना ॥
5.51.e: May Bhaga and the Aśvins grant us health and wealth, and Goddess Adid and he whom none resist.  The Asura Pūṣan grant us all prosperity, and Heaven and Earth most wise vouchsafe us happiness.

5.51.d: स्वस्तये वायुमुप ब्रवामहै सोमं स्वस्ति भुवनस्य यस्पतिः । बृहस्पतिं सर्वगणं स्वस्तये स्वस्तय आदित्यासो भवन्तु नः ॥
5.51.e: Let us solicit Vāyu for prosperity, and Soma who is Lord of all the world for weal;  For weal Bṛhaspati with all his company. May the Ādityas bring us health and happiness.

5.51.d: विश्वे देवा नो अद्या स्वस्तये वैश्वानरो वसुरग्निः स्वस्तये । देवा अवन्त्वृभवः स्वस्तये स्वस्ति नो रुद्रः पात्वंहसः ॥
5.51.e: May all the Gods, may Agni the beneficent, God of all men, this day be with us for our weal.  Help us the Ṛbhus, the Divine Ones, for our good. May Rudra bless and keep us from calamity.

5.51.d: स्वस्ति मित्रावरुणा स्वस्ति पथ्ये रेवति । स्वस्ति न इन्द्रश्चाग्निश्च स्वस्ति नो अदिते कृधि ॥
5.51.e: Prosper us, Mitra, Varuṇa. O wealthy Pathya, prosper us.  Indra and Agni, prosper us; prosper us thou, O Aditi.

5.51.d: स्वस्ति पन्थामनु चरेम सूर्याचन्द्रमसाविव । पुनर्ददताघ्नता जानता सं गमेमहि ॥
5.51.e: Like Sun and Moon may we pursue in full prosperity our path,  And meet with one who gives again, -who knows us well and slays us not.

5.52.d: प्र श्यावाश्व धृष्णुयार्चा मरुद्भिर्ऋक्वभिः । ये अद्रोघमनुष्वधं श्रवो मदन्ति यज्ञियाः ॥
5.52.e: SING boldly forth, Śyāvāśva, with the Maruts who are loud in song,  Who, holy, as their wont is, joy in glory that is free from guile.

5.52.d: ते हि स्थिरस्य शवसः सखायः सन्ति धृष्णुया । ते यामन्ना धृषद्विनस्त्मना पान्ति शश्वतः ॥
5.52.e: For in their boldness they are friends of firm and sure heroic strength.  They in their course, bold-spirited, guard all men of their own accord.

5.52.d: ते स्यन्द्रासो नोक्षणोऽति ष्कन्दन्ति शर्वरीः । मरुतामधा महो दिवि क्षमा च मन्महे ॥
5.52.e: Like steers in rapid motion they advance and overtake the nights;  And thus the Maruts’ power in heaven and on the earth we celebrate.

5.52.d: मरुत्सु वो दधीमहि स्तोमं यज्ञं च धृष्णुया । विश्वे ये मानुषा युगा पान्ति मर्त्यं रिषः ॥
5.52.e: With boldness to your Maruts let us offer laud and sacrifice:  Who all, through ages of mankind, guard mortal man from injury.

5.52.d: अर्हन्तो ये सुदानवो नरो असामिशवसः । प्र यज्ञं यज्ञियेभ्यो दिवो अर्चा मरुद्भ्यः ॥
5.52.e: Praiseworthy, givers of good gifts, Heroes with full and perfect strength -  To Maruts, Holy Ones of heaven, will I extol the sacrifice.

5.52.d: आ रुक्मैरा युधा नर ऋष्वा ऋष्टीरसृक्षत । अन्वेनाँ अह विद्युतो मरुतो जज्झतीरिव भानुरर्त त्मना दिवः ॥
5.52.e: The lofty Heroes cast their spears and weapons bright with gleaming gold.  After these Maruts followed close, like laughing lightning from the sky, a splendour of its own accord.

5.52.d: ये वावृधन्त पार्थिवा य उरावन्तरिक्ष आ । वृजने वा नदीनां सधस्थे वा महो दिवः ॥
5.52.e: They who waxed mighty, of the earth, they who are in the wide mid-air,  Or in the rivers’ compass, or in the abode of ample heaven.

5.52.d: शर्धो मारुतमुच्छंस सत्यशवसमृभ्वसम् । उत स्म ते शुभे नरः प्र स्पन्द्रा युजत त्मना ॥
5.52.e: Praise thou the Maruts’ company, the valorous and truly strong,  The Heroes, hasting, by themselves have yoked their deer for victory.

5.52.d: उत स्म ते परुष्ण्यामूर्णा वसत शुन्ध्यवः । उत पव्या रथानामद्रिं भिन्दन्त्योजसा ॥
5.52.e: Fair-gleaming, on Paruṣṇī they have clothed themselves in robes of wool,  And with their chariot tires they cleave the rock asunder in their might.

5.52.d: आपथयो विपथयोऽन्तस्पथा अनुपथाः । एतेभिर्मह्यं नामभिर्यज्ञं विष्टार ओहते ॥
5.52.e: Whether as wanderers from the way or speeders on or to the path,  Under these names the spreading band tend well the sacrifice for me.

5.52.d: अधा नरो न्योहतेऽधा नियुत ओहते । अधा पारावता इति चित्रा रूपाणि दर्श्या ॥
5.52.e: To this the Heroes well attend, well do their teams attend to this.  Visible are their varied forms. Behold, they are Paravatas.

5.52.d: छन्दःस्तुभः कुभन्यव उत्समा कीरिणो नृतुः । ते मे के चिन्न तायव ऊमा आसन्दृशि त्विषे ॥
5.52.e: Hymn-singing, seeking water, they, praising, have danced about the spring.  What are they unto me? No thieves, but helpers, splendid to behold.

5.52.d: य ऋष्वा ऋष्टिविद्युतः कवयः सन्ति वेधसः । तमृषे मारुतं गणं नमस्या रमया गिरा ॥
5.52.e: Sublime, with lightnings for their spears, Sages and Orderers are they.  Ṛṣi, adore that Marut host, and make them happy with thy song.

5.52.d: अच्छ ऋषे मारुतं गणं दाना मित्रं न योषणा । दिवो वा धृष्णव ओजसा स्तुता धीभिरिषण्यत ॥
5.52.e: Ṛṣi, invite the Marut band with offerings, as a maid her friend.  From heaven, too, Bold Ones, in your might haste hither glorified with songs.

5.52.d: नू मन्वान एषां देवाँ अच्छा न वक्षणा । दाना सचेत सूरिभिर्यामश्रुतेभिरञ्जिभिः ॥
5.52.e: Thinking of these now let him come, as with the escort of the Gods,  And with the splendid Princes, famed for rapid courses, to the gifts.

5.52.d: प्र ये मे बन्ध्वेषे गां वोचन्त सूरयः पृश्निं वोचन्त मातरम् । अधा पितरमिष्मिणं रुद्रं वोचन्त शिक्वसः ॥
5.52.e: Princes, who, when I asked their kin, named Pṛśni as their Mother-cow,  And the impetuous Rudra they, the Mighty Ones, declared their Sire.

5.52.d: सप्त मे सप्त शाकिन एकमेका शता ददुः । यमुनायामधि श्रुतमुद्राधो गव्यं मृजे नि राधो अश्व्यं मृजे ॥
5.52.e: The mighty ones, the seven times seven, have singly given me hundred gifts.  I have obtained on Yamuna famed wealth in kine and wealth in steeds.

5.53.d: को वेद जानमेषां को वा पुरा सुम्नेष्वास मरुताम् । यद्युयुज्रे किलास्यः ॥
5.53.e: Who knows the birth of these, or who lived in the Maruts’ favour in the days of old  What time their spotted deer were yoked?

5.53.d: ऐतान्रथेषु तस्थुषः कः शुश्राव कथा ययुः । कस्मै सस्रुः सुदासे अन्वापय इळाभिर्वृष्टयः सह ॥
5.53.e: Who, when they stood upon their cars, hath heard them tell the way they went?  Who was the bounteous man to whom their kindred rains flowed down with food of sacrifice?

5.53.d: ते म आहुर्य आययुरुप द्युभिर्विभिर्मदे । नरो मर्या अरेपस इमान्पश्यन्निति ष्टुहि ॥
5.53.e: To me they told it, and they came with winged steeds radiant to the draught,  Youths, Heroes free from spot or stain: Behold us here and praise thou us;

5.53.d: ये अञ्जिषु ये वाशीषु स्वभानवः स्रक्षु रुक्मेषु खादिषु । श्राया रथेषु धन्वसु ॥
5.53.e: Who shine self-luminous with ornaments and swords, with breastplates, armlets, and with wreaths,  Arrayed on chariots and with bows.

5.53.d: युष्माकं स्मा रथाँ अनु मुदे दधे मरुतो जीरदानवः । वृष्टी द्यावो यतीरिव ॥
5.53.e: O swift to pour your bounties down, ye Maruts, with delight I look upon your cars,  Like splendours coming through the rain.

5.53.d: आ यं नरः सुदानवो ददाशुषे दिवः कोशमचुच्यवुः । वि पर्जन्यं सृजन्ति रोदसी अनु धन्वना यन्ति वृष्टयः ॥
5.53.e: Munificent Heroes, they have cast heaven's treasury down for the worshipper's behoof:  They set the storm-cloud free to stream through both the worlds, and rainfloods flow o’er desert spots.

5.53.d: ततृदानाः सिन्धवः क्षोदसा रजः प्र सस्रुर्धेनवो यथा । स्यन्ना अश्वा इवाध्वनो विमोचने वि यद्वर्तन्त एन्यः ॥
5.53.e: The bursting streams m billowy flood have spread abroad, like milch-kine, o’er the firmament.  Like swift steeds hasting to their journey's resting-place, to every side run glittering brooks.

5.53.d: आ यात मरुतो दिव आन्तरिक्षादमादुत । माव स्थात परावतः ॥
5.53.e: Hither, O Maruts, come from heaven, from mid-air, or from near at hand  Tarry not far away from us.

5.53.d: मा वो रसानितभा कुभा क्रुमुर्मा वः सिन्धुर्नि रीरमत् । मा वः परि ष्ठात्सरयुः पुरीषिण्यस्मे इत्सुम्नमस्तु वः ॥
5.53.e: So let not Rasā, Krumu, or Anitabha, Kubha, or Sindhu hold you back.  Let not the watery Sarayti obstruct your way. With us be all the bliss ye give.

5.53.d: तं वः शर्धं रथानां त्वेषं गणं मारुतं नव्यसीनाम् । अनु प्र यन्ति वृष्टयः ॥
5.53.e: That brilliant gathering of your cars, the company of Maruts, of the Youthful Ones,  The rain-showers, speeding on, attend.

5.53.d: शर्धंशर्धं व एषां व्रातंव्रातं गणंगणं सुशस्तिभिः । अनु क्रामेम धीतिभिः ॥
5.53.e: With eulogies and hymns may we follow your army, troop by troop, and band by band,  And company by company.

5.53.d: कस्मा अद्य सुजाताय रातहव्याय प्र ययुः । एना यामेन मरुतः ॥
5.53.e: To what oblation-giver, sprung of noble ancestry, have sped  The Maruts on this course to-day?

5.53.d: येन तोकाय तनयाय धान्यं१ बीजं वहध्वे अक्षितम् । अस्मभ्यं तद्धत्तन यद्व ईमहे राधो विश्वायु सौभगम् ॥
5.53.e: Vouchsafe to us the bounty, that which we implore, through which, for child and progeny,  Ye give the seed of corn that wasteth not away, and bliss that reacheth to all life.

5.53.d: अतीयाम निदस्तिरः स्वस्तिभिर्हित्वावद्यमरातीः । वृष्ट्वी शं योराप उस्रि भेषजं स्याम मरुतः सह ॥
5.53.e: May we in safety pass by those who slander us, leaving behind disgrace and hate.  Maruts, may we be there when ye, at dawn, in rest and toil, rain waters down and balm.

5.53.d: सुदेवः समहासति सुवीरो नरो मरुतः स मर्त्यः । यं त्रायध्वे स्याम ते ॥
5.53.e: Favoured by Gods shall he the man, O Heroes, Marutr! and possessed of noble sons,  Whom ye protect. Such may we be.

5.53.d: स्तुहि भोजान्त्स्तुवतो अस्य यामनि रणन्गावो न यवसे । यतः पूर्वाँ इव सखीँरनु ह्वय गिरा गृणीहि कामिनः ॥
5.53.e: Praise the Free-givers. At this liberal patron's rite they joy like cattle in the mead.  So call thou unto them who come as ancient Friends: hymn those who love thee with a song.

5.54.d: प्र शर्धाय मारुताय स्वभानव इमां वाचमनजा पर्वतच्युते । घर्मस्तुभे दिव आ पृष्ठयज्वने द्युम्नश्रवसे महि नृम्णमर्चत ॥
5.54.e: THIS hymn will I make for the Marut host who bright in native splendour cast the mountains down.  Sing the great strength of those illustrious in renown, who stay the heat, who sacrifice on heights of heaven.

5.54.d: प्र वो मरुतस्तविषा उदन्यवो वयोवृधो अश्वयुजः परिज्रयः । सं विद्युता दधति वाशति त्रितः स्वरन्त्यापोऽवना परिज्रयः ॥
5.54.e: O Maruts, rich in water, strengtheners of life are your strong bands with harnessed steeds, that wander far.  Trita roars out at him who aims the lightning-flash. The waters sweeping round are thundering on their way.

5.54.d: विद्युन्महसो नरो अश्मदिद्यवो वातत्विषो मरुतः पर्वतच्युतः । अब्दया चिन्मुहुरा ह्रादुनीवृतः स्तनयदमा रभसा उदोजसः ॥
5.54.e: They gleam with lightning, Heroes, Casters of the Stone, wind-rapid Maruts, overthrowers of the bills,  Oft through desire to rain coming with storm of hail, roaring in onset, violent and exceeding strong.

5.54.d: व्य१क्तून्रुद्रा व्यहानि शिक्वसो व्य१न्तरिक्षं वि रजांसि धूतयः । वि यदज्राँ अजथ नाव ईं यथा वि दुर्गाणि मरुतो नाह रिष्यथ ॥
5.54.e: When, mighty Rudras, through the nights and through the days, when through the sky and realms of air, shakers of all,  When over the broad fields ye drive along like ships, e’en to strongholds ye come, Maruts, but are not harmed.

5.54.d: तद्वीर्यं वो मरुतो महित्वनं दीर्घं ततान सूर्यो न योजनम् । एता न यामे अगृभीतशोचिषोऽनश्वदां यन्न्ययातना गिरिम् ॥
5.54.e: Maruts, this hero strength and majesty of yours hath, like the Sun, extended o’er a lengthened way,  When in your course like deer with splendour unsubdued ye bowed the hill that gives imperishable rain.

5.54.d: अभ्राजि शर्धो मरुतो यदर्णसं मोषथा वृक्षं कपनेव वेधसः । अध स्मा नो अरमतिं सजोषसश्चक्षुरिव यन्तमनु नेषथा सुगम् ॥
5.54.e: Bright shone your host, ye Sages, Maruts, when ye smote the waving tree as when the worm consumeth it.  Accordant, as the eye guides him who walks, have ye led our devotion onward by an easy path.

5.54.d: न स जीयते मरुतो न हन्यते न स्रेधति न व्यथते न रिष्यति । नास्य राय उप दस्यन्ति नोतय ऋषिं वा यं राजानं वा सुषूदथ ॥
5.54.e: Never is he, O Maruts, slain or overcome, never doth he decay ne’er is distressed or harmed;  His treasures, his resources, never waste away, whom. whether he be prince or Ṛṣi, ye direct.

5.54.d: नियुत्वन्तो ग्रामजितो यथा नरोऽर्यमणो न मरुतः कबन्धिनः । पिन्वन्त्युत्सं यदिनासो अस्वरन्व्युन्दन्ति पृथिवीं मध्वो अन्धसा ॥
5.54.e: With harnessed team like heroes overcoming troops, the friendly Maruts, laden with their water-casks,  Let the spring flow, and when impetuous' they roar they inundate the earth with floods of pleasant meath.

5.54.d: प्रवत्वतीयं पृथिवी मरुद्भ्यः प्रवत्वती द्यौर्भवति प्रयद्भ्यः । प्रवत्वतीः पथ्या अन्तरिक्ष्याः प्रवत्वन्तः पर्वता जीरदानवः ॥
5.54.e: Free for the Maruts is the earth with sloping ways, free for the rushing Ones is heaven with steep descents.  The paths of air's mid-region are precipitous, precipitous the mountains with their running streams.

5.54.d: यन्मरुतः सभरसः स्वर्णरः सूर्य उदिते मदथा दिवो नरः । न वोऽश्वाः श्रथयन्ताह सिस्रतः सद्यो अस्याध्वनः पारमश्नुथ ॥
5.54.e: When, as the Sun hath risen up, ye take delight, O bounteous radiant Maruts, Heroes of the sky,  Your coursers weary not when speeding onṭheir way, and rapidly ye reach the end of this your path.

5.54.d: अंसेषु व ऋष्टयः पत्सु खादयो वक्षःसु रुक्मा मरुतो रथे शुभः । अग्निभ्राजसो विद्युतो गभस्त्योः शिप्राः शीर्षसु वितता हिरण्ययीः ॥
5.54.e: Lances are on your shoulders, anklets on your feet, gold chains are on your breasts, gems, Maruts, on your car.  Lightnings aglow with flame are flashing in your hands, and visors wroughtof gold are laid upon your heads.

5.54.d: तं नाकमर्यो अगृभीतशोचिषं रुशत्पिप्पलं मरुतो वि धूनुथ । समच्यन्त वृजनातित्विषन्त यत्स्वरन्ति घोषं विततमृतायवः ॥
5.54.e: Maruts, in eager stir ye shake the vault of heaven, splendid beyond conception, for its shining fruit.  They gathered when they let their deeds of might flash forth. The Pious Ones send forth a far-resounding shout.

5.54.d: युष्मादत्तस्य मरुतो विचेतसो रायः स्याम रथ्यो३ वयस्वतः । न यो युच्छति तिष्यो३ यथा दिवो३ऽस्मे रारन्त मरुतः सहस्रिणम् ॥
5.54.e: Sage Maruts, may we be the drivers of the car of riches ful I of life that have been given by you.  O Maruts, let that wealth in thousands dwell with us which never vanishes like Tisya from the sky.

5.54.d: यूयं रयिं मरुतः स्पार्हवीरं यूयमृषिमवथ सामविप्रम् । यूयमर्वन्तं भरताय वाजं यूयं धत्थ राजानं श्रुष्टिमन्तम् ॥
5.54.e: Maruts, ye further wealth with longedfor heroes, further the Ṛṣi skilled in chanted verses.  Ye give the Bhārata as his strength, a charger, and ye bestow a king who quickly listens.

5.54.d: तद्वो यामि द्रविणं सद्यऊतयो येना स्व१र्ण ततनाम नॄँरभि । इदं सु मे मरुतो हर्यता वचो यस्य तरेम तरसा शतं हिमाः ॥
5.54.e: Of you, most swift to succour! I solicit wealth wherewith we may spread forth mid men like as the Sun.  Accept, O Maruts, graciously this hymn of mine that we may live a hundred winters through its power.

5.55.d: प्रयज्यवो मरुतो भ्राजदृष्टयो बृहद्वयो दधिरे रुक्मवक्षसः । ईयन्ते अश्वैः सुयमेभिराशुभिः शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
5.55.e: WITH gleaming lances, with their breasts adorned with gold, the Maruts, rushing onward, hold high power of life.  They hasten with swift steeds easy to be controlled. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: स्वयं दधिध्वे तविषीं यथा विद बृहन्महान्त उर्विया वि राजथ । उतान्तरिक्षं ममिरे व्योजसा शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
5.55.e: Ye, as ye wist, have gained of your own selves your power: high, O ye Mighty Ones, and wide ye shine abroad.  They with their strength have even measured out the sky.  Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: साकं जाताः सुभ्वः साकमुक्षिताः श्रिये चिदा प्रतरं वावृधुर्नरः । विरोकिणः सूर्यस्येव रश्मयः शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
5.55.e: Strong, born together, they together have waxed great: the Heroes more and more have grown to majesty  Resplendent as the Sun's beams in their light are they. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: आभूषेण्यं वो मरुतो महित्वनं दिदृक्षेण्यं सूर्यस्येव चक्षणम् । उतो अस्माँ अमृतत्वे दधातन शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
5.55.e: Maruts, your mightiness deserves to be adored, sight to be longed for like the shining of the Sun.  So lead us with your aid to immortality.  Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: उदीरयथा मरुतः समुद्रतो यूयं वृष्टिं वर्षयथा पुरीषिणः । न वो दस्रा उप दस्यन्ति धेनवः शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
5.55.e: O Maruts, from the Ocean ye uplift the rain, and fraught with vaporous moisture pour the torrents down.  Never, ye Wonder-Workers, are your Milch-kine dry. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: यदश्वान्धूर्षु पृषतीरयुग्ध्वं हिरण्ययान्प्रत्यत्काँ अमुग्ध्वम् । विश्वा इत्स्पृधो मरुतो व्यस्यथ शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
5.55.e: When to your car-poles ye have yoked your spotted deer to be your steeds, and put your golden mantles on,  O Maruts, ye disperse all enemies abroad. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: न पर्वता न नद्यो वरन्त वो यत्राचिध्वं मरुतो गच्छथेदु तत् । उत द्यावापृथिवी याथना परि शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
5.55.e: Neither the mountains nor the rivers keep you back: whither ye have resolved thither ye, Maruts, go.  Ye compass round about even the heaven and earth. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.  Whate’er is ancient, Maruts, what of recent time, whate’er is spoken, Vasus, what is chanted forth,  They who take cognizance of all of this are ye. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: यत्पूर्व्यं मरुतो यच्च नूतनं यदुद्यते वसवो यच्च शस्यते । विश्वस्य तस्य भवथा नवेदसः शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
5.55.e: Whate'er is ancient, Maruts, what of recent time, whate'er is spoken, Vasus, what is chanted forth, They who take cognizance of all of this are ye. Their cars moved Onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: मृळत नो मरुतो मा वधिष्टनास्मभ्यं शर्म बहुलं वि यन्तन । अधि स्तोत्रस्य सख्यस्य गातन शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
5.55.e: Be gracious unto us, ye Maruts, slay us not extend ye unto us shelter of many a sort.  Pay due regard unto our friendship and our praise. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: यूयमस्मान्नयत वस्यो अच्छा निरंहतिभ्यो मरुतो गृणानाः । जुषध्वं नो हव्यदातिं यजत्रा वयं स्याम पतयो रयीणाम् ॥
5.55.e: O Maruts, lead us on to higher fortune deliver us, when lauded, from afflictions.  Accept, ye Holy Ones, the gifts we bring you. May we be masters of abundant riches.

5.56.d: अग्ने शर्धन्तमा गणं पिष्टं रुक्मेभिरञ्जिभिः । विशो अद्य मरुतामव ह्वये दिवश्चिद्रोचनादधि ॥
5.56.e: AGNI, that valorous company adorned with ornaments of gold,  The people of the Maruts, I call down to-day even from the luminous realm of heaven.

5.56.d: यथा चिन्मन्यसे हृदा तदिन्मे जग्मुराशसः । ये ते नेदिष्ठं हवनान्यागमन्तान्वर्ध भीमसंदृशः ॥
5.56.e: Even as thou thinkest in thy heart, thither my wishes also tend.  Those who have come most near to thine invoking calls, strengthen them fearful to behold.

5.56.d: मीळ्हुष्मतीव पृथिवी पराहता मदन्त्येत्यस्मदा । ऋक्षो न वो मरुतः शिमीवाँ अमो दुध्रो गौरिव भीमयुः ॥
5.56.e: Earth, like a bounteous lady, liberal of her gifts, struck down and shaken, yet exultant, comes to us.  Impetuous as a bear, O Maruts, is youi rush terrible as a dreadful bull..

5.56.d: नि ये रिणन्त्योजसा वृथा गावो न दुर्धुरः । अश्मानं चित्स्वर्यं१ पर्वतं गिरिं प्र च्यावयन्ति यामभिः ॥
5.56.e: They who with mighty strength o’erthrow like oxen difficult to yoke,  Cause e’en the heavenly stone to shake ' yea, shake the rocky mountain as they race along.

5.56.d: उत्तिष्ठ नूनमेषां स्तोमैः समुक्षितानाम् । मरुतां पुरुतममपूर्व्यं गवां सर्गमिव ह्वये ॥
5.56.e: Rise up! even now with lauds I call the very numerous company,  Unequalled, of these Maruts, like a herd of kine, grown up together in their strength.

5.56.d: युङ्ग्ध्वं ह्यरुषी रथे युङ्ग्ध्वं रथेषु रोहितः । युङ्ग्ध्वं हरी अजिरा धुरि वोळ्हवे वहिष्ठा धुरि वोळ्हवे ॥
5.56.e: Bind to your car the bright red mares, yoke the red coursers to your car.  Bind to the pole, to draw, the fleet-foot tawny steeds, the best at drawing, to the pole.

5.56.d: उत स्य वाज्यरुषस्तुविष्वणिरिह स्म धायि दर्शतः । मा वो यामेषु मरुतश्चिरं करत्प्र तं रथेषु चोदत ॥
5.56.e: Yea, and this loudly-neighing bright red vigorous horse who hath been sutioned, fair to see,  Let him not cause delay, O Maruts,, in your course, urge ye him onward in your cars.

5.56.d: रथं नु मारुतं वयं श्रवस्युमा हुवामहे । आ यस्मिन्तस्थौ सुरणानि बिभ्रती सचा मरुत्सु रोदसी ॥
5.56.e: The Maruts’ chariot, ever fain to gather glory, we invoke,  Which Rodasī hath mounted, bringing pleasant gifts, with Maruts in her company.

5.56.d: तं वः शर्धं रथेशुभं त्वेषं पनस्युमा हुवे । यस्मिन्त्सुजाता सुभगा महीयते सचा मरुत्सु मीळ्हुषी ॥
5.56.e: I call that brilliant band of yours, adorable, rapid on the car  Whereon the bounteous Dame, auspicious, nobly born, shows glorious with the Marut host.

5.57.d: आ रुद्रास इन्द्रवन्तः सजोषसो हिरण्यरथाः सुविताय गन्तन । इयं वो अस्मत्प्रति हर्यते मतिस्तृष्णजे न दिव उत्सा उदन्यवे ॥
5.57.e: OF one accord, with Indra, O ye Rudras, come borne on your golden car for our prosperity.  An offering from us, this hymn is brought to you, as, unto one who th irsts for water, heavenly springs.

5.57.d: वाशीमन्त ऋष्टिमन्तो मनीषिणः सुधन्वान इषुमन्तो निषङ्गिणः । स्वश्वाः स्थ सुरथाः पृश्निमातरः स्वायुधा मरुतो याथना शुभम् ॥
5.57.e: Armed with your daggers, full of wisdom, armed with spears, armed with your quivers, armed with arrows, with good bows,  Good horses and good cars have ye, O Pṛśni's Sons: ye, Maruts, with good weapons go to victory.

5.57.d: धूनुथ द्यां पर्वतान्दाशुषे वसु नि वो वना जिहते यामनो भिया । कोपयथ पृथिवीं पृश्निमातरः शुभे यदुग्राः पृषतीरयुग्ध्वम् ॥
5.57.e: From hills and heaven ye shake wealth for the worshipper: in terror at your coming low the woods bow down.  Ye make the earth to tremble, Sons of Pṛśni, when for victory ye have yoked, fierce Ones! your spotted deer.

5.57.d: वातत्विषो मरुतो वर्षनिर्णिजो यमा इव सुसदृशः सुपेशसः । पिशङ्गाश्वा अरुणाश्वा अरेपसः प्रत्वक्षसो महिना द्यौरिवोरवः ॥
5.57.e: Bright with the blasts of wind, wrapped in their robes of rain, like twins of noble aspect and of lovely form,  The Maruts, spotless, with steeds tawnyhued and red, strong in their mightiness and spreading wide like heaven.

5.57.d: पुरुद्रप्सा अञ्जिमन्तः सुदानवस्त्वेषसंदृशो अनवभ्रराधसः । सुजातासो जनुषा रुक्मवक्षसो दिवो अर्का अमृतं नाम भेजिरे ॥
5.57.e: Rich in adornment, rich in drops, munificent, bright in their aspect, yielding bounties that endure,  Noble by birth, adorned with gold upon their breasts, the Singers of the sky have won immortal fame.

5.57.d: ऋष्टयो वो मरुतो अंसयोरधि सह ओजो बाह्वोर्वो बलं हितम् । नृम्णा शीर्षस्वायुधा रथेषु वो विश्वा वः श्रीरधि तनूषु पिपिशे ॥
5.57.e: Borne on both shoulders, O ye Maruts, are your spears: within your arms is laid your energy and 3trength.  Bold thoughts are in your heads, your weapons in your cars, all glorious majesty is moulded on your forms.

5.57.d: गोमदश्वावद्रथवत्सुवीरं चन्द्रवद्राधो मरुतो ददा नः । प्रशस्तिं नः कृणुत रुद्रियासो भक्षीय वोऽवसो दैव्यस्य ॥
5.57.e: Vouchsafe to us, O Maruts, splendid bounty in cattle and in steeds, in cars and heroes.  Children of Rudra, give us high distinction: may I enjoy your Godlike help and favour.

5.57.d: हये नरो मरुतो मृळता नस्तुवीमघासो अमृता ऋतज्ञाः । सत्यश्रुतः कवयो युवानो बृहद्गिरयो बृहदुक्षमाणाः ॥
5.57.e: Ho! Maruts, Heroes, skilled in Law, immortal, be gracious unto us, ye rich in treasures,  Ye hearers of the truth, ye sage and youthful, grown mighty, dwelling on the lofty mountains.

5.58.d: तमु नूनं तविषीमन्तमेषां स्तुषे गणं मारुतं नव्यसीनाम् । य आश्वश्वा अमवद्वहन्त उतेशिरे अमृतस्य स्वराजः ॥
5.58.e: Now do I glorify their mighty cohort, the company of these the youthful Maruts,  Who ride impetuous on with rapid horses, and radiant in themselves, are Lords of Amṛta.

5.58.d: त्वेषं गणं तवसं खादिहस्तं धुनिव्रतं मायिनं दातिवारम् । मयोभुवो ये अमिता महित्वा वन्दस्व विप्र तुविराधसो नॄन् ॥
5.58.e: The mighty glittering band, arm-bound with bracelets, givers of bliss, unmeasured in their greatness,  With magical powers, bountiful, ever-roaring,—these, liberal Heroes, venerate thou singer.

5.58.d: आ वो यन्तूदवाहासो अद्य वृष्टिं ये विश्वे मरुतो जुनन्ति । अयं यो अग्निर्मरुतः समिद्ध एतं जुषध्वं कवयो युवानः ॥
5.58.e: This day may all your water-bringers, Maruts, they who impel the falling rain, approach us.  This fire, O Maruts, hath been duly kindled; let it find favour with you, youthful Sages.

5.58.d: यूयं राजानमिर्यं जनाय विभ्वतष्टं जनयथा यजत्राः । युष्मदेति मुष्टिहा बाहुजूतो युष्मत्सदश्वो मरुतः सुवीरः ॥
5.58.e: Ye raise up for the folk an active ruler whom, Holy Ones! a Master's hand hath fashioned.  Ye send the fighter hand to hand, armmighty, and the brave hero, Maruts with good horses.

5.58.d: अरा इवेदचरमा अहेव प्रप्र जायन्ते अकवा महोभिः । पृश्नेः पुत्रा उपमासो रभिष्ठाः स्वया मत्या मरुतः सं मिमिक्षुः ॥
5.58.e: They spring forth more and more, strong in their glories, like days, like spokes where none are last in order.  Highest and mightiest are the Sons of Pṛśni. Firm to their own intention cling the Maruts.

5.58.d: यत्प्रायासिष्ट पृषतीभिरश्वैर्वीळुपविभिर्मरुतो रथेभिः । क्षोदन्त आपो रिणते वनान्यवोस्रियो वृषभः क्रन्दतु द्यौः ॥
5.58.e: When ye have hastened on with spotted coursers, O Maruts, on your cars with strong-wrought fellies,  The waters are disturbed, the woods are shattered. Let Dyaus the Red Steer send his thunder downward.

5.58.d: प्रथिष्ट यामन्पृथिवी चिदेषां भर्तेव गर्भं स्वमिच्छवो धुः । वातान्ह्यश्वान्धुर्यायुयुज्रे वर्षं स्वेदं चक्रिरे रुद्रियासः ॥
5.58.e: Even Earth hath spread herself wide at their coming, and they as husbands have with power impregned her.  They to the pole have yoked the winds for coursers: their sweat have they made rain, these Sons of Rudra.

5.58.d: हये नरो मरुतो मृळता नस्तुवीमघासो अमृता ऋतज्ञाः । सत्यश्रुतः कवयो युवानो बृहद्गिरयो बृहदुक्षमाणाः ॥
5.58.e: Ho! Maruts, Heroes, skilled in Law, immortal, be gracious unto us, ye rich in treasures,  Ye hearers of the truth, ye sage and youthful, grown mighty, dwelling on the lofty mountains.

5.59.d: प्र वः स्पळक्रन्त्सुविताय दावनेऽर्चा दिवे प्र पृथिव्या ऋतं भरे । उक्षन्ते अश्वान्तरुषन्त आ रजोऽनु स्वं भानुं श्रथयन्ते अर्णवैः ॥
5.59.e: YOUR spy hath called to you to give prosperity. I sing to Heaven and Earth and offer sacrifice.  They bathe their steeds and hasten through the firmament: they spread abroad their radiance through the sea of cloud.

5.59.d: अमादेषां भियसा भूमिरेजति नौर्न पूर्णा क्षरति व्यथिर्यती । दूरेदृशो ये चितयन्त एमभिरन्तर्महे विदथे येतिरे नरः ॥
5.59.e: Earth shakes and reels in terror at their onward rush, like a full ship which, quivering, lets the water in.  Marked on their ways are they, visible from afar: the Heroes press between in mighty armament.

5.59.d: गवामिव श्रियसे शृङ्गमुत्तमं सूर्यो न चक्षू रजसो विसर्जने । अत्या इव सुभ्व१श्चारवः स्थन मर्या इव श्रियसे चेतथा नरः ॥
5.59.e: As the exalted horn of bulls for splendid might, as the Sun's eye set in the firmament's expanse,  Like vigorous horses ye are beauteous to behold, and for your glory show like bridegrooms, O ye Men.

5.59.d: को वो महान्ति महतामुदश्नवत्कस्काव्या मरुतः को ह पौंस्या । यूयं ह भूमिं किरणं न रेजथ प्र यद्भरध्वे सुविताय दावने ॥
5.59.e: Who, O ye Maruts, may attain the mighty lore of you the mighty, who may reach your manly deeds?  Ye, verily, make earth tremble like a ray of light what time ye bring your boons to give prosperity,

5.59.d: अश्वा इवेदरुषासः सबन्धवः शूरा इव प्रयुधः प्रोत युयुधुः । मर्या इव सुवृधो वावृधुर्नरः सूर्यस्य चक्षुः प्र मिनन्ति वृष्टिभिः ॥
5.59.e: Like steeds of ruddy colour, scions of one race, as foremost champions they have battled in the van.  The Heroes have waxed strong like we.1grown manly youths; with floods of rain they make the Sun's eye fade away,

5.59.d: ते अज्येष्ठा अकनिष्ठास उद्भिदोऽमध्यमासो महसा वि वावृधुः । सुजातासो जनुषा पृश्निमातरो दिवो मर्या आ नो अच्छा जिगातन ॥
5.59.e: Having no eldest and no youngest in their band, no middlomost, preeminent they have waxed in might,  These Sons of Pṛśni, sprung of noble ancestry: come hitberward to us, ye bridegrooms of the sky.

5.59.d: वयो न ये श्रेणीः पप्तुरोजसान्तान्दिवो बृहतः सानुनस्परि । अश्वास एषामुभये यथा विदुः प्र पर्वतस्य नभनूँरचुच्यवुः ॥
5.59.e: Like birds of air they flew with might in lengthened lines from heaven's high ridges to the borders of the sky.  The steeds who carry them, as Gods and mortals know, have caused the waters of the mounuains to desGend.

5.59.d: मिमातु द्यौरदितिर्वीतये नः सं दानुचित्रा उषसो यतन्ताम् । आचुच्यवुर्दिव्यं कोशमेत ऋषे रुद्रस्य मरुतो गृणानाः ॥
5.59.e: May Dyaus, the Infinite, roar for our banquet: may Dawns toil for us, glittering with moisture.  Lauded by thee, these Maruts, Sons o Rudra, O Ṛṣi, have sent down the heavenly treasure.

5.60.d: ईळे अग्निं स्ववसं नमोभिरिह प्रसत्तो वि चयत्कृतं नः । रथैरिव प्र भरे वाजयद्भिः प्रदक्षिणिन्मरुतां स्तोममृध्याम् ॥
5.60.e: I LAUD with reverence the gracious Agni: here may he sit and part our meed among us.  As with spoil-seeking cars I bring oblation: turned rightward I will swell the Marut's, praise-song.

5.60.d: आ ये तस्थुः पृषतीषु श्रुतासु सुखेषु रुद्रा मरुतो रथेषु । वना चिदुग्रा जिहते नि वो भिया पृथिवी चिद्रेजते पर्वतश्चित् ॥
5.60.e: The Maruts, yea, the Rudras, who have mounted their famous spotted deer and cars swift-moving,—  Before you, fierce Ones! woods bow down in terror: Earth, even the mountain, trembles at your coming.

5.60.d: पर्वतश्चिन्महि वृद्धो बिभाय दिवश्चित्सानु रेजत स्वने वः । यत्क्रीळथ मरुत ऋष्टिमन्त आप इव सध्र्यञ्चो धवध्वे ॥
5.60.e: Though vast and tall, the mountain is affrighted, the height of heaven is shaken at your roaring  When, armed with lances, ye are sporting, Maruts, and rush along together like the waters.

5.60.d: वरा इवेद्रैवतासो हिरण्यैरभि स्वधाभिस्तन्वः पिपिश्रे । श्रिये श्रेयांसस्तवसो रथेषु सत्रा महांसि चक्रिरे तनूषु ॥
5.60.e: They, like young suitors, sons of wealthy houses, have with their golden natures decked their bodies.  Strong on their cars, the lordly Ones, for glory, have set their splendours on their forms for ever.

5.60.d: अज्येष्ठासो अकनिष्ठास एते सं भ्रातरो वावृधुः सौभगाय । युवा पिता स्वपा रुद्र एषां सुदुघा पृश्निः सुदिना मरुद्भ्यः ॥
5.60.e: None being eldest, none among them youngest, as brothers they have grown to happy fortune.  May their Sire Rudra, young and deft, and Pṛśni pouring much milk, bring fair days to the Maruts.

5.60.d: यदुत्तमे मरुतो मध्यमे वा यद्वावमे सुभगासो दिवि ष्ठ । अतो नो रुद्रा उत वा न्व१स्याग्ने वित्ताद्धविषो यद्यजाम ॥
5.60.e: Whether, O blessed Maruts, ye be dwelling in highest, midmost, or in lowest heaven,  Thence, O ye Rudras, and thou also, Agni, notice the sacrificial food we offer.

5.60.d: अग्निश्च यन्मरुतो विश्ववेदसो दिवो वहध्व उत्तरादधि ष्णुभिः । ते मन्दसाना धुनयो रिशादसो वामं धत्त यजमानाय सुन्वते ॥
5.60.e: O Maruts, Lords of all, when Agni and when ye drive downward from sublimest heaven along the heights,  Shakers of all, rejoicing, slayers of the foe, give riches to the Soma-pressing worshipper.

5.60.d: अग्ने मरुद्भिः शुभयद्भिर्ऋक्वभिः सोमं पिब मन्दसानो गणश्रिभिः । पावकेभिर्विश्वमिन्वेभिरायुभिर्वैश्वानर प्रदिवा केतुना सजूः ॥
5.60.e: O Agni, with the Maruts as they gleam and sing, gathered in troop, rejoicing drink the Soma juice;  With these the living ones who cleanse and further all, joined with thy banner, O Vaiśvānara, from of old.

5.61.d: के ष्ठा नरः श्रेष्ठतमा य एकएक आयय । परमस्याः परावतः ॥
5.61.e: O HEROES lordliest of all, who are ye that have singly come  Forth from a region most remote?

5.61.d: क्व१ वोऽश्वाः क्वा३भीशवः कथं शेक कथा यय । पृष्ठे सदो नसोर्यमः ॥
5.61.e: Where are your horses, where the reins? How came ye? how had ye the power?  Rein was on nose and seat on back.

5.61.d: जघने चोद एषां वि सक्थानि नरो यमुः । पुत्रकृथे न जनयः ॥
5.61.e: The whip is laid upon the flank. The heroes stretch their thighs apart,  Like women when the babe is born.

5.61.d: परा वीरास एतन मर्यासो भद्रजानयः । अग्नितपो यथासथ ॥
5.61.e: Go ye, O Heroes, far away, ye bridegrooms with a lovely Spouse  That ye may warm you at the fire.

5.61.d: सनत्साश्व्यं पशुमुत गव्यं शतावयम् । श्यावाश्वस्तुताय या दोर्वीरायोपबर्बृहत् ॥
5.61.e: May she gain cattle for her meed, hundreds of sheep and steeds and kine,  Who threw embracing arms around the hero whom gyavaiva praised.

5.61.d: उत त्वा स्त्री शशीयसी पुंसो भवति वस्यसी । अदेवत्रादराधसः ॥
5.61.e: Yea, many a woman is more firm and better than the man who turns  Away from Gods, andoffers not.

5.61.d: वि या जानाति जसुरिं वि तृष्यन्तं वि कामिनम् । देवत्रा कृणुते मनः ॥
5.61.e: She who discerns the weak and worn, the man who thirsts and is in want  She sets her mind upon the Gods.

5.61.d: उत घा नेमो अस्तुतः पुमाँ इति ब्रुवे पणिः । स वैरदेय इत्समः ॥
5.61.e: And yet full many a one, unpraised, mean niggard, is entitled man:  Only in weregild is he such.

5.61.d: उत मेऽरपद्युवतिर्ममन्दुषी प्रति श्यावाय वर्तनिम् । वि रोहिता पुरुमीळ्हाय येमतुर्विप्राय दीर्घयशसे ॥
5.61.e: And she, the young, the joyous-spirited, divulged the path to Śyāva, yea, to me.  Two red steeds carried me to Purumīlha's side, that sage of far-extended fame,

5.61.d: यो मे धेनूनां शतं वैददश्विर्यथा ददत् । तरन्त इव मंहना ॥
5.61.e: Him who, like Vaidadasvi, like Taranta, hath bestowed on me  A hundred cows in liberal gift.

5.61.d: य ईं वहन्त आशुभिः पिबन्तो मदिरं मधु । अत्र श्रवांसि दधिरे ॥
5.61.e: They who are borne by rapid steeds, drinking the meath that gives delight,  They have attained high glories here.

5.61.d: येषां श्रियाधि रोदसी विभ्राजन्ते रथेष्वा । दिवि रुक्म इवोपरि ॥
5.61.e: They by whose splendour both the worlds are over-spread they shine on cars  As the gold gleams above in heaven.

5.61.d: युवा स मारुतो गणस्त्वेषरथो अनेद्यः । शुभंयावाप्रतिष्कुतः ॥
5.61.e: That Marut band is ever young, borne on bright cars, unblamable,  Moving to victory, checked by none.

5.61.d: को वेद नूनमेषां यत्रा मदन्ति धूतयः । ऋतजाता अरेपसः ॥
5.61.e: Who knoweth, verily, of these where the All-shakers take delight,  Born, spotless, after sacred Law?

5.61.d: यूयं मर्तं विपन्यवः प्रणेतार इत्था धिया । श्रोतारो यामहूतिषु ॥
5.61.e: Guides are ye, lovers of the song to mortal man through holy hymn,  And hearers when he cries for help.

5.61.d: ते नो वसूनि काम्या पुरुश्चन्द्रा रिशादसः । आ यज्ञियासो ववृत्तन ॥
5.61.e: Do ye, destroyers of the foe, worshipful and exceeding bright,  Send down the treasures that we crave.

5.61.d: एतं मे स्तोममूर्म्ये दार्भ्याय परा वह । गिरो देवि रथीरिव ॥
5.61.e: OUrmya, bear thou far away to Darbhya this my hymn of praise,  Songs, Goddess, as if chariot-borne.

5.61.d: उत मे वोचतादिति सुतसोमे रथवीतौ । न कामो अप वेति मे ॥
5.61.e: From me to Rathaviti say, when he hath pressed the Soma juice,  The wish I had departeth not.
This wealthy Rathaviti dwells among the people rich in kine,  Among the mountains, far withdrawn.
